# Working notes for The Hallowmarch

Read this before changing anything. It covers what the game is, the owner's standing requirements, how the code fits together, how to test it, and what is planned. A summary of this handoff (the status, the owner's requirements, how to build, the roadmap's latest rows and the history, with the commit whose CLAUDE.md holds the rest: `tools/handoff/make_handoff.py ... summary`) is also kept in the owner's Interego pod as the graph `urn:graph:project:hallowmarch`, updated at each milestone.

- **Owner:** Mark (GitHub `markjspivey-xwisee`)
- **Living world (owner reaffirmed 2026-10-27):** Everyone begins at level 1 and develops at their own pace, becoming better at the activities they practise. Enemies must gain their own experience and develop too. Shared world development opens new possibilities and content; it must not automatically raise individual levels. Everything in the world should be alive and functional, have a purpose, be useful, and evolve through experience. Apply this to inhabitants, combat, work, economies and world systems; do not substitute hidden player-specific damage adjustments for actual development. Preserve earned character and world history when changing progression.
- **Repository:** https://github.com/markjspivey-xwisee/hallowmarch. Several sessions work on it at once: work on a branch and fast-forward it into `main` (see Working alongside other sessions), commit often, and push at each milestone.

## The owner's standing requirements

These apply to every change, not only to the feature that prompted them.

1. **Original work only.** The game is inspired by the three-realm war structure of the old realm-versus-realm MMOs. It uses no names, classes, places, lore, art, UI or branding from them or from any other game. Do not draw known characters or logos.
2. **Everything real and functional.** If something is drawn, it works:
   - Doors and gates open, and stairs and ramps lead up to the wall walks and towers.
   - A guard standing on a wall walked up there.
   - Nothing floats, clips through other objects or vanishes. Banners must not swing into walls.
   - Animations match what the body is doing.
3. **A reactive world:**
   - Trees can be chopped or knocked down, grass cut or set alight, and the ground cratered.
   - Walls, gates and houses break and can be repaired.
   - Houses have doors and shutters that open and close, and real interiors you can see through the windows and walk into. They can be set on fire: the fire spreads, the walls char, the roof falls in, and the house is rebuilt later.
4. **Gear lives.** Armour and clothing get dirty, wet, bloodied and damaged, and can be cleaned and repaired.
5. **Weather acts on everything.** Rain wets surfaces and cloth, snow settles on upward-facing surfaces, thunderstorms strike and set things alight, and sun dries and melts.
6. **It must look great.** Every feature ships with its own model and shader work, and visual quality is part of "done".
7. **Late game stays interesting.** The level cap is 50. Content past 20 must scale with the player, and later levels bring new abilities, ranks and goals.
8. **Players know what to do.** There is lore, onboarding and clear objectives:
   - A playtester said the armies' choice of targets "seems random" and that nobody ever wins.
   - Army orders must be visible and steerable.
   - Campaigns must be winnable.
9. **Phones too.** Every feature works with touch, and at all three quality levels (high, medium, low).
10. **Nothing clips.** No grass, flower, prop, log or body pokes through a floor, wall, roof, stair or paving, anywhere in the world. People stand on what they stand on (floors, steps, platforms), never sunk into it. Check new content for this in general, not case by case (the 1 m cover map, `natClearSpot`, `natFallHits`).
11. **Bodies move like living things.** Feet stay planted while on the ground (the gait is foot-locked IK, `HUMAN_GAIT`; beasts plant by stride and leg length), limbs never move in slow motion against the ground speed, and creatures keep moving when they idle or fly (Cinderwing beats, glides with trims, banks, looks about).
12. **Real water.** Water is physical: you can wade and swim (people and animals), ponds and rivers work (rivers flow and carry you), it splashes and ripples, puts out fire, soaks gear, and can be drunk.
13. **Deep systems, easy to play, hard to master, balanced, wired into the realms.** All of these are built (version 8); keep them deep, balanced and wired into each other:
    - class systems with real depth: an elemental magic system that reacts to the world, and systems as deep for warriors, archers and priests, each with realm flavours;
    - animals: taming, pets, livestock, breeding with inherited traits;
    - survival: food and water, hunger and thirst (gentle);
    - farming and herb lore (botany), with plant breeding;
    - crafting (materials, workstations, recipes) and building (placed structures that burn, weather and are repaired);
    - fire for everyone: a burning brand from any fire sets roofs, trees and grass alight.

- **Terrain block CPU topology (2026-10-29):** Far terrain blocks lazily reuse only lattice coordinates and triangle order. Each geometry still reads current heights/normals and owns fresh index data and attributes; crater rebuilds are unchanged. Pinned pre-change CPU tests compare all sixteen blocks, geometry bytes, bounds, resource construction order and UUID random draws. An external Node comparison supports less repeated CPU work; no native loading or frame improvement is established.

- **Bounty HUD focus (2026-10-29):** Desktop hides the standalone bounty card only while the expanded tracked bounty already renders its active counter. Folded/auto-compact/hidden path, narrow target, RTS and touch states retain their existing alternatives. The CSS mirrors current visibility rules; unsupported `:has` keeps the duplicate card. No progress, rewards, interactions, saves or ownership rules change.

- **Prologue final action (2026-10-29):** The final page has one exit: Begin, or Return to the march during replay. Earlier pages retain Skip the prologue/Close; Back restores that option. Only the header markup changes. The existing close, keyboard, focus, prologue-seen save and first-note behavior remain unchanged. Actual-source CPU checks cover the page controls and identical exit effects; native visual verification remains with the coordinating chat.

- **Low-health guidance (2026-10-29):** Badly hurt can show during combat while the player is alive, below 35% health and carrying a healing draught. Its original combat trigger remains; queued unseen help waits when irrelevant and can teach during a later injury. Healing, death or losing the last draught ends an active banner without replay or changing its collected Field note, saves or earned progress. Other note predicates and stores guidance are unchanged.

- **Phone QA viewport witness (2026-10-29):** The ergonomics test retains its exact renderer/aspect condition, 20 ms polling and 15 s deadline. Bounded host/page poll timestamps are diagnostic only; no successful after-state can waive a failed wait. Existing geometry/report reads harvest observations without an added success-path browser await. This records scheduling evidence; the prior CI resize failure is not claimed fixed.

## Build and run

- Run `python3 build.py`. It concatenates `src/page.html` and every `src/NN[a-z]_*.js` module in filename order into one `<script type="module">`, and writes `hallowmarch.html`. three.js 0.160.0 is imported from jsDelivr.
- All modules share one top-level scope after concatenation:
  - Top-level names must be unique across files. `tools/lint.sh` reports redeclarations.
  - No module may contain a closing script tag; `build.py` refuses to build if one does.
- Load order is filename order, but most cross-module references happen at call time. A module can use functions from later modules inside functions, not at top level.

## Working alongside other sessions

Several Claude sessions (and other agents) change the March at the same time, each in its own container or clone. They meet in three places: GitHub's `main`, the Interego record and the live artifact.

1. **A branch for each piece of work** (`feature/<name>`).
   - Before it goes into `main`: `git fetch origin`, then `git rebase origin/main`.
   - Build and lint again, and run the tests the change touches again on the rebased tree.
   - Then `git push origin HEAD:main`, which is accepted only as a fast-forward.
   - Never force-push `main`. If the push is refused, someone landed first: fetch, rebase and test again.
   - Conflicts in `CLAUDE.md` are usually two new lines side by side: keep both.
2. **A worktree for each session that shares a checkout** (sessions on one computer, or helper agents started for tests): `git worktree add ../hallowmarch-<name> -b feature/<name> origin/main`. A cloud session has its own clone and needs none. Two sessions building in one folder overwrite each other's `hallowmarch.html` and `tools/out`.
3. **Say what you are working on in Interego.**
   - Publish a note as the graph `urn:graph:project:hallowmarch:work:<name>`, Hypothetical while in progress: what it is, the branch, the files it touches.
   - Before starting, look at the other notes: `discover_context` on the pod, newest first.
   - When the work is merged, mark the note done.
   - The handoff record `urn:graph:project:hallowmarch` is written only with compare-and-swap: `get_current_head` first, then `publish_context` with `if_match` set to that head.
4. **The live artifact only from merged `main`.**
   - Read it first (the Artifact tool's read).
   - If what it holds is not in `main`, another session published something not merged yet: wait for it, or merge it, rather than overwrite it.
   - Omit `capabilities` and `icon` when republishing.

## Testing

The harness lives in `tools/`:

- `hm.py` is a scriptable runner.
- `hmlib.py` provides `setup()`, used by the test files.
- Both load the page wrapped like the claude.ai host does, serve three.js from `tools/node_modules`, and stub web fonts.
- Chromium runs with SwiftShader (software WebGL), so expect about 30–90 s to boot and a slow frame rate.

**Workflow for any change:**

1. `tools/lint.sh` must report 0 errors. A few unused-variable warnings are known.
2. `python3 tools/tests/shaders.py`: every shader program compiles at high, medium and low, by day and by night. If you touch indoor rendering, also check inside the Barrow (see `tests/barrow.py`). [late3] It also draws the Deep Barrow (the Hall of Pyres with its pitch burning) and a veteran of 50 riding in its mantle and barding at each quality; on a machine loaded by other builders' runs it took more than 15 minutes.
3. Write a focused test for the feature through `window.__hm`:
   - Use `__hm.simulate(seconds)` to advance game time deterministically.
   - Do not wait on wall-clock timers; they run slowly under SwiftShader.
4. Take screenshots from a fixed camera and look at them:
   - Set `__hm.UI.modal = 'menu'; __hm.CAM.mode = 'fixed'`, then position `__hm.camera`.
   - Use `page.screenshot(timeout=300000)`.
5. For war or AI changes, run `python3 tools/soak.py 10`. It must show no errors and no non-finite positions.
   For abilities, scaling and camps, run `python3 tools/tests/level50.py shots`.
   ([perf2]) For anything that draws, thinks or holds more: `python3 tools/tests/perf.py budget` (every view within its budget) and `python3 tools/tests/perf2.py long` (an hour of war: it fails if the heap, the ArrayBuffers or the scene keep growing); `perf2.py boot` and `views` before and after (the boot's steps and memory, a step's and a frame's JS, the worst frames).
6. Check the phone layout with `python3 tools/tests/phone.py`.
7. For lore and onboarding (prologue, Chronicle, path, notes), run `python3 tools/tests/lore.py` and ([guide], version 13) `python3 tools/tests/guide.py` (a new player's first steps by touch alone, and on a desk).
8. Each big system has its own test. Run the ones your change touches:
   - `castles.py`, `houses.py`, `nature.py` and `siege.py` (engines, breaches, sallies, the player's crew). [war2] `houses.py` also has a house's people beat its fire out (and the player with Use); where a house must burn down (its fall, its ruin, its rebuilding) the tests set `__hm.war2.HCREW.off` (so does `worldstate.py`)

a player's deliveries (an hour's timber, stone and iron and an hour of work, every day and every third day) pour more into the realm's works and place it better on average, never always first; a realm without food, iron or timber shows it (no levies, hungry, its projects stalled); the same seed gives the same season; a season saved, read back and run on is the same; a damaged state is made sane and runs a month; votes and officers' orders; a returning player's summary; offensives announced a day and more ahead; the state under 200 KB. `loops.py only=season` runs it (six seeds) and then, in the page: a new game's season (42 days, its muster, every keep its own), the war panel's line, a keep taken in the field in the muster not taken in the season, a delivery and gold given counting season points, a vote, the Chronicle's Season page and its gold button by a click, eight days away (`__hm.season.away`: the war begun, the news told, the keeps in the field as the season holds them, the stores the season's), a keep taken in the field in the war taken in the season and staying its taker's at the battle's end, a live offensive's bands sent at its keep and the holder's bracing, a save read back three days later stepped on and told (and the title's text), a damaged or missing part a fresh season. Also there: a hallow placed in a temple in the field taken by the season and put back where it holds them, the walls' tier on the gate, a season won while away (told, paid, the deed and the name of the Long War). `loops.py only=seasonshots`: `loops_season_phone_{hud,page,work}.png` (390x780, touch) and `loops_season_desk_*` (1280x720, and the war panel alone, `_war`): the war panel's line, the Season page, its works with their buttons, nine days into a season (no sideways overflow).

In the world (after a real click): the listener at the player's head, a blow to the camera's right heard on the right, a house between muffling one (`shotHit`) and the open not, a crash at 150 m a tenth as loud and duller, 400 m off not played; the cap (60 asked in a frame: 2 new voices played, 1 at low and on a phone; of 40 blows at 3 to 100 m the nearest played); the places' air (Brackenford by day and night, each town's murmur at its own pitch, the densest wood, a keep's wall walk, rain out of doors and drumming on a house's roof over you, the street coming in at its open door, a jetty's shore, the Barrow's echo); About 7 minutes; `only=` a few sections.

[net] (second round) `season`: a local server whose season runs 30 times as fast (`HM_SEASON_SPEED`) and its admin key: a phone's page of Ériu (390x780, touch) told the season, the war panel's line, a headless player of its realm on its roster, timber brought from the packs and a work voted for by taps on the Season page, a keep taken in the live war taken in the season and one the season takes (`POST /admin op=keep`) taken in the live war, the live war's own capture not taken back, what the server says set as text, then a desk's page of Thule at Logres' first keep keeping that region (`hosts`), the shard's host told so, the keeper's capture told to the host by the server and into the season, the host's own capture there held for the keeper; `net_season_page.png`. `deployed` (`host=` the Railway domain): its health, `net_season.mjs` against it, two pages on it at once seeing each other and told the season, the round trip. `room`: two pages of one browser in one room (the stand-in, 00n_netstub.js): each the other as a body (realm, calling, level, look), a walk drawn within about two metres behind (median), the gait, a strike, mounting and dismounting, realm chat with markup shown as text, a party (invite, answer, the party's frames, party chat), a tree felled and a fire landed on one page done on the other, the sizes on the wire, the host's keep taken on the follower's page, a follower's capture held and told to the host and taken there, the host leaving (the other takes the war over, its body gone); `lossy` runs the stand-in with 60 ms latency, 40 ms jitter and 5% of moments dropped. `server`: `server/server.js` on a free port, a page with `?server=` and two headless players (`net_client.mjs`): the save asked of the server at the boot, a guest account and its token, the headless player as a walking body, the page heard by it, interest (the near player hears every state, the far one a few for its map), a blow over the server landed and told back, a blow from the muster dropped, a jump to nowhere not relayed, the save held by the server and read back by a new page with the same browser's token, the shared war kept, the guest's account named from the Players sheet, a wrong password refused, and the account signed in from another browser (the page loads again with its character). `perf`: one page alone and with ten players walking round it (`net_fake.js`): a step and a frame (each frame's JS with the GPU drained first, as `perf2.py` does), draw calls, the bytes heard (`quick`: the picture alone). `shots`: `net_room_ally`, `net_room_sheet`, `net_room_kill`, `net_ten_others` (960x540). `net_fake.js`: players that are not pages, speaking the stand-in's messages from inside a page (`NF.add({ name, realm, cls, level, x, z, walk: 'circle', cx, cz, r, speed, accept, d })`: `d` lies dead; also `touch_flows.py only=net`). The server measures a pace by its own clock, so the server part walks the page at the wall clock's pace (stepped faster, its run reads 70 m/s and is rightly dropped). A page boots in 40 to 80 s here; two pages boot together.
   - `merged.py`: a quick smoke test of the whole game after merging branches. It checks that every system comes up, runs a stormy war for a few minutes, and takes two screenshots.
   - `integration.py`: how the version 8 systems fit together: nothing one system places (workstations, halls, paddocks, beds, plants, herbs, animals) stands in another's way or in the water; ice forms at a pond's own level and carries a body; drinking at a river fills the empty waterskins; recipes give their skins back; nothing is built on a tilled bed; three minutes with everything going.
   - `classes.py` (the callings: `mech` checks, `balance` table, `shots`) and `classes_phone.py` (the class panel and buttons on a phone). `classes.py balance` plays every calling with the simple and the skilled bot (`simple` or `skilled` alone; `levels=10,30,50`; `reps=N` for the dummy and the pack, `dreps=N` for the duels, `mreps=N` for the mastery duels; `HM_BAL=path` writes the JSON): the time to kill a standard foe (a level-matched garrison warrior), the time survived against an endless pack of three wolves and two outlaws of the level, their health and harm raised with the fighters' ability rank and gear (`rankMult`, and 8% at 20-39, 16% from 40), every newcomer 1% stronger for each second the fight has lasted ([balance2]: an endless pack of one strength left a fighter either about 30 s or the whole cap, and the median swung between them), the arena their home so they never give up the chase (capped at 150 s, a survivor scores 1.5 times), duels of every pair of callings (both on the same bot, realms swapped), and mastery duels (each calling's skilled bot against its simple bot). Fighters have a player's own measure (`ROLE_MULT.player`) and fair gear (item level = the level, every piece at the stats its slot, grade and level give on average: `fairGear`, 06e_gearcurve.js). TTK and survival are medians, so a stray arrow into a log does not swing the table. [balance3] Every level is measured under clear skies (rain damps fire, soaks foes for storms and swung a run's duels), the arenas are wiped of what the last fighters left (armed snares, runes, holy ground, steam, ice, arrows and bolts in flight), and `together` runs both bots' dummies and packs in one phase when the land has 16 arenas (half the time). `classes.py shots` adds `cls_shieldwall` (a guarded warrior walking on behind a raised shield into an archer's arrows) and `cls_dazzle` (a priest's Smite has dazzled a warrior: motes of light circle its head); `only=` picks the scenes (only those are set up and shot). `classes.py b3` (also run with `mech`): the rules of version 11 checked by number (pursuit (set aside since version 12), frost holds and deep frost, one rush, half piercing, the dazzle by rank and no parry, the shield wall's pace and NPC warriors walling against a bow, the wound and a priest's own healing by rank). [balance4] `classes.py b4` (also run with `mech`): Charge rushes the warrior to its foe and strikes it, its abilities wait for its footing and Shield Bash longer, a snare in its line catches it and holds it there, a rush reaches a foe walking away at 6 m/s and (until Leap Strike) slows it by 45% for 3 s, a skilled priest of rank I holds its mace from a warrior's guard, no rush on a horse or in the water, a guard at its post rushes only within its leash, Mend by the wound, a priest in its own Pillar of Dawn mends as its own wounds do, Rallying Cry's heal at every rank, a volley over a raised shield, the realm's way set aside; `classes.py shots only=rush` adds `cls_rush` (a warrior rushing a mage, shield forward). [balance5] `classes.py b5` (also run with `mech`): Holy Fire flares a mage's firebolt away within 10 m and not beyond, a priest steadfast from its Renewal keeps its Mend through the flare, every Renewal on yourself steadies (the fresh Renewal's rule set aside), a crippling arrow's wound takes 30% off healing while it slows, Whirlwind gives back 2% a foe a cut, a Logres archer draws 15% sooner; `classes.py shots only=hallow` adds `cls_hallow` (a warrior dazzled on a priest's holy ground: the motes over its head). `classes.py balance flat` undoes every crater before each simulated second (a mage's own meteor's bowl shields its foe from its bolts: see Balance of the callings, version 13). Every phase of `classes.py balance` and `duels.py` starts on whole ground: `CB.wipe` undoes the craters and puts out the grass fires the last fighters left (`__hm.bal5.flattenCraters`; a meteor's bowl or a leap's dent with its rim in the line of fire decided the later duels of a run). [balance6] `classes.py b6` (also run with `mech`): renewing yourself while your last Renewal still mends costs twice the power, a seasoned mage's step (12% from rank II, 2% a rank after), a Charge held on its way comes round in half its wait, a mage's ward keeps its spell from a breaking blow for a quarter of what it holds, a skilled archer takes a priest for a blade at its throat only at its mace, the Well of Ériu heals beside the Renewal; `classes.py shots only=ward` adds `cls_ward` (a mage behind its Arcane Ward in the middle of a firebolt the moment a breaking blow is taken by the ward, the warrior who struck beside it, with the HUD: the cast bar running on and "Warded" over the mage); `cls_rush`'s guard has the leash to reach the mage again (since version 12's leash rule it stood at its post and the picture showed no one). `classes.py balance`'s own duels and mastery duels fight in `CB.spotsWide` (below), and every phase has a firebreak round each arena (`CB.breakFires`; 25 m round the pack's arenas, which must stay within 170 m of the player: beasts and outlaws rest beyond it), and no arena lies within 24 m (36 m for duels) of water a fighter could kite into. [balance7] `classes.py b7` (also run with `mech`): the archers' realm ways on their own ground by number (a Logres archer on the ground and on a perch, an Ériu archer in the open and among trees, hiding there within a second where a Logres one takes 1.5 s, a Thule archer in the warm south and in Thule's winter snow: the wind on its arrows, its snare's hold and freeze, a Logres archer there as a plain one), and the rules: at 50 Charge comes round in 12 s, holds Leap Strike back the rush share (`B7T.rushShare`, 5 s) and its blow slows by 40%, plain shafts by rank (1, 1.05, 1.1, 1.15 at 20, 30, 40, 50), Mend at 95% health 0.235 of its measure and all of it at half, the tooltips naming the share and the wait. `classes.py balance`'s duels fight in the open arenas 80 m apart too (`wooded`: version 14's), and every phase's arenas are made whole: `CB.wholeGrass(x, z, r)` lets the cut, burnt and thrown-up ground within 36 m grow back at once (`__hm.nature.NAT`), from `CB.wipe` and after every duel in `duels.py`. [balance8] Its checks read the rules as they stand (`__hm.bal7.B7T`, `__hm.bal8.B8T`): the wound at rank I and from rank II, a priest's own healing rank by rank, Holy Fire's flare through a Renewal's steadiness (`b5`), and Charge's wait and slow from Leap Strike's level (`b7`).
   - `duels.py [levels=10,30,50] [reps=24] [kind=skilled|simple|mastery|both] [pairs=warrior-priest,...] [tap] [trace=N] [cap=60] [gap=90] [narrow]` ([balance3]): the duel scope. Every pair of callings (or the pairs named) fights `reps` duels per level, realms rotated and swapped, up to 18 arenas at once ([balance6] in `CB.spotsWide`: open, dry ground anywhere on the homelands' ring at least `gap` m apart, 11 arenas at 90 m, a firebreak round each; `narrow` for version 13's 52 m round one centre; each arena runs its own queue, the next duel beginning as soon as the last ends and the arena is made whole: 576 duels at 10 in about 2 minutes, at 30 and 50 in about 8) (made exactly as `classes.py balance` makes its fighters; `HM_BAL=path` writes every duel); `kind=mastery` is each skilled bot against its simple self. With `tap`, what happened in each pairing: harm per second by ability (the auto-attack, a drawn arrow, a wound ticking, a ward biting back, or the ability last used: arrows and bolts in flight can land under the next one's name), self-healing, shields, parries, and the share of the fight stunned, rooted, slowed, casting, behind a shield, drawing, praying and in reach, and any harm from outside the duel (`FOREIGN`); `trace=N` prints a timeline of the first N duels. A whole table (three levels, 24 duels a pair) takes 3-10 minutes, much faster than `classes.py balance`'s duels. Pairs of 12 or 24 duels still move by 3 or 4 wins from run to run (and more when other work loads the machine): read a pair's number over two runs before tuning on it. [balance4] `kind=flavour` (`fbot=simple` for the simple bots): each realm's way of each calling against the same calling played plain (`e.plainCalling`: no realm's way), `reps` duels a realm a calling; with `tap` the healing is told by what gave it (`mend`, `sanctuary`, `tick` for a renewal's or holy ground's ticks, ...). Nothing is drawn: the page's own frame loop stops while it measures (`loop` keeps it), which also spares the machine (so does `classes.py balance` run alone). On a machine loaded by other work a whole skilled table took 15-25 minutes. [balance5] A page killed for memory ends the run at once (`PAGE CRASHED`; it waited for ever), and the run ends with a `rules` line: how often each rule came into play (flares, the press's healing, the skilled bots' dodges, the rushes and how they ended, dazzled misses, frost holds). [balance7] The arenas stand on open ground by default (no more than two trees within 20 m of the middle and six within 30 m), 80 m apart (`gap=80`; 9 arenas; `wooded` for version 14's 90 m and trees or not), and the meadow round an arena grows back as each duel ends (`CB.wholeGrass`: a duel's fire burnt it, and the next duels there were fought on ash, where no grass catches and no skilled bot steps out of the flames: the skilled warrior won 22 of 48 duels against a mage at 50 on ash and 9 on whole grass); the duels' scope is told for each bot kind apart (`kind=both` mixed them), and `dry` the share of a fight a side spent short of power (under 15%). **The side made first acts first in every step** (the world's lists are walked in the order bodies were made, and a duel's A side, the first calling of a pair, the realm's way in `kind=flavour`, the skilled bot in `kind=mastery`, was always made first): in a mirror of archers, both of no realm's way, the A side won 71% of 72 duels at 50, and the skilled archer beat its simple self 23 of 24 made first and 14 of 24 made second (a priest's mirror leans less, 42% and 58%). `alt` makes every other duel's B side first (half the duels each way); `kind=flavour` takes `plain=a` (the plain calling as the A side) and `plain=ab` (both plain: the measure's own lean). Read the archer's mirrors (mastery, the realm's ways) with `alt`. [balance8] **Each arena's craters are undone as its duel ends** (`__hm.bal6.cleanArena` finds a crater by its own middle: from version 14 to 16 it looked in the wrong place and a level's queue was fought in arenas cratered ever deeper, the ground 3 to 12 m from where it lay: see Balance of the callings, version 17); each level prints a `clock` line as it begins and ends (game time, the season and its warmth, the night, rain and snow, the arenas in the cold, the craters left, the bodies, the trees within 20 m), and `idle=S` runs the world on S seconds before each level's duels with nothing fought (to tell what the clock does from what earlier duels leave behind). [balance9] **Where a level falls in a run** (version 17's ±7 points at 10): three level 10 tables in one page (`levels=10,10,10`, version 17's rules) moved the simple priest 74, 81 and 70% and the skilled priest 22, 20 and 17% with no rain, no snow and none or one arena in the cold, as 144 duels a calling move by chance (a share's binomial spread is 3.5 to 4 points: over four tables the shares spread as chance spreads them); and one thing did move with the run's clock: a priest bot's devotion (07b_classes.js `csOf` gave every NPC priest 20 to 50, faded at its first look by 0.8 a second of game time, so a bot made in a page's first minute kept most of it and blessed with its first Renewal: the first duels of every page, and every run whose pairs began with a priest's, e.g. `pairs=warrior-priest,...`), now none for a bot at any hour (`B9T.botNoDevotion`). So `clock=fix` (the default) begins every level on the day of the year the page began with and settles the lying snow for it (`seasonSettle`) at every level's start, the first's too (`clock=run` lets the year run on; a jump back settles the snow, which a page fresh from its boot has not done: two of the nine arenas lay in the cold at the later levels' starts and none at the first's, and none or one by each level's end), and level 10, whose duels are quick, fights twice the reps (`reps10=N` sets them: 96 a pair, 288 duels a calling, narrow a share's chance spread from about 3.6 points to 2.5). `pre=JS` runs JS once the page is up, before the levels (a rule set against its absence: `pre=__hm.bal9.B9T.bluntDrawn=0.5`). The clock line's `night` is the uniform the frames last set: nothing is drawn while the duels run, so it does not move. Its `hallows`: the enemy hallows each realm's temple holds (the war runs on beside the duels; each made every body of its realm strike 10% harder, `REALM_BONUS`, the measures' bots too until version 18: with two given to Logres the simple priest of 10 fell from 74% of its duels to 56%).

Screenshots `depth_*`.
   - `gifts.py`: each realm's passive gifts by their numbers, each realm ultimate (effects, cooldown, key 9, HUD, a champion using it), the Chronicle page, the phone pad; screenshots of each ultimate.
   - `motion.py [tag=...] [only=human,beast,farm,bird,player,pose,dragon,shots]`: every kind of body measured from what its shader draws (`__hm.motion`): people at 0.4 to 7 m/s and turning on the spot, wolves, boars, bears, deer, horses, sheep, cattle, pigs, hounds, hens, pheasants and mallards at a crawl, a walk, a trot and a gallop, the player running, sprinting, up a keep's stair, riding (the horse's hooves) and swimming (how far a stroke carries), a kneel and a crouch (feet and knees over the floor), [polish] a person walking while shoved sideways and standing shoved sideways, a wolf and a horse trotting shoved sideways, the player cutting 46 and 92 degrees at a sprint and 46 at a run (`MO.shove`, `MO.cut`), the feet on the stair's treads (`motion_tread.js`: where a foot stands still, its height over the floor under it: on its tread about 0, on the flight's slope line up to half a riser off), every lane clear of anything standing on each body's own line (the cover map: a rack on a lane slid the runner along it mid-measure), and Cinderwing on its circuit, taking off and landing (`motionDragon`, its bones read directly: wingbeats a second, how far a wing tip travels in a beat, the share of time gliding, its bank, how far its head and tail move, its airspeed and the hardest change of it, its feet on the ground once landed). For each body: how far a planted foot slides (cm), its slip as a share of the body's speed (slipK), how high a swinging foot rises, the lowest foot over the floor (5th percentile and lowest), steps a second; the worst offenders listed; writes `tools/out/motion_<tag>.json`; `shots` adds pictures at 960x540 (a pheasant bursting up, beating and gliding, a mallard running across the water and beating, Cinderwing rearing, springing, flying and landing, a runner, a kneeling priest: `tools/out/motion_*.png`); [polish] `seq` adds strips of six frames 1/20 s apart (a horse at a gallop and a bear at a trot from the side with the camera keeping pace, the player cutting 90 degrees at a sprint from a fixed camera: `tools/out/motion_seq_*.png`, at `q=high` unless `q` says otherwise); [motion3] usable at high quality: the page's own frame loop is stopped first (it drew whole frames at high between the strip's own) and one frame drawn to compile the high programs, the lane is mown (`natureCut`) so the legs show over the grass, the camera on whichever side of the lane has no tree or plant near it (`MS.pickSide`), and up a stair the camera behind the player while it steps (it walks the way the camera looks) and abreast and above it for the picture; strips of nine frames of the gallop (a whole stride), the horse's trot and the player walking up a keep's stair from the side, six of the bear and the cut; `seq=gallop,trot,bear,cut,stair` picks them (about a minute a frame at high on a busy machine). Run it before and after anything that moves a body.
   - `gaits.py [only=falls,feet,stair,shove,cuts,crowd] [reps=3] [cuts=26]` ([motion3]; [motion4] `cuts`: the player cutting 46, 92 and 135 degrees at a sprint and 46 and 92 at a run, the cut started at every frame of a whole stride, 26 runs a case, every run's worst stance under 2 cm): the footfalls of a horse's walk (the lateral sequence in four even beats), trot (diagonal pairs together, within a frame of each other: a real trot's pairs part by up to 30 ms) and gallop (hind right, hind left, fore right, fore left, the fore right down before the hind left lifts, one leap a stride after the fore feet); no foot near the ground moving over it (lift-off and touchdown too, within 4 cm of where each foot stands: every beast at a walk and a trot, people running, 1.5 cm at most); a person up a keep's stair at a walk and at a run with no foot in a tread or a riser, every frame; shoves and cuts run after run, every run's worst stance under its limit; 400 bodies near the camera all with their feet held (more than 256) and the lock's JS time a step. [motion5] A person's foot near the ground is measured by the point it stands on (its lowest sole point frame to frame, `soles`: a foot rolls from heel to toe now), the sole's middle printed beside it (`mid`).
   - `actions.py [only=ladder,blow,shove,rush,stop,row,kneel] [noshots] [shots=climb,climb_back,shove,row,rush] [tag=...]` ([motion4], version 14): every action since version 10 measured as a body from what the shaders draw (13r_motion.js's probe, its feet and now its hands: a fist's own points, none another vertex shares): a person climbing a Logres corner tower's ladder (every foot standing on a rung while it holds, its sole on the rung's top and the ball of the foot over it; every hand round a rung while it holds; each limb holds still on its rung 10 to 14 frames at a time), striking from the rungs (the feet on theirs through every blow), the warrior's Charge (its stride's worst stance at 18 m/s, and its landing: no foot moving over the ground), the player halting from a run and from a sprint, six stops across the stride each (a foot near the ground moves at most 2 cm), shoving a beached boat off (the feet step into the stance and stand), at the oars (each hand from its oar's grip, every frame of three strokes, the grips worked out as boatsDraw swings and dips the oars out in the rowlocks: 90% of the frames within 8 cm), a kneeling body (its front foot on the floor, its back knee on it). Pictures (unless `noshots`, 960x540): `act_climb` and `act_climb_back` (a climber half way up a corner tower's ladder, from beside it in the room), `act_shove`, `act_row`, `act_rush`. Writes `tools/out/actions_<tag>.json`.
   - `motion5.py [only=birds,gallop,heel,hammer,jump,rubble,shove,dive] [tag=run] [q=low] [shots]` ([motion5], version 16): what versions 14 and 15 added and what was still off, as bodies from what the shaders draw. `birds`: a hen, a cock pheasant and a mallard walking and running (each planted foot's worst stance in contact within 1.5 cm, a bird's leg being a fifth of a person's; no foot moving over the ground within 1.2 cm of it; the feet on the ground; how high a foot lifts; the head-bob: the share of each step the beak holds still in the air, its speed along the way under a quarter of the body's). `gallop`: a horse at 4.5, 8, 11 and 13 m/s: the share of the time no foot is down, the longest leap as a share of the stride, each foot's share down, the planted feet. `heel`: a person at 0.6 to 5 m/s: how high the heel rises before the toes leave the ground, and how far the point each foot stands on (its lowest sole point, frame to frame: `soles`, 13r_motion.js) moves over the ground in a stance (at most 1 cm), the sole's middle as motion.py measures it. `hammer`: a builder at three houses of Brackenford brought down and being built back, hammering (action 23) at its work spot: the mallet's farthest point at the blow against the wall's face (a shot along its facing), the feet. `jump`: a soldier jumping down from a keep's wall walk into its court as war2's leaders do (a walk whose inner edge drops into the court, the court cleared of bodies round it): no foot in the ground through the landing (a trace of the frames round it), none sliding once down. `rubble`: a Logres corner tower brought down, the player walked (and run) from the field over the rubble into the store room: each planted foot (still in all three axes) against the stone drawn under its sole (`__hm.motion5.rubbleFootFloor`, the highest under heel, middle and toes), with the feet on the stones and with them on the ramps as before (`RUBHF.off`). `shove`: where every beached boat's gunwale lies for a shover at her end (`shoveGeo`: ahead, up over its floor, across), then shoving one off (her drawn pose kept up with her place each step, `__hm.motion5.boatPose`): each hand's lowest point over her gunwale's cap where the hand is along her (from her pose that step), from 0.15 to 0.5 of the action (her first 15 cm away; then the arms straighten after her and come away), by tenths of the action with the hands and the gunwale in the shover's frame, and the feet. `dive`: a diver swimming on under a lake: how far a stroke carries it, strokes a second, the hands' reach ahead and behind. Writes `tools/out/motion5_<tag>.json`; `shots` takes `m5_*.png` at 960x540.
   - `perf.py [low|medium|high] [views=...] [tag=...] [js|render] [profile] [budget] [seed]` ([war3] `budget` and `seed` measure the same war each run: Math.random seeded before the page's own script, through `hmlib.setup`'s `init`, and the page's own frames held once it is up): draw calls, triangles (main and shadow pass) and programs in fixed views (the Logres town with its fields, a keep courtyard, inside its hall, a river, the biggest fight of a running war, a forest, the Barrow, the mountains from the Logres orchard; [perf2] a Thule burh on fire stormed by a band with its garrison at the fires, the Logres town with three houses burning and their crews, a house in rubble and one behind its scaffold, a breached tower mended by the masons: `siege`, `townfire`, `rubble`, `masons`) at each quality ([perf2] `budget`: the run fails when a view goes over its budget, `BUDGET`), the top meshes by triangles (instances x triangles each, named by the function that made them), the JS cost of a step and a frame and the top systems by JS time (every update and draw function timed), the boot's steps and the heap; `profile` adds a sampling profile of the simulation. Writes `tools/out/perf_<tag>.json`. Run it before and after anything that draws or thinks more. [war4] `war=MIN`: the war MIN minutes on before the views (the player kept in town; seeded with `budget` or `seed`, the same war each run: compare builds with the same MIN). [look6] `deep` (one of the default views, standing for four): the Deep Barrow's halls with the player in each (`deep_cistern` flooded, `deep_pyres` burning, `deep_gallery` with a slab fallen, `deep_throne` with the Ash-Crowned speaking his Word): their draw counts and frame, no JS timing; measured after every other view at every quality (they move the war on).
   - `perf2.py boot|views|long|phone|geohash|ab|ctx [...]` ([perf2], version 16): the March on a phone, measured as a whole. `boot [track] [sample] [profile]`: the boot's steps (every one, the first too: `BOOT_STEPS`) with the JS heap as each ends and when the script began, then after the boot and after a game started and a minute played: the JS heap (after a GC, CDP), the ArrayBuffers' backing stores, the GPU's buffers, textures and renderbuffers (counted at the WebGL calls by an init script: `window.__perf2.glBytes()`), the scene's geometries and textures by the system that made them, the processes' RSS, and the world's own checksums (the map image's pixels, the heights); `track` follows every typed array of 64 KB or more from its making (where, and whether it is still alive), `sample` the live JS heap by allocating function, `profile` a CPU profile of the boot (self and with callees, module:line). `views [low,medium] [views=town,keep,siege,battle,barrow,townfire] [frames=60] [profile] [fprofile]`: in each view the steady cost of a step (80 steps, the systems timed, and 160 single steps: median, p99, max, and what the systems of each step over 40 ms took), the first frames in view (programs linked, geometries made and KB sent on first sight) and a minute of the world with a frame each second (each frame drawn with the GPU drained first by a `readPixels`, so its JS is measured apart from SwiftShader's drawing, which is timed on its own); the systems' JS within the frames; the worst frames and what they did; `profile` a CPU profile of 8 s simulated (the timers' wrappers left out), `fprofile` one of ten frames drawn back to back (where a frame's own JS goes; it warms the view, so the first frames it reports are not a first sight). `long [minutes=60] [every=5]`: an hour of AI-only war (the player in its town), every `every` minutes the heap after a GC, the ArrayBuffers, the GPU's bytes, the scene's objects, geometries, textures and programs, the lists that can grow (fires, projectiles, the queue of later work, stuck arrows, the shadow's proxies, engines, masons, rubble, rafters, roles) and three frames at low (the town, the biggest fight, a keep); fails if the heap grows by a quarter (and 12 MB) from the tenth minute to the last, the ArrayBuffers by 24 MB, the scene by 400 objects, the renderer by 300 geometries or 8 textures, or on an error or a non-finite position. `phone [cpu=4]`: 390x780 with touch, the CPU slowed `cpu` times (CDP), the boot at the phone's own quality (low), the first 3 s at 30 frames a second and a minute with a frame each half second, a step's cost, the touch controls' own cost (200 moves of the stick, 200 of a camera drag and 40 taps that pick what is under the finger, each a pointer event dispatched to the canvas, and the style and layout the next frame pays), the memory after. `ab`: the old way and the new turn and turn about in one page (a loaded machine moves each run's time a lot; turns of a few milliseconds see the same load): `collidersNear` with a Set against the stamp, the same lists checked. `ctx`: the WebGL context lost and given back (`WEBGL_lose_context`): the page loads again, the character saved and played on. `geohash`: the merged meshes' arrays hashed (houses, castles, the towers' rooms and moving parts, the Barrow) with the static meshes' arrays kept (`__perf2NoRelease`): run on two builds (`HM_HTML`), the same hashes say the same geometry. The page's own frames are held (`__rafHold`) once it is ready. Writes `tools/out/perf2_<mode>_<tag>.json`.

Under SwiftShader on 2 CPUs a frame at 960x540 takes about 3 s at low, 7.5 to 10 s at medium and 8.5 to 13 s at high, and two browsers at once are no faster (it uses both CPUs): a clip of 4 s at 24 frames a second at medium is 12 to 15 minutes.

9. In test scripts, a `page.evaluate` must never return `window.__hm` or a helper object that holds it. Playwright tries to serialise the whole game and stalls. End helper scripts with `;0`.

**Debug API (`window.__hm`, defined at the end of `13_main.js`):**

- `ready` and `errors`: the boot flag and every runtime error caught.
- `start({realm, cls, level})` starts a game. `realm` is 0 Logres, 1 Ériu or 2 Thule; `cls` is `warrior`, `archer`, `mage` or `priest`.
- `simulate(sec)` runs the fixed-step simulation and returns a war summary.
- `teleport(x, z)`, `setTod(p)` (time of day) and `look(yaw, pitch, dist)`.
- `frame()` renders one frame; `renderInfo()` returns draw calls, triangles and programs.
- `GAME`, `WAR`, `ENT`, `UI`, `CAM`, `DUN`, `INDOOR`, `BARROW`, `BARROW_STATE`, `INV`, `LOOT`.
- `dbg.*` exposes renderer internals; `fn.*` exposes most game functions.
- [walls] `walls` (`07g_walls.js`): `WALLS` (`stuck`, `fall`, `stats`), `shotHit(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz, o)`, `wallsShotClear(e, t, arc)`, `wallsAimY`, `wallsProj`, `wallStrike`, `wallArrow`, `wallsStoneStep`, `wallMatOf`, `wallHouseOf`, `wallInRoof`. `breach` (`04g_breach.js`): `TBREACH` (`stats`: hits, breached, mended, fell), `list()` (the towers' sections), `sync`, `upload`.
- `heights` (attached by `03d_heights.js` at boot): `HTS` (the land before the shaping `H0`, `walk0`, what anyone could reach `reach`, the shaped texels `changed`, the keep mask), `stats()` (time, texels changed, blocked, filled, taken back, settled, hardy trees, crags), `was(x, z)` (the height before), `changedAt(x, z)`.
- `LORE` (attached by `10c_lore.js`): `openPrologue`, `openChronicle(section)`, `complete(stepId)`, `check()` (one look at the world for steps and notes), `progress()`.
- `guide` (attached by `10e_guide.js`, [guide]): `GUIDE` (`mark`, `near`, `stats`: notes held and shown), `GUIDE_WATCH`, `GUIDE_HELP`, `CHRON_EXTRA`, `mark()` (the next step's place now, how far and which way), `guideMarkOf(step)`, `guideWhere`, `guideAims`, `guideNoteIndex`, `guideMade(rec)`, `guideQuiet`, `chronGoals`, `chronGear`, `chronSieges`, `drawMinimap`.

## Architecture

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `00_util.js` | Maths, noise and random helpers |
| `00n_netstub.js` | [net] (version 19) A stand-in for the artifact runtime's `room`, `db` and `user` over a BroadcastChannel and localStorage, with the runtime's rules where they shape the client (presence merged, 4 KiB, coalesced; topics refused unless `emit: true`; db writes refused for a Viewer; named rooms; latency, jitter and drops on demand). Installed only when `window.__HM_NET` is set before the page's script (the tests) or the address has `?net=local`, never over a real `window.claude`; loaded right after 00_util.js so the boot's save sees it. See Multiplayer |
| `01_world.js` | World layout (realms, sites, lakes, navigation graph), heightfield, masks, colliders (`COLL`, `addBox`), `heightAt` / `isWalkable` / `zoneAt` |
| `01b_water.js` | Where the water stands: a river per realm carved down its valley into its lake (`RIVERS`), ponds in the closed hollows (a priority flood; other hollows are filled, so there are no dry pond beds; `PONDS`), `WATERGRID` (surface, flow and white water per 2 m texel), `waterAt(x, z)`, deep water in `W.walk` (2), `swimPassable`, `deepWaterAt`, `riverAt` |
| `02c_water_map.js` | The water map every shader can read (`GLSL_WATER_MAP`: `waterMapAt`, `rippleAt`, `causticNet`); the ground under and beside the water (`GLSL_WATER_GROUND`, called by the terrain shader: bed of sand, silt or gravel with a wobble, caustics, beach, the wet band the waves lap); the ripple simulation round the player (`stepRipples`, `rippleDrop`: high 256², medium 128², low off) |
| `03b_water.js` | The water surface: one mesh over every lake, pond and river at its own heights (no overlaps), see-through with absorption by depth, flow-mapped waves downstream, white water where rivers fall, shore foam, sky, clouds and far shore mirrored, rain rings and the ripple field |
| `02_render.js` | Renderer, `QUALITY_PRESETS`, shared uniforms `U`, `mat()` / `shareMat()`, GLSL chunks, sky, post-processing (bloom, light shafts) |
| `02b_nature_map.js` | The nature map: one texel per metre over the whole land for cut, burnt, burning and dug-up ground, uploaded to the GPU only where it changed |
| `02d_season.js` | The seasons' side of every shader: the uniforms `uSeasonA` (spring, summer, autumn, winter weights), `uSeasonB` (leaves turned, leaves fallen, blossom, fresh green), `uSeasonC` (flowers, summer gold, snow line shift, the air's temperature now), `uSeasonD` (apples, drifting leaves, fireflies), the season map `uSeasonMap` and `uSnowK`; `GLSL_SEASON`: `seasonMapAt`, `seasonTemp`, `snowHere`, `frostAt`, `seasonGrass`, `seasonLeaf`, `seasonTurnK`, `seasonFallen`, `twigCard` |
| `03_terrain.js` | Terrain, water, grass, flowers, trails, decals. [land] The terrain shader's rock lies in beds at the mountain's own scale (`landFacets`), with scree fans of angular stones set in grit (`talusAt`: two sizes, each stone smaller than its Voronoi cell and lying at its own tilt, so it never reads as paving), heather on the lower slopes, water streaks, damp gullies and the high snow by altitude, realm and season (one marked block after the rock block, and the `rk`, `nr` and `snow` lines) |
| `02e_land.js` | [land] The mountains' shader side: the land map `uLandMap` (2 m texels: r bare rock round the crags, g scree, b gullies, a heather) and `GLSL_LAND` (`landMapAt`, `landRockTone`, `landStrata`, `landAlong`: a coordinate along a face that never swings with its normal (world x or z, switched on a ragged fault line); `landFacets`: the faces broken as bedded rock breaks, not as a wall is built (version 10's first blocks read as coursed masonry from the orchard): beds about 2.9 m on average, thick and thin, their lines wavy, each with its own tone, the harder ones with a rounded lip that catches the light and holds the snow and a shaded undercut; bed lines open only along stretches; joints 6 to 18 m apart, wandering and only some open, within about 70 m; the beds within about 230 m; smooth where a bed would be only a few pixels; cracks at least a pixel wide or none (no dashed lines); `landStreaks`, `landSnowLine`: Thule's peaks white all year, the south's only in winter; `landSnowHold`: how much of it holds on a face that steep) |
| `03c_land.js` | [land] The mountains. `mtnShape` (from `buildWorld`, once the walk mask exists): the mountain ground with nothing walkable within two texels and no hollow near it is reshaped (teeth and notches along the crests, gullies down the fall line, ledges along the bedding planes as a monotone remap of height), then any hollow it made is filled and any change to a spill height elsewhere taken back, so every height, slope and normal a body or a later placement reads is exactly as it was. `mtnPlaceCrags` ([heights] from `mtnHeights`, once the whole mountain is shaped: 03d_heights.js): crags on the final ground, clear of every walkable texel's square by 1 m, of the water and the trees (kinds: 0 cliff band, a lens along the contour, 1 buttress leaning into the slope, 2 pinnacle on a crest or a sharp ridge, 3 tor, 4 boulder in the scree below a crag; shrunk to fit narrow faces), the bare rock and scree round them, `MTN.top` (the highest rock over each texel), the land map. `buildCrags`: one ring-and-layer mesh shaped per instance in `CRAG_VS` (uneven strata, stepped ledges, lobes, joints, lean, a top that follows the slope, a broken edge), a near model (12 x 7) and a far one (9 x 4) dithered across each other and out by `MTN_D` per quality; the nearest cast shadows. `updateMountains` (from `tick`) refills the lists when the camera has moved 3 m. `mtnCamRoom` (asked by `cameraRoom`, 09_player.js) pulls the camera in before it would enter a crag; `mtnCoverAll` (from `buildCoverMask`) keeps grass out of them. Test hooks `__hm.mtn` |
| `03d_heights.js` | [heights] The mountains shaped from everywhere, the walkable slopes and the skyline too (version 11). `mtnHeights` is a boot step after the farming (13_main.js, "Raising the mountains"): everything (trees, rocks, camps, plants, herbs, workstations, boats) has been placed on version 10's ground by then, so every list and every saved index is as it was. `htsField` reads each part of the range (the ring, the ridges between the realms, the outer wall: `htsParts`) in its own frame, along its crest and across it (the across direction squeezed so patterns run down the fall line), and adds peaks and saddles along the crests (`htsPart`), ribs down the faces, knobs, notches and false summits whichever way a ridge runs (`htsKnobs`, isotropic ridged noise), roughness and a lift to the peaks (the south's stay under its summer snow line: `htsCap`); the ribs, knobs and roughness grow with the slope (to 2.6 times), since a change of height moves a cliff only by the height over the slope. `htsErode`: a few rounds of stream-power erosion (each texel drains to its steepest neighbour; the water gathered cuts by its square root and the fall, never below the next texel down and never more than 10 m; the hillsides creep and the steepest faces slump), so gullies branch down the fall line round the ends of the ring at the passes and the junctions as anywhere. `htsKeep`: the ground stays exactly as it was on and round the roads, sites, camps, rivers, water and the ponds' hollows, standing stones, every collider and the farm plots (ground rising well above a road, a site or a camp is not kept: the walls of the passes are shaped); trees, rocks, plants and herbs are not kept but keep their footing (the ground round each moves as one with it, `objs`) and settle onto it. `htsApply`: every texel anyone could reach (`htsReach`, flooded from the roads as the land's checks do) stays walkable (where a slope there would pass the limit the share is eased off over a few metres, never at one texel; a few texels by a filled hollow may end a little steeper and stay walkable), any hollow the shaping made is filled (`mtnFlood`: no dry pond bed), and round ground left as it was that would become a deeper hollow, or drain another way by a pond, the shaping is taken back; the map's corners beyond the outer wall are left as they were. Then: the walk mask (texels no one could reach that are too steep now are blocked, `HTS.walkLost`; nothing new opens), the rock, grass and flower masks from the new slopes, everything on the mountains settled (trees in their chunk instances, rocks in theirs, colliders' `baseY`, plants, herbs), the land map's gullies, `htsTrees` (hardy pines and birches on the gentler lower slopes, sparse, thinning and stunted with height, none above 46 m in the south or 30 m in Thule; added after every tree there was, each with its collider, near-tree grid entry and nature state, drawn in a chunk mesh that already draws pines or birches there, so no draw is added: 126 of them, 75 pines and 51 birches), the crags on the final ground (`mtnFreeAgain`, `mtnPlaceCrags`: about 1,300) and outcrops on the walkable lower slopes (`htsOutcrops`, 40 of them: tors and boulders, mostly on the spurs, in belts, clear of everything kept and placed and of the roads; each a crag with `c.outcrop` and a collider of its own, tag `rock`, marked `outcrop` and left out of mountains.py's checksum of the colliders, stamped into `MTN.top` for the camera; the walk mask is left as it was; `mtnCheck` leaves them out of its checks of crags on unwalkable ground), `buildCrags`, the terrain's vertices, bounds and textures (`htsRefresh`) and the cover map. About 2.8 s at boot here on a quiet machine, 6-7 s while other runs kept it busy (the field 0.2 s, the erosion 0.5, the slope limit and the fills 1.0, the crags 0.5, which version 10 spent in `buildWorld`: `stats().T`, `TT`). Test hooks `__hm.heights` |

The towers: Logres, four corner drums (`towerStone`: store, guard room at the walks with a door onto each, open top) and two gate drums (`towerGateStone`, `GATE_TW.stone`: the gate-ward's room, a room at the walks with a door onto the front walk and one onto the walk over the gate, an open top over the gate); Ériu, two gate drums of stone under thatch (`towerGateRath`: a store, a ladder up through a hatch onto the platform at the walks' height) and two side lookouts in the ring wall (`towerLookout`: the same, the walk running on through the platform); Thule, four corner and two gate shafts of logs (`towerTimber`: a store, a room at the walks with a door onto each walk that meets it, a fighting gallery under the shingles). The doors and lids of a keep are one mesh moved vertex by vertex when one swings (`towerParts`, `towerPose`); what is only seen from inside is a mesh of its own for each castle, drawn only within 70 m of the camera (`towerInnerVis`, called each frame by `updateMountains`). The rooms keep the rain and snow out (`towerRoofOver` in `skyOver` and the splashes, `towerRoofsForRain`). `towerRoomOf(e)`: the tower whose rooms hold a body, and the floor (`lv`, `top`). Routes: `towerWayUp` (a corner drum from its side walk), `towerWayIn` (any tower from its courtyard door, up every ladder). The section's own machinery does the rest (`castleSiegeHit` wears and breaches it, `castleBreach`, `updateBreaches` mends it in peace, `castleRepairDone`, the land's save): `W.floors` (the rooms' and the top's floors, the thresholds at the walks), `W.colls` (the ring of masonry open in the V, its pieces above the stump, the top's crenels and pole, the furniture), `W.lower` (pieces cut down to the stump while it lies breached), `W.rubbleFloors` (a ramp up from the field over the fallen face and one down into the store room), `W.wreck` (`towerRubbleGeo`: the mound, tumbled blocks, the floor's broken beams, the broken ends of the drum) and `W.scaffold` (`towerScaffoldGeo`). `towerBreachUpload` (from `castleCutUpload`) gives the castle shader each tower (`uKA`/`uKB`/`uKC`: centre and radius and the height above which nothing stands, the breach's direction and the V's foot and half-angle, the inner radius and the rubble's top, wear and fresh stone; `towerBreachCut` in `TBREACH_GLSL`, part of `CASTLE_CUT_GLSL`: cracks spread over the drum as it wears, the upper works and a ragged V are discarded, the store room's contents above the rubble) and keeps the tower's own state with its section's (`towerBreachSync`, idempotent: `T.breached`, ladders `gone`, hatches and doors at the walks `gone`, the pieces cut down, the torches out, the banners on its top folded away). `towerBreachFall` (from `castleBreach`): whoever stands up there falls (the ladder fall's motion: harm by the height), the climbers on its ladders are knocked off. `towerBreachMended` (from `castleRepairDone`): the archer whose post is on its top walks up again. A breached tower is open ground (`towerRoomOf`, `towerRoofOver` and the shader's shelter leave it out). [siege2] (version 13) The engines take a tower for their mark when it is the weaker way in (`siegeMarks`, 04i_siege2.js), and a band storms a fallen tower one or two at a time through its store room (`siegeStormBand`, `siegeStormStep`: in version 12 a band of ten sent in over the rubble stood stuck in the store room and the gap for over two minutes); the garrison holds the court before its courtyard door either side of the door's line (`towerPlugAt`), and the player can storm it (`towerBreachRoute`). Loads before 04g_castles.js (its GLSL is part of the castle shader's). Test hooks `__hm.breach` [motion5] (version 16) The stones of `towerRubbleGeo` over the ways in lie sunk in a mound of broken stone over the ramps (`rubbleSinkY`, `rubbleMound`, 13y_motion5.js), so a stormer's feet are on the stones drawn under them. |

A fire spell or a burning arrow landing on the logs, a brand held to them (E: 'Set the palisade alight', `palisadeFireOffers` from `towerFireOffers`), the dragon's breath (`palisadeFireCone`) or a burning tower beside them sets a cell alight (`palisadeFireAt`, asked by `fireLandsAt` with the caster: never the fire of the keep's own realm, `palisadeSpared`; the player's always, a soldier's only now and then, `PAL_T.npcCatch` 0.3; a spark with no caster never takes again in a charred stretch); it takes hold over `PAL_T.climb` s with real flames and smoke against both faces and along the top (`palisadeSpots`), chars the logs, spreads to the cells either side (`PAL_T.spread`, at most `PAL_T.reach` (3) stretches from where it took hold: `c.gen`; at a wall's end into the tower its logs meet), the keep's own people within 3.5 m beat it down (`PAL_T.douse`), burns whoever stands against it or on the walk behind it, sets the grass alight with its embers (never the wall itself: `PAL.sparking`), and rain or snow damps it (a young fire in a downpour goes out, `st` 2: charred, standing). After `PAL_T.burn` s a cell burns through (`st` 3): neighbouring burnt cells are gathered into a gap (`palisadeGapOpen`: a section-like record, kind `burnt`, `pal` set: `wx`, `wax`, `half`, `across`, `state` 'breach'), the palisade's colliders on that line are cut over it (`palisadeWallColls`, `castleSplitColl`: the middle stands down), a heap of charred stumps and fallen logs lies in it (`palisadeWreckGeo`), and it is a breach (`palisadeGaps`: `siegeOpenBreach`, `siegeDanger`, `siegeOnBreach` plugs it with the guards not already holding another breach, and tells of it once in 30 s a castle). In peace (`PAL_T.quiet`, and no fire within 6 m of it along its wall) its owners build it back behind scaffolding over `PAL_T.rebuild` s (`palisadeScaffoldGeo`, `palisadeGapClose`), and a charred stretch that stood is replaced; new logs pale for `PAL_T.fresh` s. The castle shader (`PAL_GLSL` in `CASTLE_CUT_GLSL`: `palisadeCut(vW, vMat)`, its logs, sharpened tops and loopholes only) reads up to `PZ_MAX` (6) zones a castle (`uPS`, `uPY`, `uPA`, `uPB`: runs of burning or charred, burnt-through, rebuilding or fresh cells, `palisadeUpload`): their char, embers and fresh timber as a burnt tower's (`tChar`, `tGlow`, `tFresh`), and above a gap's stumps it discards (a ragged top and ragged ends). `updatePalisades` from `updateSiege`. Save part `world.x.palisade`. Loads before 04g_castles.js. Test hooks `__hm.palisade` |

Save part `world.x.blaze` (cells not whole: burning with their time, charred, burnt through and how far built back; burning gates). Also calls `houseRafterSync` (04j_rafters.js) each step. [motion3] `HUMAN_GAIT`: `footPath` lands a foot at the stance's pace (standing still over the ground) and steeply, `humanStepCap` (short steps on a steep flight); a leg swung out for the lock is turned by the ankle's real depth under the hip (where the leg cannot reach that deep and `legIK` lifts the ankle, by the depth it reaches: `rL`, `upL`); the toes point down in the air no faster than the foot rises (the toes 0.13 m ahead of the ankle and 0.09 below it rise at least three quarters as fast as the ankle) and the ankle comes forward over them as the foot turns (`pvL`), so they leave the ground from where they stood; a body leaning into a turn has each ankle first set where the lean (about the ground under its middle) will carry it to its place (`lnK`); the ankle undoes the leg's turns in the reverse of their order (the thigh's and knee's pitch, then the hip's swing out and the lean), then gives the foot its heading (the lock's: a planted foot keeps its own while the body turns over it) and its pitch; `FOOT_LOCK` has 1024 rows, its fourth channel 10 (20 on a stair's tread) plus half that heading's turn [motion4] (version 14) `armIK` (the arm's two-bone IK in the body's own plane), `rungLimb`, `ladderLegs` and `ladderHands` (each foot on a rung while it bears the climber, its sole on the rung's top and the ball of the foot over it, each hand round a rung while it holds, then the limb reaching up past the next rung for the one above, the diagonal pair together, on the rungs' cycle: the phase from `towerLadderStep`, the rungs `LADDER_AHEAD` 0.33 m ahead, in the world's metres over the body's own size) in actions 14 and 18; a blow, a flinch, a reach, a smash and a parry (1, 4, 5, 8, 11) shift the weight over feet that stay (the legs reach them by IK from `fL.x - stepZ`); the boat's shove (19) steps each foot into the stance, lifted, over the floor the lock gives, the hips sinking as far as the legs need; at the oars (16) the hands reach the grips where boatsDraw has the oars (`OAR_GRIP`, `OAR_LOCK`; no horse's seat motion for a rower), each arm swung in at the shoulder as its grip comes in toward the keel (`uaLy`, `uaRy`: a turn about the chest's upright, applied after the shoulder's pitch and roll, none unless set); the kneel's front foot on the floor (`legIK(0.5, -0.402)`). [motion5] (version 16) A walker's heel rises before its toes leave the ground: the ankle pitches the foot about the ball (0.14 m ahead of the ankle and 0.088 below it) through the last `hoD` (0.3 of the duty walking, 0.24 running) of the stance, up to `hoP` (0.62 rad walking, 0.5 running), and on into the swing's toes-down, so the point it stands on stays put while the sole's middle rises and rolls forward (a walker stood flat-footed to the last frame and the foot left the ground all at once); a mallet in the right fist (`WB.hammer`, bit 22) and body action 23 (hammering at a wall); a crouch (action 13) keeps each foot where it stands (the lock's place, on its own floor) with the legs reaching it wholly as the hips sink (it set the feet at fixed places, and its legs, mixed by their angles with the gait's, stood a body landing from a fall 10 cm in the ground); a shover's hands on her gunwale (action 19: the gunwale's height and her keel's offset come packed in the action's value, `motion5ActValue`, 13y_motion5.js; the hips as low as the hands need, the body following her for her first 0.3 m). |

[polish] `beastBodyGLSL(K)`: the gait (`bbGait`, `bbFoot`: the foot meets the ground and leaves it still going back under the body, the retraction kept to the ends of the swing, lifted and set down steeply), the target of each leg's low joint with the hoof or paw level under it (`bbTarget`, `bbTuck`), the vault (`bbVault`: the forequarters and hindquarters come down as far as their planted legs need to reach the ground, so straight-legged beasts no longer float their feet at the ends of a stride) and the body's turns (`bbBodyFwd`, `bbRot`); in `beastVS` every turn and drop of the body (lean, bob, lunge, vault, pitch, the back's flex) is undone along the leg before its IK, and the hoof or paw keeps its rest angle (`lowA`); the planted-foot lock (`footLock`, 13s_footlock.js) moves a foot's target along and across (the leg swings out about its top, the hoof rolls back level). The same chunk with the horse's joints gives `horseSeat` to the humanoid shader (`HORSE_SEAT_GLSL`, set here, then `humanoidMat` is built again): the saddle and the rider move with the horse's back. [motion3] (version 12) A foot rises its first `BB_LIFT` m (5.5 cm, once the beast moves at all) in the last `BB_CLEAR` (0.15) of its stance still standing where it stood, and comes down its last ones onto its landing place in the first of the next (`bbFoot` returns its clearance in z; `bbLift` adds it to the swing's arch), so no foot moves over the ground near it; the walk is the lateral sequence in four even beats (hind left, fore left, hind right, fore right: it was the diagonal one), the trot the diagonal pairs, the gallop hind right, hind left, fore right, fore left spread by its own duty (`gp` 0.12 between the pairs, the fore right `gq` = 0.8 of the duty after the hind left, so it is down before the hind left lifts: no leap with the legs flung fore and aft, only the gathered one after the fore left), the gallop's legs reaching to 0.46 of their length (0.42); the vault reaches where the lock holds each foot along the body (`bbVault`'s `dz`: a foot held back as the body sets off dragged up off the ground); a foot to the side turns the leg about its top by the angle that sets the low joint over it (`Tr.y - tg.y`: the hock and the fetlock hang straight below, so from the top the hind feet went half as far as the lock asked) and steps in under the body to 0.85 of the way to the middle. The test uniform `uBbDbg` is gone [motion4] Each foot's paw or hoof is built with its sole on the ground (y 0) wherever the rig's foot point is (`sole` by the kind of foot): a wolf's and a hound's pads stood 1.3 to 1.6 cm over it, a deer's hooves 0.9, a boar's and a pig's 0.7 to 1 cm and the cattle's 1.7 to 2 cm into it. [motion5] (version 16) The gallop's stance is longer (duty 0.3 of the stride, at most 0.58 of the leg's reach: `dG`; the pairs `gp` 0.14 apart, `gq` 0.8 of the duty) and the trot's too (at most 0.5 of the reach), so a horse at 11 m/s is in the air for a third of its stride, once, gathered (the leap was 0.48 of it); the hind feet's stance is set back under the body by `hb` (what the longer stance would carry them past the hip, `bbVault` and the foot both: the hind feet dragged 1.7 to 3.7 cm as they left the ground without it); `flBeastGait` (13s_footlock.js) mirrors it. |

At the end of a boat drawn up on the shore (or aground) that lies up the beach, E or the pad's Use shoves her off (`boatShoveOff`, `boatShoveEnd`: the player leans into her, body action 19, and she grinds down into the water, `boatLaunchStep`, then drifts on free). | `07c_balance.js` | [balance] The balance of the callings. Bots that play a calling (`e.bot`, `botMake(e, 'simple' or 'skilled', home)`): an NPC bot has the role `bot` (no other think runs for it; `updateNPCs` still ticks its buffs, swings, power and footing) and is played by `botStep` from `npcClassStep`; the player with `P.bot` is played from `updateClasses` (the Hollow King check in `barrow.py`). The simple bot presses 1-8 in turn and lets the auto-attack run; the skilled one parries on the glint, spends momentum and changes stance (warrior), keeps range, kites, snares, picks arrows and draws fully (archer), plays the combos, minds attunement and blinks from blades (mage), heals early, keeps a renewal up, shields, hallows the ground, prays when safe and smites (priest). `fairGear(cls, level)`: a full set of the quality a soldier of that level wears (fine below 20, rare to 40, epic above). Diminishing returns on crowd control (`ccAdjust`, asked by `addBuff`): for players, bots and champions (`ccChampion`: camp champions, keep lords, hallow and muster wardens, warband leaders) a stun (a freeze counts as one), root or snare within 15 s of the last of its kind lasts half, then a quarter, then 6 s of immunity; a parry's stun goes through it for anyone (`{ ccAll: true }`); shown on the class panel (`classDrHud`). An allied priest near the fallen player offers to raise them (`raiseOfferStep`; the death screen's `#death-raise` beside the release): accepted, the priest walks over, prays if devotion is short, and raises you (`raisePlayer`). Tracked quarry on the minimap (`drawTrackedMinimap`). [balance2] The callings' answers: the mage's ward takes a stun (`wardTakesStun`), the warrior's Charge frees it for 2 s (`chargeFree`), the priest's own Renewal steadies its spells (`priestSteadfast`, `breakCast`) and its own healing falls with the square of its rank (`priestSelf`), the archer's Tumble slows the foes it leaps from (`tumbleSlow`) and its broadheads' wounds mend slowly (`healWound`); a melee blow sets a cast back (`castPushback`). Out of a court: a band's way starts at the court of the walls its leader stands in (`bandStartNode`, from `wbPlan`: the nearest node in sight was often one outside the wall), and a leader or member in a court whose way lies outside goes out by the gate (a gate of its own realm opens for it while no foe stands within 19 m of it; with foes before it the band waits inside: `bandLeaderExit` at the end of `updateWarband`, `bandGateOut`, `bandExitPoint`); a band in the court of the keep it attacks takes the court for its goal, not the gate behind it (`bandInsideKeep`, in `updateWarband`). A leader that gets no nearer its next point for 8 s with nothing holding it finds its way round on a 1 m grid toward it, at most 60 m on (`bandLeaderDetour`: `localPath` with `gates`, so a castle's gate and a wall standing from the ground are walls), else its way is planned again. A climber (not the player) held on a ladder by a foe ahead for 25 s goes back the way it came (`ladderHeldTurn`, from `ladderRungs`). A band cut down to fewer than three (not bearing a hallow, not under the player's order) no longer holds its place at the muster (`cwBandsCounted`, from `planWar`: at low a realm musters two bands, and a lone soldier stuck at a far keep held one for ten minutes), and the next band to muster takes them in (`cwMergeRemnants`). | `08m_realm.js` | [loops] The realms' own life over a season of weeks (version 19), the shared contract with net: one plain JSON state `RS` and pure functions, with no three.js, DOM, canvas, audio or `window` (it runs unchanged in Node: `module.exports` at its end when there is a `module`). `realmSimInit(seed, opts)` (a fresh season: `opts.days` (42), `opts.keeps` (each keep's home realm), `opts.names` (the realms' and keeps' names for the news), `opts.t0` (ms of its start)), `realmSimStep(RS, dt)` (sub-steps of at most 60 s; deterministic for a seed: its own mulberry32 on `RS.rs`), `realmSimContribute(RS, realm, kind, amount, who)` (a good of `RSM_GOODS`, gold, or `'work'` hours: into the stores up to their cap and the rest into the realm's works, `R.bank`; returns the season points it earned), `realmSimOrder(RS, realm, order, who)` (`{type:'project', id}`: a vote, or from realm rank 5 an officer's order; `{type:'target', keep}` and `{type:'muster'}` officers only), `realmSimSummary(RS, realm, since)` (the clock, the standing, the stores, the project, the offensives, the news since `since`), `realmSimSanitize(obj, opts)` (anything not a state: a fresh season), `realmSimLive(RS, ev)` (the live war's news: a keep taken, a battle won, a hallow carried). **The season** (`RSM`): 42 days (`RSM.days`, a setting), the muster for its first sixth (a week: the realms build and train, nothing can fall), the war, the reckoning for its last two days (the points frozen, the winner named), then a new season (the keeps and hallows home, half the stores kept, the levies halved, a smithy, granary and yard kept at one, walls at a tier at most, `RS.past` the record). **Each realm** (`RS.realms[r]`): its stores `s` (food, timber, stone, iron, hides, wool, horses, gold: `RSM_GOODS`; capped at four times `RSM.target`, the granary raising food's, the yard horses'), filled while nobody plays by its town's work an hour (`RSM.prod`, weighed by the keeps as 08m_loops.js weighs it: `keepLost`, `keepWon`; a realm behind in points works up to a third harder, `RSM.catchUp`) and each keep's land to whoever holds it, drawn by its soldiers eating (`RSM.eat` an hour each: the levy, the garrisons, the armies; with none it goes hungry: its sieges and its walls hold worse), its levies trained (`RSM.levyCost` a soldier, every quarter hour, up to `RSM.levyMax`), its garrisons refilled from the levy, its gates mended (timber and stone), its treasury buying at the border fairs a share of what its work lacks (`RSM.price`; gold comes from its town and the players), and its works: one project at a time (`act`, `prog`), each with its goods (`RSM.projects`: walls a tier (a keep's: the one an offensive is announced against first), a granary, a horse-breeding yard, a smithy, siege engines stockpiled for the offensive) drawn above a reserve of half the target as fast as a day (so the stores, and what players bring, set the pace); the players' votes choose the next. **The strategic war** (while nobody plays): every two hours each realm decides: an offensive announced `RSM.lead` of the season ahead (two days) against the keep it can take that weighs most (its own lost keep, the leader's, the weakest walls and garrison, the nearest; an officer's aim first), raids on the fields and yards of another (the leader most often: food, timber and hides carried off, or the raiders caught), a hallow raid by a realm holding three keeps on a temple whose realm has lost one (the hallow home two days later), an army to win back a keep of its own. Armies (`RS.armies`) march on the strategic map (the game's own layout, `RSM_GEO`) at `RSM.march` metres an hour; a siege is resolved by the numbers an hour at a time (the attackers by their number, arms (the smithy), hunger, engines and how far behind their realm is; the defenders by their garrison, arms, hunger, the walls' tier, the gate and the catch-up), the holder relieving it from its levy up to a garrison and a half; a keep that falls goes to the attackers with a share of the loser's stores. **Season points** (`RSM.sp`): an hour of the war, a realm's own keep 0.5, a keep taken 2.5, an enemy hallow in its temple 3; a project 20 (walls a tier 12, an engine 5), an offensive that takes its keep 15 (beaten off, 9 to the defender), a battle won in the field 10 (5 in the muster), each 40 units delivered 1 (gold a quarter, iron four times, a horse forty).
