a fallen slab's cells are 0, no ground), the dais) and `late3BuildDeep` (from `buildDungeon`): its walls, headers and roofs (`deepShell`, the Barrow's own builder leaves every deep cell to it: `late3IsDeepCell`), in dark basalt with ember-lit cracks in the hot halls and weeping stains in the cistern (the embers in its cracks, the rings of its pillars and its throne's runes in a glowing material of their own, `deepEmberMat`: a `DeepBatch` sends what is added as a rune in an ember's red to a batch of its own, drawn inside its mesh), its floor (`deepFloorMat`: great worn flags of basalt, ash in the joints, embers glowing faintly in the hot halls' joints, damp and catching the light in the cistern), the stair's steps, a kerb round the basin, pillars standing in it and three sluices in its wall, six pyres (two burning) and braziers, the trenches under the slabs and their beds of embers (`deepPitMat`), the channels of pitch (`deepChannelMat`: black and glossy, ash once burnt, flames running along them from a texture of each cell's heat and char, `DEEP.heatTex`), the throne (a seat for a king twice a man's height, ember runes), pillars, fire-bowls and lights of what burns there (`DUN.lights`); the seal (`deepSealMesh`), the cracked wall and its rubble (made when first shown), the 17 slabs, the cistern's water (`deepWaterMat`, one sheet moved up and down). It is drawn only while you are in it or in the Hollow King's hall above it (`DEEP.root.visible`). Its halls are lit by what burns and glows in them: with the camera in one, `applyIndoor` (04d_barrow.js) asks `late3IndoorLight`, which gives the ambient the hall's own colour and strength (`DEEP_AMB`: the cistern's cold teal, the pyres' and the pits' warm red, about one and a half times the Barrow's) and thins the fog in the great halls (0.018, the Barrow's 0.03), so the far side of a hall reads at low with its four lights (the cistern was black). **The seal**: in the south wall of the Hollow King's hall, a slab of the first kings' runes (collider tag `gate`); Use at it breaks it for the Hollow King's slayer (`LATE2.d.king` or `prog.kingKills`) at level 45 (`late3SealReady`; else 'Read the seal' says why: `late3SealWhy`); it sinks into the floor and stays open to the character (saved). **The cistern** (`deepFloodStep`): past its middle the sluices burst (once in 150 s), the water rises from 0.4 m in the basin to 0.75 m over the walkways in 16 s, holds 40 s and drains in 24; `late3WaterAt` answers `waterAt` (01b_water.js) there, so bodies wade, swim (no spell, no shot), a fire on them goes out and it can be drunk (07b_swim.js lets the deep through); two drowned rise with it. **The pitch** (`DEEP.cells`: 119 cells of 2 m along the channels of the Hall of Pyres and the Ash Throne, each with its neighbours along its run and where runs cross): lit by `late3FireAt` (asked by `fireLandsAt` under the Barrow: a fire spell or a burning arrow of anyone's), a pyre-keeper's Kindle (a 2 s spell at the pitch by its foe: break it) or the lord's Word; a cell climbs to full heat in 1.2 s, lights its neighbours from half heat, burns 12 s, dies down in 3 s and lies charred 45 s before the pitch seeps back (`DEEP_FIRE`); whoever stands in it (not the cinder-thralls or their king) takes 4.5% of its health at full heat each half second; real flames (`addFire`, untimed, let go when the cell goes out) on every other burning cell within 50 m of the camera, 24 at most. **The slabs** (`DEEP.slabs`, `deepSlabStep`): a gallery slab stood on 1.5 s cracks (shaking, embers through its cracks, an `aoeMarker`), falls 1.1 s later; the lord's stamp cracks the slabs of his hall nearest his foe (1.9 s); a meteor or a leap strike cracks one at once (`late3Impact`, asked by `natureImpact` under the Barrow). A falling slab drops whoever stood on it (`deepFall`, `deepFallStep`: a fall of 2.8 m, harm by the height as a ladder's fall, the embers 3% a half second, then a scramble up the pit's side, body action 14, onto the nearest firm ground; the player's place set each step after its own movement, an NPC's `fixedY`); its cells are no ground till it rises again (a gallery slab 40 s later with nobody near, the hall's when the lord resets or falls). **The cracked wall**: three blows with Use (body action 8) or a heavy blow bring it down to rubble (saved), and a forgotten tomb with a chest lies beyond. **The dead** (`MOBS`: `cinder` thralls (their blows set you alight, the pitch does not burn them), `drowned` (a hand that roots a foe in the water), `gravehound` (the wolf's rig, bone-pale), `pyrekeeper` (an ember bolt and the Kindle); `DEEP_PACKS`, one a hall and two thralls at the throne, `baseLevel` 21-22 so they stand at w+1 to w+2 with `barrowBoost`; `late3MobThink`: the Barrow's own think (`thinkBarrowMob`, the flow field), a pack's wake, each kind's move; back in 7 minutes with nobody near). **Vorlach the Ash-Crowned** (`DEEP_LORD`; role `dungeonBoss` with `deepLord`: `late3LordThink`, `late3LordDeath`, from 08_ai.js): `baseLevel` 24 (w+4: 54 at 50), the barrow-king's might times 3.4 and 1.0 harm, a hundredth more health for each rank of veterancy (to 30), 5 m/s (6 in his fury), a reach of about 6 m; asleep on his throne until you come into his hall; a cleave (1.3 s, body action 8 and a marker before him: 160%, parry, shield or step out), the Ember Word (2.8 s, 2.2 in his fury, every 16-19 s: a custom cast any interrupt clears: a stun or a shield bash, a priest's Holy Fire (07c_balance5.js lets a flare and the bots' `castBreakable` through for him), a mage's storm, a blunt arrow, a mace; spoken, a ring of fire 6.5 m, the pitch within 5 m of every foe in his hall lit and 4% of his health back; broken, he reels), from two thirds the stamp (a ring of 4.2 m and the two or three slabs nearest his foe cracking) and his ash-wardens called up out of the pits, at a third his fury (20% harder, faster, the Word sooner, two more wardens); you leave his hall and after 5 s he is back on his throne whole, his slabs mended, his pitch out. His fall: a deed (`LATE2.d.deep`, the name Ashbane: the dead struck 5% harder and fire 10% softer), his hoard by the throne (three pieces at your level + 2, to 50: epic or legendary, 700-1,000 gold, grave-iron), back on his throne 15 minutes later with nobody near. **The skilled bots** step off a cracking slab, out of his cleave's and stamp's markers and out of burning pitch by the nearest way that is not burning (`late3BotHazard`, `late3FireWay`, asked by `botDodge`, 07c_balance5.js); a bow or a staff kites a giant from its own reach (`late3KiteReach`) and, under the Barrow, round the pillars, pits and burning pitch of a hall (`late3KiteWay`): two marked edits in `botMove` (07c_balance.js). **What players are told**: the herald (`late3HeraldText`, from level 40), the Chronicle's page The Deep (`chronDeep`, after The Barrow), the Aims page's tier, the tracker's aims past the path (`late3Aims`, from `late2Aims`), field notes `l3seal`, `l3deep`, `l3slab`, `l3pitch`, `l3flood`, `l3lord`, a help block and three loading tips. Sounds placed where they happen (`sfxAt`, `sfxAtE`: the seal's grind, the slabs' crack and collapse, the pitch's fire, the sluices, the lord's roar, swing, quake, the Word's roar and its breaking). Save part `char.x.deep` (`o` the seal broken, `k` his falls, `w` the wall down, `c` the chests taken and the seconds till they fill). Test hooks `__hm.deep`; `tools/tests/late3.py` |
| `10n_veteran.js` | [late3] A veteran the March can see (version 17). **The mantle of your name**: from level 40, while you wear a name (`late3MantleOk`), drawActors (13_main.js) gives the player's cape bit and the device above its emblem (`late3MantleCode`: emblem + 8 x (device + 1) in `iStyle.y`), and the people's shader (05a_rig.js, the cape's branch) draws the device in the realm's charge on the mantle's back and a gilt border down its edges and hem, before the weather and wear (so it is wet, muddy, bloodied and frayed as the rest); the Deeds page puts it away (`data-l3="mantle"`). **The standard's device**: late2StdShow (10l_late.js) gives its flag the realm + 4 x (device + 1) (`late3StdCode`), and the banners' shader (04_props.js) draws the device in a gilt border in place of the realm's arms. **Struck down**: once a second (`late3StdStep`, from `late2StdStep`) every foe of yours fighting within 2.8 m of the planted standard hews at it (7% of its might, a champion, a risen champion or a boss 18%, a lord or a warden 13%; it steadies 2% a second in a lull); spent, it falls (`late3StdFall`: the pole topples over 0.8 s, the flag lies furled on the ground in the realm's colour, `L3V_HEAP`, the log and a banner tell it, no strength about it: `late3StdDown`, asked by `late2StdStep`) until you raise it (`late3StdRaise`: 'Raise your standard', Use beside it, `late3StdOffers` from `late2Offers`). **The barding of your horse**: from veterancy 3 (`L3V_BARD`) the horse you ride, and your own tamed horse standing, wears the device of the name worn (a peak, veterancy's own, with none) in gold on each flank of its saddle cloth with a gilt band above the fringe: drawActors adds `late3BardCode` (4 x (device + 1)) to the cloth's red in the beast's `iColB`, and the beasts' shader's cloth branch (05c_beasts.js, material 10) takes it off and draws the device in the cloth's own frame (`vUV`: round the body and along it). Field notes `l3mantle`, `l3stdfall`, `l3bard`; loading tips; the Deeds page's lines (`late3MantleHTML`, `late3BardHTML`, `late3StdHTML`). Save part `char.x.vet3` (`m` the mantle worn, `f` the standard fallen; the barding follows the veterancy and the name, nothing to save). Test hooks `__hm.vet3` |
| `10o_late4.js` | [late4] The late game alive (version 18). **The risen as bodies**: a risen champion's wind-up is a body that tells its kind (`late4WindUp`, from late2ChampThink: a humanoid's overhead smash, body action 8; a bear rearing onto its hind legs, 20; a wolf or a boar crouching to spring, 22: both on the beast rig, 05c_beasts.js, their feet planted where they stand); a stun as it rears or crouches brings it down at once (`late4WindBroken`, also from `updateLate4` while a marked beast is stunned). **A second move from the rally** (`late4Second`, `LATE4_SECOND`, on a clock of its own from half its strength, `S.next3` in late2ChampThink: 12 to 15 s, 9 to 12 enraged, never within 2 s of its kind's move, and its wrath held 3 s after): a bear's maul (a ring before it, 0.8 s: 150%, the foe thrown back 3.5 m and wounded 30% for 8 s), a wolf's pounce (crouched 0.7 s with a ring under a foe 6 to 16 m off, then a leap, `e.motion` kind `leap` by `leapPlan`: 115% and a 0.8 s stun), a boar's gore rush (three rings down its line, then a charge at 15 m/s by `dashReach`: whatever stands in it 130%, a 0.6 s stun, tossed 2.5 m aside: `late4RushStep`), the dead's grave-hands (a cold ring 1.3 s under a foe within 20 m: 90% frost and rooted 2.2 s), an outlaw's fire flask (a ring 1.1 s under a foe 7 to 22 m off, the flask on its arc: 100% fire, a burn, and `fireLandsAt` with the outlaw as its caster: the grass, a roof, a tree catch), a troll's hurled boulder (a ring 1.6 s under a foe 9 to 30 m off, the boulder on its arc: 140%, a 0.8 s stun and a crater, `natureImpact` 'leap'), a wisp's lure (its light draws a foe 7 to 24 m off up to 10 m to it over the land, `dashReach`, then a ring 1.1 s where the wisp was: 110% frost and a 40% snare); every ring an `aoeMarker` with the champion's faction (the stunning ones `stun`: a skilled warrior steps out too), so the skilled bots step out; things thrown are drawn by particles (`LATE4.bolts`, `late4DrawBolts`); `late4Shove` moves a body no farther than `dashReach` lets it. **Marked risen to the eye** (`late4MarkRisen`, from late2OnSpawn and the hosts): a humanoid's look carries flag 512 (the people's shader, 05a_rig.js: embers smouldering in the seams of its mail, leather and cloth, ember eyes, an outline glowing as a coal does, the dead's in cold fire, and its weapon's glow 2.2 times as bright), a beast's second colour 4 above its green (the beasts' shader, 05c_beasts.js: `l4ris`, scars raked pale across its flanks, its coat singed dark where embers run in its veins, ember eyes and mouth, an ember rim); about each one near the camera a glow (`glowPush`, by day as by night) and embers rising (`drawLate4`, `LATE4.marked`); its name in ember on its plate, seen from 62 m (`.np.risen`, 10_ui.js, page.html). **The roaming risen** (`LATE4_HOSTS`, `LATE4.hosts`): from level 40 (`late4HostOn`) a host walks each homeland's borderlands (the Pale Herald of the Roads and his dead in Logres, Grimhowl the Moon-Hunter and his wolves in Ériu, Jarl Ormr Road-Walker and his draugr in Thule: a risen champion two above you, `l2k` 1, and three or four of its kind), along a track worked out once (`late4Route`: the homeland's borderland camps in a ring about its town, a point 17 m off each toward the town, and from each on to the next a way found by `localPath` on 2 m cells, then 4 m, then by a point between drawn in toward the town; a camp no way reaches is passed by; a homeland with no track has no host; one host's track is worked out a step at most, `LATE4.stats.routeMs`: 227 ms for the three, 24 ways, on this machine). The host is a point on its track (`H.px`, `H.pz`, `H.ri`) that goes on at 2.4 m/s while it does not fight and its bodies keep up (none more than 9 m from its place; held 25 s, the laggards are set at their places); its bodies walk to their places behind it two by two (`late4HostIdle`, from thinkMob's idle, 08_ai.js; a place off walkable ground falls back onto the track) and look about them for any body of the realms within 16 m (`late4HostAggro`: the whole host falls on it); their home (`H.home`, shared) goes with the point and stands still while they fight (the leash). Far from you (160 m: no mob thinks 170 m off) the bodies go on with the point out of sight. Its leader's own moves are a risen champion's (`late4CampOf`, `late4Adopt`: the dead it calls and the pack at its rally walk with the host, not a camp; nothing of a host is in `CAMPS`, every body's `camp` is null). Its leader brought down with your share (`late4HostKill`, from late2OnKill): the deeds `roam` and `high`, a risen champion's spoils, the news; the host walks again 900 s later (`LATE4_HOST_BACK`) where it fell. The name **Roadwarden** (`roadwarden`, three hosts; you strike the risen 4% harder, `late2HarmMult`'s `risen`, and your gear wears 5% slower; device: a tower). On the map an ember ring (`late4MapMarks`, from late2MapMarks), on the Aims page and in the tracker's aims (`late4Aims`, from late2Aims; `late4HostsHTML` on the Aims page's tier). **The veteran's standard** (`late4StdKind`, `late4StdFlag`, `late4StdTear`): its flag is the banners' kind 2 + how torn it is (04_props.js), torn by each blow struck on it (`late4StdTear`, from late3StdStep: 0.6 of the blow), mended when it is taken up (late2StdTake). Struck down (late3StdFall, 10n_veteran.js) it falls the way that is clear (`late4StdFallSide`: the side whose pole and flag would lie through less of a house, a wall, a fence, a tree, a bush or water; either when both are clear; on loading too), its head down on the ground where it lands (`late4StdFallA`: the turn from the ground's height at its foot and its head), and the flag itself lies spread on the ground by its head (`late4StdLie`: the banners' kind 3 + how torn, its hoist along the pole and its fly across the ground in loose folds, its height the ground's under every point, `l4Ground` in the banners' vertex shader, 5 cm over it and drawn 8 cm nearer the eye, since the land's drawn chunks lie a few centimetres off the height map; snow all over it; its tear read from the kind with a margin), the texels under the pole and the flag bare of grass (`late4StdCover`: the cover map raised to 255 there and given back as it was when it is raised or taken up, `L4STD.marks`; marked again if the map is rebuilt meanwhile); late3's heap of cloth is no longer shown. **The March's other veterans** (`late4MantleCode`, from drawActors, 13_main.js): a risen outlaw or troll wears a mantle with the crowned skull of the risen on its back, and a keep lord the tower of the keeps once you and the March are past 40 (the people's shader's cape and device, as yours: 05a_rig.js); the dead wear none. **A long name on a phone's frame** (`late4FrameName`, from updateHUD, 10_ui.js): on a touch screen a name longer than the frame shows (`LATE4_FRAME_CH` 22 characters) is set in a smaller letter (`.l4-long`, page.html; `LATE4.frameSmall`: "Aldric, Marshal of Logres" whole), and one longer still (`LATE4_FRAME_CH_SMALL` 25) keeps the deed whole and shortens your own before it ("Wilhe., Marshal of Logres"; a deed too long for both, the deed alone); the Character page says it whole. **The Deeds page** (`late4DeedsHTML`, from chronDeeds): how each kind winds up, the second ways, the roaming risen and where each host walks. **The deep remembers** (`late4DeepSave`, `late4DeepLoad`): its dead not yet back (by pack and kind, with the seconds left: those saved are taken out of their packs on loading and come back in their time), its slabs down (lying in their pits, their cells no ground, rising in their time), its pitch burning (with its time), charred (with the seconds to seep back) or charred where it seeped back, the cistern's water (rising, high, draining, and the seconds before its sluices can burst again). **The deep's own air** (`LATE4_AIR`, `late4AirBuf`, `late4AirStep`): three placed voices of its own on buffers made from noise and arithmetic (`l4drip`, `l4embers`, `l4hall`: water dripping into the cistern at its sluices and basin, louder as it floods; embers ticking and sighing in the gallery's trenches, louder with a slab down; the low breath of the Ash Throne's hall), each at the nearest of its sources to the listener through `sndMixAt` (its fall, pan and low-pass), on audio2's air bus (`SND.air.duck`), made at the first descent and silent out of the deep; the pitch's flames are fires (audio2's loops). Field notes `l4host` (a host near you) and `l4second` (a second move by a champion near you, `fight`), a help block, three loading tips. Save parts `world.x.roam` (each host: where its point is, its point on the track, the seconds till it walks again, its leader's health), `char.x.deep4`, `char.x.late4` (the standard's tear). Test hooks `__hm.late4`; `tools/tests/late4.py` |
| `11_audio.js` | Synthesised sound effects and ambience (Web Audio). [audio2] `sfx(name)` plays a sound where the listener is (the interface, the player's own doings) through `sfxSynth(name, t, v, o)`, which writes a sound's synth into `AUDIO.sfxBus` (a placed voice points that at its own chain while it is made: 11c_sound.js) and asks `SND_SYNTH` first; `tone`, `noiseBurst` and `brass` note when the voice being made falls silent (`AUDIO.voiceEnd`); the buses at the levels' Medium (`AUDIO_BASE`: master 0.5, effects 0.9, ambience 0.55) times `AUDIO.lvl` (Volume, Effects, Ambience); a limiter after the compressor (`AUDIO.lim`, -4 dB, 20:1: nothing reaches a speaker over -1 dBFS at any setting); `AUDIO.fx` is the effects bus itself; the old ambience (wind, rain hiss, crickets, chirps) is steered by 11c_sound.js's air once it is up (`updateAudio` returns after `sndUpdate`) |
| `11c_sound.js` | [audio2] The March heard as it is seen (version 16). **Placed sounds**: `sfxAt(name, x, y, z, o)` (y null: 1.2 m over the ground) and `sfxAtE(name, e, o, h)` ask for a sound at a place; requests wait in `SND.q` for the frame's end (`sndFlush`, from `updateAudio`), where each is weighed at the listener (`sndListener`: the player's head while the play camera follows it, else the camera, facing the camera's way): its distance by its `SND_DEF` (`ref`: full within, an inverse fall beyond by `roll`, a fade to nothing at `max`; nothing is even queued beyond `max`), the air (a low-pass from 20 kHz falling with distance), behind the head a little duller, a wall, a closed door, a roof or a hill between (`sndOcc`: 07g_walls.js `shotHit` from just short of each end with the walls' own counts swapped out, `WALLS.stats` is the tests'; and the ground every 6 m on a far line; cached half a second by place: a third as loud, low-passed to 650 Hz), a sound under the water heard from above dull (the listener under the water: 07d_dive.js's low-pass on the master). The loudest are played (`r.loud` = the sound's `lvl` x its gain; a cue x6): at most `per` of a name a frame, `gap` seconds between two at one 4 m place, at most 2 new voices a frame (1 at low and on a phone: a voice's synth and chain cost a few tenths of a millisecond under SwiftShader) and `SND.cap` at once (26 high, 20 medium, 14 low, 12 a phone), the quietest still sounding giving way to one 1.5 times louder; a far one starts `d / 343 x 0.8` s late (to 0.55 s; `o.now` for thunder, which keeps its own); `o.at` delays it, `o.vol` scales it, `o.ref` / `o.max` widen it, `o.noOcc`. A voice (`sndPlay`) is its gain, a low-pass when under 15 kHz and a stereo panner, into `SND.fxIn` (the placed sounds: they dip under a cue, `sndDuck`) or, for a cue, the effects bus; let go when silent (`sndReap`). **The modules' own sound functions** (`houseSfx`, `houseSound`, `wallSfx`, `classSfx`, `natSfx`, `giftSfx`, `anVoice`, `survSfx`, `boatSfx`) are wrapped at load (`sndAdopt`, a microtask after every module): each asks for `'<prefix>:<kind>'` at its place and its voice runs the module's own synth as if at the listener (it measures its own distance: given the listener's place), so each still sounds as it did; `houseSound`'s roar of a burning house gives way to the fire loops. **The sounds of version 16** (`SND_SYNTH`, each made here, a little different each time): `chisel`, `mallet`, `creak`, `saw` (masons, townsfolk building, scaffolds, boats), `crack`, `tiles`, `collapse` (a house battered and brought down), `timberfall` (a burh's walk or gate, a palisade, a tower falling in, burning), `beat` (a fire beater's blow: `sndBeat(e)`, two in action 21), `shout`, `warcry`, `march` (a call of fire, a band storming, a column on the march), `rubble` (stormers on a fallen tower's rubble), `oar`, `plop` (a stroke from `boatPhys`, a fish leaping), `bell`, `clash`, the beasts' and the town's voices (`chirp`, `bark`, `cluck`, `bleat`, `moo`, `howl`, `owl`, `caw`, `woodpecker`, `anvil`, `chatter`: a voice is a buzz through a vowel's formants, `sndVoiceSyn`), `stagger`, `quake` and `flap` for the late game to place (a risen champion's wind-up broken off, the ground bursting up under a foe, a planted standard's cloth in the wind: 10l_late.js), and the cues (a cue is a cue only where it matters to you, `sndMatters`: your own body, your target, or within 12 m; elsewhere it is only placed) `loose`, `incoming` (a foe's shot at you, from `spawnProjectile`: `sndOnLoose`), `flare` (07c_balance5.js), `wardbreak` (a mage's Arcane Ward worn through, from `dealDamage`'s shields: `sndShieldBroke`; and a stun taken on it), `alarmBell` (a keep of yours attacked: `sndKeepAlarm`, from `updateWar`), `alarmCue` (the war's alarm news: `sndNewsCue`, from `news`); old sounds overridden here: `swim` (its high-pass onset clicked 30 dB over the stroke) and `shock` (softer on top). **Loops** (`sndLoopsStep`, four times a second): five looping voices (three at low and on a phone) on the loudest fires near the listener (every `FIRES` entry: a torch, a hearth, a campfire, a burning roof, wall or tree, merged in cells of 7 m; `crackle`, or `roar` for a big one), each placed, panned and occluded, moved to another source only once silent. **The air** (`sndAirStep`, four times a second, eased; `sndPlaceAt`: a town, a keep's court and walls, the woods (`sndTreesNear`: its own grid of every tree), the meadows, the mountains, a lake's shore, under a roof, in a room, the Barrow): wind by exposure (height, the walls, the mountains, a storm; less under a roof and in the trees), a howl in the heights and storms, leaves in the woods (fewer bare in winter), insects on summer days in the meadows, crickets on warm nights, rain's hiss out of doors and its drumming on the roof over you, a room's door and windows open to the street letting it in (`sndHouseOpen`: the rain's hiss, the wind, the town's voices), a lake's lapping, the town's murmur by day (each town's at its own pitch, `SND_TOWN_RATE`), banners on the walls, the echo (a convolver send: the Barrow 0.45, a room 0.2, under a roof 0.1, a keep's court 0.06); birds in the trees round you, woodpeckers, owls, ravens, wolves howling at night from where they are (`sndAround`, `sndWolfHowl`); the world's voices (`sndLifeStep`, twice a second): a beast's or a townsman's voice in a while, the town's forge by day, a column on the march, a band storming, stormers on rubble, a climber's rungs knocking and creaking, boats creaking; a battle heard from afar (`sndBattleStep`: the two biggest fights 30 to 470 m off, a din toward each, its clashes and cries now and then). **Footsteps** (`sndSteps`, each frame): the player's own and, on a desk at medium and high, the six walkers nearest the ears within 12 m, a step at each half turn of the gait (`sndStep`), each on what is under it (`sndStepKind`: boards on a deck, a jetty, a scaffold, a hatch, what was built, a timber keep's walks and a house's floor; stone on a stone keep's walks and in the Barrow; snow lying; a road's grit; turf); none while riding, swimming, wading, in a boat, diving or in a motion (a ladder, a leap). Every rider's horse is heard (09b_mount.js: the hooves placed), siege engines as they are built (a mallet, a saw), rolled (a creak) and loaded and loosed, and the river from its side (`sndRiverPan`: 07b_swim.js's river sound panned toward its nearest course). The loop buffers are made in JS at the first touch (`sndBuf`: crackle, roar, lap, roofrain, murmur, battle; seeded, seamless). **A phone's speaker** (`IS_TOUCH`): the effects' bass driven into a soft clip and its partials from 200 to 700 Hz added (`sndExciter`), nothing under 90 Hz sent to the speaker. **The levels**: `SOUND_LEVELS` (Off, Low 0.5, Medium 1, High 1.4) for Volume (`master`: Off is the old Sound Off, `AUDIO.on`), Effects and Ambience (`setSoundLevel`, the settings' rows `soundSettingsHTML` / `soundSettingsWire` in 10_ui.js; saved as `settings.master`, `effects`, `ambience`, read by `soundApplySettings`). A fault in the sound never stops a frame (`sndUpdate`'s try, `sndSet` lets go of a value that is not finite). How to play's block and two tips. Test hooks `__hm.snd`; `tools/tests/audio2.py` |
| `11b_music.js` | The score: an original procedural score synthesised in Web Audio (no samples, no borrowed tunes). Each mood (title, the three homelands, frontier, battle with layers that follow the fighting, the Barrow, night) is a small generative piece: voice-led chords on weighted progressions in the mood's mode, melodies grown from motifs that are stated, sequenced, varied and cadenced, a new texture every eight bars; stingers for a level, a keep or hallow won or lost, victory and defeat. Hooks (marked [music]): `updateAudio` and `sfx` in 11_audio.js, the settings menu (10_ui.js) and save (12_save.js), `campaignVictory` (08g_campaign.js); `tools/tests/music.py` renders moods offline |

| `12c_weather2.js` | [weather2] (version 19) Weather that is real. **The systems** (`WX.cells`): fronts, showers, storms, cloud banks and mist (`WX_KINDS`: each an ellipse on the map with its half length `a` along its line and half width `b`, its cover, rain, storm and mist at full strength, how tall its cloud stands; it grows over `grow` s, holds, and dies away over `fade` s: `wxCellS`), born of each realm's climate and the season (`wxSpawnStep` every 5 to 10 s: from beyond the March upwind with the climate of the realm the wind comes over, `realmAt` of the upwind side, or over a realm by its own odds, `WEATHER_ODDS` through `seasonWeatherOdds`, `wxClimateKind`; mist only by night and at dawn, and it burns off in the sun), carried by the wind (`WX.wind`: the bearing it blows from and its speed, veering every few minutes: westerlies off Ériu most of the year, northerlies out of Thule now and then and more in winter, a calm easterly in summer; `WX.off` the air carried, which the clouds' noise rides on). Stepped in the simulation (`updateWeather2`, from `simStep`). **The weather at a place** (`weatherAt(x, z, out)`: cover, overcast, fog, raining (rain or snow falling), rain, snowing, storm, mist, temp, wet (the ground's), snow (lying), wind, kind, label; `wxFieldAt` the cells' shape without the shaders' ragged edges; quick askers `wxRainAt`, `wxPrecipAt`, `wxStormAt`, `wxSnowingAt`, `wxWetAt`, `wxOvercastAt`; the coarse grid `wxGridAt(key, x, z)`, 32 m texels over the land each half second: precip, rain, snowing, cover and the ground's wetness, which soaks where it rains and dries in the sun). A held weather (`wxHeld()`: Always clear, `WEATHER.next` past 1e6 as the tests set it, or `WX.on` false) is one weather everywhere: `weatherAt` answers `WEATHER`'s values, and the clouds are one sky of its cover. **Lightning** under the storms (`wxStrikeStep`: each storm cell's own clock; a point under its core; in the cloud now and then, `wxCloudFlash`, which lights the dome toward it, `uWxFlash`; on the ground near the player `strikeNear` (its tallest things), elsewhere on the map `natureStrike` and a bolt from the cloud base, `wxBoltVisual`, and far off only the bolt; thunder from where it was; `WX.stats.at` the last strikes). **The forecast** (`wxForecast(x, z)`: a shower, front or storm whose way the wind takes over a place within five minutes, and from where; `wxForecastText`, the war panel's time line: "Rain coming from the west"); the herald's word (`wxHeraldText`, from `openHerald` in 10_ui.js: the wind, what is coming over you and from where, and the rain, snow, storms or mist over the realms' towns); field note `w2coming`, a help block, two tips. **The clouds drawn** (`wxCloudsFrame`, from `tick` after the weather and the sky are applied): the cells nearest the camera (`WX_N` 12) to the uniforms `uWxA`/`uWxB`/`uWxC`, the fair weather's cover of each realm `uWxBase`, a held weather's `uWxHeld`; the cloud field (`WXR.field`, an RGBA8 target of 256/192/128 texels by quality, warped round the camera so it reaches the horizon: world = camera + q R / (1 - |q|), `WX_R` 1500 m, `uCloudMapP`; r the cloud's density (heaps of cumulus where the cover is thin, a broken deck, a sheet under a full cover; the shapes a warped fbm riding on `WX.off`), g how tall each heap stands (a dome over each cell's heart, storms' towers), b the rain, a the storm: `GLSL_WXFIELD`); the dome of the sky (`WXR.dome`, 384/288/224 texels of half floats by quality: each texel a direction, its elevation (pi/2)(1 - r)^1.6 so the horizon has the most texels; ray-marched from the camera through the slab from the cloud base `WX_BASE_Y` (230 m) up to 650 m above it in 14/10/7 steps, the finer shapes only where the steps are short enough to see them, lit by the sun or the moon through the field toward it, `uCloudLit`/`uCloudShade` and the sky's ambient, rain and storm darkening the base, the far clouds hazed into the horizon, and at high and medium the rain hanging under a distant cloud as a veil; rgb the clouds' light, a what they let through: `GLSL_WXMARCH`'s `wxMarch(ro, rd, jit)`), now 256/192/160 texels for the water's mirror and the northern lights; **the view's own clouds** (`wxCloudsScreen`, from `tick` once the camera is placed: the same march for each pixel of the view at a half, a third or a quarter of its size by quality, `WX_Q.scr`, into `WXR.scr`; the sky reads its own pixel there with four taps half a texel apart, `cloudScreen` in 02_render.js; the dome alone blurred a cloud over nine pixels of a 640 px view). Within the cloud its sides bulge and draw in with height (the field read a little aside by a noise of the height) and its light comes by two looks along the way to the sun or the moon (110 and 340 m: the cloud counted only where the way passes under its top), so a crown or a side toward the light is lit. The field and the view's clouds are drawn every frame at high and the field turn about at medium and low, the dome half as often again while the view has its own (`WX_Q`); neither the dome nor the view's clouds are drawn indoors. Cloud shadows (`uCloudSh`: the light's way per metre up and the shadows' strength, fading with the light's height and under an overcast already dimming the light), mist in the valleys (`uMist`: the camera's mist lying over the lowest ground about it). **The shelter map** (`WXS`, `U.uShelter`, 1 m texels of floats over the land): over each texel the highest roof, room or floor standing over it (`wxShelterBuild`: every intact house and hall under its roof's covering (0.45 m), not under a hole in it; the roofs the player built; every tower's rooms not breached, to their shelter's height; the camps' tents; every walk, gallery or deck standing 1.3 m or more over the ground, not a rampart's masonry nor a scaffold), made again when what decides it changes (`wxShelterKey`, looked at once a second: each house's state and hole, the built roofs, the towers breached, the floors standing; about 70 ms); `wxShelterY(x, z)` and `wxSheltered(x, z, y)` on the CPU. Save part `world.x.wx` (the cells, the wind, the air carried, the ground's wetness: about 2 KB; the one small part a host shares). **The wet film by place** (`wxWetUpload`: the grid's wetness to `U.uWxWet` each half second, `uWxWetOn` while live and out of the Barrow; `wetHere` in the shaders). **The realms' skies** (`wxClimateKind`'s leanings, `wxRainOut` with `WX_WETK`: Ériu wet, Logres in a lee). Test hooks `__hm.weather2` (`calm()`, `release()`, `fairSet`, `precip()`, `sites`, `TRACKS`); `tools/tests/weather2.py` |

| `13q_lod.js` | Level of detail. Terrain chunks at full, half and quarter detail by distance, always with full-detail rims (neighbours never crack; craters show at every level); far chunks drawn four at a time (`terrainBlockGeo`, rebuilt after a crater). Far tree chunks swap to the far model (`treeGeometry(kind, 1)`) and, farther, to the crown's big lobes only (`treeGeometry(kind, 2)`, beyond `TREE_FAR2_D`: 200 m on medium, 64 m on low); on medium and low the chunks round the camera are split tree by tree (`treeSplit`): their trees go into three bands per kind, one draw each (`treeBandsFill`, [motion] version 10): the full model within 60 / 36 m, the far model to `TREE_FAR2_D`, the lobes beyond, each tree culled against the view (with a margin for the camera's turn) and sorted again when the camera moves 3 m or turns 5 degrees, the quality changes or a tree falls or grows; the near band's shadows come from a copy with every near tree all round (band 3, on a layer the camera does not draw); trees the near-tree set draws in full (04c_trees.js) are left out; far chunks cast no shadow (they lie outside the shadow box). Rocks beyond reach, the far glass of towns and halls and the furrowed soil of far fields are not drawn on medium and low. People beyond `HUMAN_FAR` (90 / 60 / 38 m) go in a third crowd with the farthest model (`buildHumanoid(2)`, `crowdHumanFar`, no shadow). `updateLod` from `tick`. The phone's quality (`phoneQualityPick`: a phone starts at low, a big tablet at medium; a saved setting left on auto keeps the pick). Test hooks `__hm.lod` |
| `13s_footlock.js` | [polish] Planted feet. The walk shaders put a foot where the gait says for its phase, which keeps it planted only while the body goes straight along its facing; here each foot is followed on the CPU (`footLockStep`, from the end of `updateAnim`): when it comes down its place on the ground is kept (taken where the body is next drawn, `footLockSlot`: the player moves after its gait steps), and while it bears weight the shaders get how far that place lies from where the gait would put it, along the body and across it (metres in the body's frame). In the air the difference eases to where the coming stance should start (half of what the body's own motion will move the foot in the body's frame over a stance: a body going sideways steps out to that side), so nothing jumps. Beyond 0.42 m a planted foot gives way and is dragged (a long shove; [motion3] it takes a quick step instead, below); a jump (a teleport) plants it afresh. People's two feet and a beast's four (and the horse under a rider: `e._flH`, from `e.mountAnim`), rows of `FOOT_LOCK` (05a_rig.js: a 4 x 256 float texture; [motion3] 4 x 1024) filled each frame by `drawActors` (`footLockBegin`, `footLockSlot`, `footLockEnd`). Each foot's floor (`flFloor`: on a flight the tread, `floorTreadAt`) goes in the row's third channel as its height over the body's (a beast's less what its tilt with the slope gives it), the fourth is 2 where a foot stands on a tread (level there; [motion3] now 10, or 20 on a tread, plus half the turn that keeps a person's planted foot on its heading). The JS mirrors of the gaits (`flHumanGait`, `flBeastGait`) must agree with `HUMAN_GAIT` and `bbGait`. Test hooks `__hm.footLock`. [motion3] (version 12) Bodies within `FL_NEAR` (75 m) of the camera are followed and get a row, all of them (`FOOT_LOCK.H` 1024: version 11 held 256 a frame and the rest of a crowd walked unlocked); farther off nothing is followed (`footLockStep` returns at once, so a big battle costs less than before). Across, a stance is kept within what the leg reaches (`lo`/`hi`: in under the body 0.12 m past a person's own line or 0.85 of a beast's way to the middle, out to 0.45): a foot that will travel in comes down farther out, one that travels out as far in as it may. A stance is placed `FL_MARGIN` (1.5 cm) inside that reach, and a person's with room for the foot to stand still on the ground as it comes down and as it rises while the body moves on (`pre`, `post`: 12 and 15% of a swing). A planted person's foot is held in under the body to `FL_HOLD_IN` (0.25 m past its own line, the legs crossing, as when the body turns hard over it; the shaders' limit too). Past the hold by `FL_GIVE` (4 mm: the shaders hold a foot across only that far, so one held past it was dragged), or about to be by the next step, or beyond `FL_MAX` (0.42 m), a planted foot takes a quick step (`o.hop`: lifted `FL_HOP_H` 7 cm and set down again where the rest of the stance can be spent, over `FL_HOP_T` 0.16 s, drawn from the place it leaves on the ground, `o.hwx`, `o.hwz`) instead of being dragged (a 92-degree cut at a sprint slid it 10 cm); only past `FL_JUMP` (1.5 m: the body was set down somewhere new) is it planted afresh. A swing that leaves from a place past the hold is lifted clear at once (`clear`), and a landing place is kept within it. The two ends of a swing are places on the ground, not on the body: where the foot lifted off (`o.ax`, `o.az`: where it was last drawn, kept by `footLockSlot`) and where it will come down (`o.lwx`, `o.lwz`: where the coming stance should start, from where the body will be by then), both seen again from where the body is drawn; a person's foot goes from the one to the other over the ground (along and across, `o.k` = `_flSS(0.12, 0.88, w)`: it rises in place and comes down in place), a beast's across only (along, its own swing: the vault reads it), and it is planted where the swing held it (`o.land`). A person's planted foot keeps its own heading (`o.yw`, `o.yo`, in the fourth channel) while the body turns over it, and comes round to the body's in the air or in a quick step. A person's foot may stand on a stair's tread up to `FL_UP` (0.8 m) over the body (other floors 0.6, as before; up a steep flight a foot lands 0.5 to 0.75 m over the body, and a tread past 0.6 was passed over: the foot stood 27 cm into the riser), and its height is let up to there (0.45 before). A swinging foot's floors (`o.hT` where it will land, `o.hN` under it now and 0.12 and 0.24 m ahead for a person) are looked for in `footLockSlot`, where the body is drawn, from the body-frame places `footLockFeet` leaves (`o.lT`, `o.lN`), and the landing by where the body will be by then, its climb too (`e._flVy`): looked for a step behind and where the body was, they were a tread short up a flight at a run and the foot came up into the next riser [motion4] (version 14) What the leg cannot draw is lifted, never dragged: where the body is drawn (`footLockSlot`, after the player has moved and turned), a person's planted foot that the hip's swing cannot reach across after the lean (`flCanReach`) or that would have to turn past `FL_YAW` (0.9 rad) to keep its heading, and a quick step still in its first frame there, start a quick step at `FL_HOP_LIFT` (clear of the ground at once); a quick step rises by `flHopH` (`FL_HOP_POW` 0.35: 4.7 cm in its first frame, it was 4.0); `footLockFeet` looks for the planted place where the body's turn as well as its motion will carry it by the next step (`e._flDy`). A person's swing keeps the place it comes down on and its heading in the world from `FL_LATCH_W` (0.85) of the swing on (`o.latch`, `o.ywL`: worked out afresh each step, they swung round with a body turning 0.2 rad a frame, and the foot came in over the ground); where the leg could not reach that place the foot is held `FL_AIR_H` over the ground (`o.air`, with the gait's own lift: `flHumanLift`) and comes down by a quick step from the air, and a landing refused at touchdown is taken the same way. A quick step goes over the floors on its way: from the floor it left to the floor where it will come down, never under the floor beneath it now (on a flight it was carried at the height it left onto the next tread). A body that halts (its gait's phase stops) keeps a foot in the air where it was drawn and sets it down there (`o.frozen`; if the gait goes on, the foot swings on from where it was held). On a ladder the lock stands down (the rungs hold the feet: `ladderLegs`); a Charge's rush runs with its feet held (`rush`). While a boat is shoved off (action 19) each foot's floor is the one under it on its way into the stance (`o.dy`). A sharp cut at a sprint slid a planted foot 2 to 24 cm at one cut in five across the stride; now 0.6 cm at most in 130 cuts (`gaits.py` cuts). [motion5] (version 16) `flBeastGait` follows the longer gallop and trot (`dG`, `gp`, `gq`, the hind feet's `hb`); `footLockBegin` brings the rubble's height maps up to date (`rubHfSync`, 13y_motion5.js) and `floorTreadAt` asks `rubbleFootFloor` first: a foot on a fallen tower's or house's rubble stands on the stone drawn under it, not the ramp the body walks. [anim2] (version 19) A body set down somewhere new has its feet planted afresh where they are drawn (`A2FL.replant`); a body standing still settles a foot it cannot hold (`a2Unsettled`: off its rest place, on a floor well above or below its own, or turned off its heading; a quick step, the farther foot first, `A2FL.settle`); a planted foot reads its floor again only when the ground changes (`A2FL.ground`, `o.hEp`); its sole is sought along its own heading (`flFloor`'s `yaw`), and on the bare ground by its middle (`A2_SOLE_UP`); a row's offsets are kept within the body's own metre (`A2FL.clamp`). See Feet, deaths and weapons. |

### Conventions worth knowing

**World**
- y is up. The map is a square centred on the origin.
- Each realm sits on a bearing: Logres 150°, Ériu 270°, Thule 30°. `rp(R, along, lat)` places a point on a realm's axis, measured from the centre.
- Per realm: two keeps at `along` 118 (lateral ±64), a temple at 170, the muster at 214 and the town at 378.
- The frontier is inside `R_RING`.
- The Barrow's dungeon lives off-map at x > 1000. `heightAt`, `isWalkable` and `zoneAt` defer to its grid there.

**Materials**
- Every material is a `THREE.ShaderMaterial` made with `mat()`. All of them share the live uniforms in `U`: time, sun, fog, wetness, snow, night and so on.
- Weather and time of day therefore reach every shader through `U`. New shaders should read the same uniforms.
- [weather2] (version 19) The clouds are drawn from the weather systems (12c_weather2.js; Weather below): the sky reads the view's own clouds (`cloudScreen`), the water's mirror and the northern lights the dome (`cloudDome`), and what follows of `uCloudCover` holds only where the dome is off.
- [v18] `uCloudCover` is the cloud noise's threshold (the sky, the water's mirror and the aurora draw cloud where the noise is above it): overcast lowers it (`applyWeather`, 05e_weather.js: toward 0.04), and the sun, the moon and the stars fade by (1 - overcast) squared. It was raised toward 0.95, so the clouds thinned as rain set in and the moon shone through a storm.
- Weather on a surface goes through the `GLSL_WEATHER` chunk in `02_render.js` (`wetAlbedo`, `wetSheen`, `rivulets`, `snowAmount`, `snowAlbedo`, `snowSparkle`), called with `uWet` and `uSnowCover` scaled by how sheltered the surface is; pass `gPL` as the heat so snow melts by fires.
- Snow lies where it is cold (the seasons, `05k_seasons.js`): `uSnowCover` is the snow lying at the camera (or 0.02 when snow lies only elsewhere in view), so CPU readers (grazing, survival's cold) get the local amount; a shader that should show snow lying elsewhere multiplies it by `snowHere(wp)` from `GLSL_SEASON` (terrain, grass, trees, buildings and houses, rocks, ice do). A shader that does not still shows the camera's own snow.
- The year on a surface: `GLSL_SEASON` (02d_season.js). Turf and blades call `seasonGrass`, broadleaf foliage `seasonLeaf` and drops its cards by `seasonFallen` (bare cards show `twigCard`), flowers fade by `uSeasonC.x`; pines (`uNeedle`, `uDecid` 0) stay green and carry snow. Anything new that grows should read the same uniforms. `uRain` is the rain falling right now (rings on the water). Characters take their own amounts from the `iWear` attribute; beasts from `iColB.w` (the hit flash in the fraction, wet and snow in whole sixteenths above it: `beastWx` in `05h_wear.js`, which now soaks and dries beasts as well).
- World maps every shader can read through `GLSL_WORLD` (built on the first frame by `updateCanopy` in `03_terrain.js`, 2 m texels unless noted):
  - `uCanopy`: rgb are the meadow's patches (`meadowPatch`: dry straw, lush clover, tall stands; ground, blades and flowers all use them), alpha is the tree-crown cover (`canopyAt`). The cover follows felled, burning, leafless and regrowing trees every 1.5 s. Ground and grass under crowns stay drier in rain, gather less snow and lie in a little shade.
  - `uGroundAO` (1 m): contact shade on the ground at the foot of walls, houses, gates, fences, props and posts, baked from `COLL` (`groundAO`); [look2] its second channel the towns' footpaths (`groundPath`, 13u_look2.js).
  - Test hooks: `__hm.visual.canopy(x, z)`, `.meadow(x, z)`, `.groundAO(x, z)`, `.refresh()`.
- `meadowHeight` sets the turf height (short sward, taller stands, long in fields, trimmed by roads); flower heads ride on it. `GRASS_SEGS` gives each quality its bends per blade layer: medium and low spend their vertices on more, simpler blades.
- Fog is exponential height fog (`applyFog`): as thick as before at the camera's height, thinner up the slopes.
- The final composite grades by time of day: the `gSat` (vibrance), `gCon` (contrast about the mid tones) and `gWarm` keys in `TOD_KEYS`.
- [look] The cover map is also how trodden the ground is: under the solid threshold (0.3) a value shortens the blades and the flowers' stems (`1 - 0.72 * smoothstep(0.03, 0.27, cover)`: a town's green is 0.25, a third of the meadow's height), from 0.3 nothing grows. Anything that wants short turf writes a value under 77 of 255 (and never lowers a texel: solid stays 255); the water is covered (200) once the herbs are placed, so no blade or flower stands in it; the map's own bilinear ramp gives every wall and post a short fringe at its foot. CPU readers keep their threshold of 100 (`tillWhy`, the herbs' placement).
- [look] No blade stands on rock: blades fade out where the rock mask is 0.6 to 0.9 (they stood straight out of the cliff faces as dark spikes).
- [look] Foliage near the camera or between it and the player (`viewBlock`) parts by whole leaf cards (the near trees) and by clumps of the crown in the world (`vnoise` of the world position: the hearts and the chunk trees' lobes), never through a screen-door pattern (a 4 x 4 Bayer of dots read as dithered green blobs against the sky). [look2] The hand-over between the near and the far tree sets does the same (`GLSL_TREE_HAND`, 04_props.js: `treeNearHidden`, `treeFarHidden`): across the 3.5 m band at the near trees' reach the near tree's leaf and needle cards come in whole, card by card (by their seed), its heart and the far crown by clumps of one field in the world (`treeClumpK`: where one is drawn the other is not), and the trunk changes over at the band's middle. Only the bark's part of the parting still dithers.
- [look2] A crown drawn as the chunk trees' lobes near the camera (every crown within 30 m at low, which draws no near trees) is drawn leaf by leaf (`treeLeafAt`, `GLSL_TREE_HAND`): cells of a jittered grid on the plane the face looks along, each an elongated leaf turned its own way with its own shade and tilt, dark gaps between them, the outline broken leaf by leaf; faded out by 30 m and once a leaf would be under about three pixels. A noise of `(x + y, z + y)` of a 3D point is constant along a line: on a round lobe it streaks diagonally (the lobes' clumps were); cross two planes instead.
- [look2] Fine relief bumped through the screen's derivatives (`bumpN`) is shaded in 2 x 2 blocks, so any detail bumped that way fades before it is under about five pixels (the roads' pebbles and grit, `pebF`, `gritF` in the terrain shader: their outlines broke into a network of dark angular cracks, and the roads read as crazy paving in a phone's or a small window's view).
- [look2] Trodden ground under snow (where the road channel `A.r` says the ground is trodden: roads, plazas, paths) is packed grey slush with darker tracks along it, and the earth that shows is wet and grey; the snow takes only a fifth of what it did off a road (`rdS` in the terrain shader). The road showed through the snow as dark brown mud.
- [look] A house wall (`holedWall`, 04b_town.js) is one slab on a grid cut at every opening's edges, sills and heads: each solid cell gives its front and back faces and only the faces that are really there are closed (the openings' reveals, the wall's ends, top and foot). Built of boxes side by side it had T-junctions (a piece over a door ending on the middle of the tall piece's edge beside it; their vertex shades, linear between each box's own corners, disagreed too) and end faces inside the wall flush with the front, which won MSAA samples along the seams at high: a thin light line ran up each side of every door and window to the eaves. Anything else built of boxes side by side in one plane has the same fault.
- [look] What is drawn by distance from the camera is refreshed at once when the camera jumps more than 20 m (a journey, a release, a portal, a fixed view), not on its next tick: the forage plants (`drawForage`, every 0.4 s: an orchard's apple trees were missing and the old place's bushes drawn), the far glass of towns and halls and the fields' soil (`lodFar`, every 20 frames). The trees, the near trees, the rocks, the crags, the farm and the bands already were.
- [look] Thatch is combed down the slope: its strands are laid across the axis the face looks along (`thw` from the normal's x and z), not summed over both axes (a plaid weave on a round house's lining), and its finest strands fade by the pixel's size.
- [look5] (version 17) Something laid on the ground that a player must see in a meadow (holy ground) is told to the grass, not only drawn under it: the grass's shader reads it (02f_look5.js `uHallow`, filled once a frame from `CLS.grounds` by `look5Frame`) and lays its light over the blades, brightest at their tips; a disc drawn on the ground (05g_spells.js) lies under the blades. A spell's area that should show through tall grass goes into the decal map instead (`aoeMarker`: the blades tint by `vDecal.b`); a heavy blow that breaks the ground pounds the grass to stubble there (`natureCut`, as `late2Wrath` does), so the cracks drawn on the ground show. A disc is draped a ring of about half a metre at a time (`DISC_RINGS` 10), so by a crag its triangles bridge from the foot of the face up it: it fades on its own steep triangles (`lie`, from the screen's derivatives of its surface: 45 to 60 degrees), and a new mark drawn on the ground that should not climb faces does the same.
- [look6] (version 18) A mesh with an index of its own faces the way it is seen: a `ShaderMaterial` draws front faces only, and the deep's pitch channels (10m_deep.js `deepChannels`) were wound facing down, so from version 17 on nothing of them was drawn (the pitch, its flames running along it, its ash); only the flame sprites on every other burning cell showed. Wind a floor's quads (a, c, b) as the floors are, or look at it from above once (`look6.py pitch` counts a mesh's triangles by the way they face).
- [look6] A ring a player must see where a body stands (an `aoeMarker`'s danger ring, the target's ring) is drawn by the ground's marks (`GLSL_DECAL`: `sampleDecal`, `applyDecal`), which only the floors' shaders read (the terrain, the Barrow's and the deep's floors): a surface a body stands on that is drawn by the building shader shows none of them. The deep's slabs are drawn with `look6SlabMat` (14_look6.js: the building shader with the marks on what faces up); anything new of that kind uses it (or reads the marks itself).
- [look6] Something that moves under a body carries it: a body on a falling slab is at the higher of its own fall and the slab's top under it (`look6SlabTop(S, x, z, dt)`, 10m_deep.js), worked out from the slab's own state for the step it is in, since a body steps before its slab (from the mesh, a step late, it stood a hand over a falling slab). A body falling into a pit with its floor (the slab) fell faster than it and lay inside it once it landed.
- [look6] The deep's embers (`deepEmberMat`, what a `DeepBatch` sends there: an ember's red over blue on `MAT.rune`): a crack's colour is darker than `DEEP_EMBER`'s full red (r under 0.96) and smoulders in broken stretches, a rune is the full colour and keeps its whole glow. The deep's materials are patched by string at load (14_look6.js `look6Patch`): a change to a patched line of 10m_deep.js's shaders skips the patch (`LOOK6.missed`; look6.py fails), so change the patch with it.
- [look6] Ash (`MAT.darkstone`, 9) is not charred by the siege material (`SIEGE_FS`, 04h_siege.js: a wreck's heaps of ash were drawn as coal), and burnt timber lying open to the sky wears pale ash on what faces up, checked by the char's fissures: the char's checks fade to their mean under a pixel, and a heap of charred boards read as one black smear from a step back.
- [look6] A broken gate's hanging leaf lies swung in at `GATE_OPEN` against the passage's side, as an open leaf stands (04g_castles.js `gateWreckGeo`): it stood across half the gateway, and every band and column passing a broken gate walked through its boards. Anything that stands in a passage the war uses either has a collider and a way round it or keeps out of the passage.
- [look6] A builder's stint at the foot of a house's scaffold (04j_rubble.js `houseScafWorkSpot(H, side, k, who)`): the k-th of the clear places along its own side of the house (`look6SpotList`: its own side, then round the back to the other side; a place is clear only where the walk mask is and no collider stands, a few of many), a golden-ratio step from the last so the stints spread along the wall, and not within 0.9 m of where another builder works (`H._l6at`); version 17's turn of three gave the first clear place after the turn's own, often the same.

**Water**
- `waterAt(x, z)` gives `{ y, depth, fx, fz }` (surface, depth over the ground, flow in m/s) or null. Lakes stand at `WATER_Y`; rivers fall along their course; ponds stand in their hollows at their own heights. Use it, never `WATER_Y`, to ask about water.
- `W.walk` is 0 walkable, 1 blocked, 2 deep water. `isWalkable` stays `=== 0`; `stepTo` uses `swimPassable` for a body with `e.swimOK` (the player always; people and beasts chasing something or getting out; never townsfolk or posted guards).
- A body in water has `e.wd` (depth), `e.wadeK`, `e.swim`, `e.swimK` (0..1, for the shaders), `e.wl` (how high it is soaked). `groundY` and the player float swimmers through `waterFloorY`. The actor shaders get swimming as a negative `iAnim.w` (death stays positive) and the soaked height in whole 5 cm steps of `iWear.x` (the fraction is the wetness).
- Anything that should ring the water calls `rippleDrop(x, z, r, depth)` or `splashAt(x, z, size)`; spells that leave an AoE mark on water splash by themselves.
- Drinking: at any lake, pond or river the water module offers the drink and survival's `drinkAt(spot, kind)` does it (you drink your fill and every `waterskin_empty` becomes a `water`). Drinking a `water` from the bags, or using one in a recipe, gives back a `waterskin_empty`. Dirty gear is washed first unless you are really thirsty; with a rod and no thirst, fishing comes first.
- A mage's ice (`freezeWater`, 07b_classes.js) lies at its water's own surface (`s.wy`) as a floor; `onIce` keeps bodies on it out of the water, and swimmers caught where it forms are lifted onto it.
- Winter ice on the lakes and ponds (05k_seasons.js): `seasonIceY(x, z)` is the ice's top where it carries a body (0.3 thick or more); `floorAt`, `onIce` and `isWalkable` ask it (check `SICE.on` first, it is cheap). No splashes or leaping fish on the ice; fishing through it cuts a hole. The rivers never freeze. [water2] A hole cut in the ice (`DIVE.holes`) is open water: `seasonIceY` is null there; `seasonIceLift` leaves divers under the ice.
- [water2] Under the water: a diver has `e.dive` (`t`, `up`, `pitch`) and moves itself (09_player.js returns early through `water2Steer`); `e.swim` stays true (no casting), `updateWater` leaves its strokes and surface splashes alone. The eye under the water (`DIVE.under.on`, the camera below the surface at it) sets `U.uUnder.x`: `applyFog` then fogs anything below the surface with `underFog` and anything above it by the water its ray passes through before it leaves the water (`underFogD`; the sky does the same), and the water surface's back faces (it is double-sided now) draw the view up through it (the window, the silver beyond it, the ice from below), letting through unfogged what shows in the window (it is fogged already) and closing on the bank at the waterline. A shader that does not use `applyFog` is not fogged under the water. A body standing more than 0.1 m above the water's surface (a jetty's deck, the air) is not in the water.
- [water2] In a boat: `e.boat` (the boat), `e.seat` (the thwart: drawn seated), `waterFloorY` gives the seat (`boatSeatY`), `updateWater` skips the body, NPC passengers have `fixedY`. Boats keep off land, ice and jetties by `boatHit`. Bodies keep off boats through `boatShove` in `stepTo` (boats move, so they are not in `COLL`).

**Weather** ([weather2], version 19; 12c_weather2.js)
- The weather is each place's own: weather systems (fronts, showers, storms, cloud banks, mist) live on the map and move with the wind, and `weatherAt(x, z, out)` gives the weather at a place from the systems over it (cover, overcast, fog, raining, rain, snowing, storm, mist, temp, wet, snow, wind, kind, label). `WEATHER` (05e_weather.js) is the weather at the camera, kept for what is about the view (the sky's light, the fog, the sound, the HUD). Anything with a place of its own asks there: a body (05h_wear.js caches its rain, snow and ground once a second with its shelter), a bed (08h_farming.js), a fire (houses, a keep's timber through `wxCastleWet(C, wet0)`, an engine, a built piece, the grass's dryness `natDry(x, z)`, a brand), a pen and its beasts, a boat, the realm's gifts, the callings' rain and storm (`rainHere(e)`, `stormNow(e)`), the snow lying (`seasonLieStep`: each texel its own snowfall, rain and air), the water's rain rings, the lightning (under the storms' cells). For loops' farms and stores, net's hosts and anything new: `weatherAt` (or the quick askers `wxRainAt`, `wxPrecipAt`, `wxStormAt`, `wxSnowingAt`, `wxWetAt`, `wxGridAt`); `farmTempAt` already weighs the rain and cloud over its place (`wxTempAdj`).
- A held weather is one weather everywhere, as before version 19: Always clear (`WEATHER.mode` 'clear'), a test that sets `WEATHER.kind` with `WEATHER.next` past 1e6, or `WX.on` false. Tests that set `WEATHER.raining` and the like by hand hold it first (most already set mode 'clear' or next 1e9), or place a system (`__hm.weather2.WX`, `wxMake(kind, x, z, { age })`, `calm()` for none).
- Snow and rain stay out from under any roof: the shelter map (`U.uShelter`, `GLSL_SHELTER` in 02d_season.js: `shelterY(xz)`, `shelteredK(wp)`) is read by `snowHere` (so every shader that shows snow lying elsewhere), the ground's snow and wet film (03_terrain.js) and the drops of rain and snow; `wxSheltered(x, z, y)` on the CPU (`skyOver`, the splashes, the drifts). Anything new that roofs over ground (a new kind of building or shelter, a canopy, a bridge) joins `wxShelterBuild` and `wxShelterKey` (12c_weather2.js), or it will snow under it. A wall's inside face gathers no drift (07f_tracks.js asks).
- The clouds are the systems' own: anything that draws the sky or a mirror of it reads `cloudDome(dir)` (`GLSL_CLOUDS`, 02_render.js: rgb the clouds' light, a what they let through; the water's mirror and the northern lights do; the sky of the main view reads its own pixel of the view's clouds, `cloudScreen(dir, gl_FragCoord.xy)`, which only a shader drawn into `sceneRT` may ask), and `shadowAt`/`shadowAtV` (GLSL_SHADOW) carry the clouds' shadows (`cloudShade`, the cloud field read up the light's way; at low, which has no shadow map, the clouds' shadows alone). A shader not made with `mat()` that includes GLSL_SHADOW gets no `uCloudSh` and so no cloud shade (its strength reads 0). `uCloudCover` still thins the sky's old noise clouds only where the dome is off.
- The wet film is each place's too: the ground's wetness on the 32 x 32 grid goes to the shaders each half second (`U.uWxWet`, `wetHere(wp, w)` in `GLSL_SHELTER`, 02d_season.js: the grid's wetness at wp while the weather is live, the camera's own `w` while it is held or in the Barrow), read by the terrain (its darkening, gloss and puddles), the grass and the building shader (`WX_WET_HERE`: the houses and the built pieces define it as their own sheltered wetness, `hWet`, `pWet`, computed through `wetHere`); so the ground and the walls are wet under the rain and where it has rained, and dry beyond its edge. Other shaders (bodies, props, trees, the wear) still take the camera's `uWet` (a body's own wet is its own already, `iWear`). A new shader that shows the wet ground reads `wetHere(vW, uWet)`.
- The realms' skies (`wxClimateKind`, `WX_WETK`, `wxRainOut`; the shaders' `wxField` the same): a grey day in Ériu often rains and Logres's rain often comes only as a grey bank; a cloud's rain falls fully over Ériu and less in Logres's lee (`p * k - (1 - k) * 0.4` by the realms' weights, k 0.62 Logres, 1.1 Ériu, 0.85 Thule: a front over Logres is often a drizzle under the threshold of rain); a storm rains wherever it builds. Measured at the towns over six game hours a season (`weather2_clim.py` in the work's scratch; rain, snow or storm): Logres 7 to 9% of the time (overcast another 26 to 37%), Ériu 21 to 25%, Thule 15 to 21% (snow in winter); before, every town 16 to 22% alike (the weather crossed the March on the westerlies).
- Cost: three passes before the frame (the cloud field, 256²/192²/128²; the dome, 256²/192²/160², every frame or two at high, every four at medium and low; the view's clouds at a half, a third or a quarter of the view, 14/10/7 strides and four times that in short steps at most, every frame, at once out of the pixels below the horizon): three more draw calls; one more sampler in every shader with shadows (the cloud field) and in every one with the seasons (the shelter map). The CPU: the systems' step and a 32 x 32 grid each half second; `weatherAt` loops over the cells (a dozen at most near the March). [weather2, round 15] A whole frame drawn and the GPU drained (`weather2_ftime.py` in the work's scratch: 640x360, the camera over the Logres town looking at the sky, four frames, SwiftShader on a machine at a load of about 10), this build against version 18's main one after the other: medium in a held rain 14.3 s against 15.9, overcast 14.9 against 12.3; high 20.6 against 22.9 and 20.4 against 20.0; low 5.9 and 6.2 (main's low not reached): the clouds' passes are lost in the frame's own cost and the load's noise.

**Mountains** ([land], 03c_land.js)
- [heights] Everything is placed on version 10's ground, then the whole mountain is shaped (`mtnHeights`, 03d_heights.js): `mtnShape` (version 10) still only touches mountain texels with no walkable texel within two, so the placements in `buildWorld` (trees, rocks, camps) and after it (forage, herbs, workstations, boats, the orchard) read exactly the heights, masks and cover they did and come out where they were (the saved land names trees and plants by number). `mountains.py` checks the land before the shaping (`HTS.H0`/`walk0`) against version 9 (`tools/tests/mountains_base.json`, unchanged), and after it: what anyone could reach, the roads, camps, colliders, the trees there were and the rocks.
- What the shaping may change: heights on the mountains away from what is kept (roads and their verges, sites, camps, water, ponds' hollows, colliders, plots; a wall rising over a road or a site is shaped above its foot); the walk mask only where texels no one could reach turned too steep (blocked: about 4,600 texels on the faces and crests, of 56,600 shaped); the rock, grass and flower masks where the slopes changed; the heights of trees, rocks, plants and herbs (settled with their ground). It never blocks a texel anyone could reach, never opens a blocked one, never leaves a closed hollow on the shaped ground. Anything placed later on the mountains (a new kind of plant, a camp) should read the final ground, after `mtnHeights`; anything that must keep a placement made before it on version 10's ground goes into `htsKeep` or `objs`.
- [look] No shaped texel stands up out of all eight round it by more than 0.6 m (`HTS.despiked`, about 150 at boot, right after `htsApply`): a 2 m spike drew a smooth, sharp-faced pyramid seen from the slopes below it. Brought down to 0.6 m over the highest of them it stays the top, so no hollow forms and every slope only eases.
- The crags are placed once the shaping is done (`mtnHeights` calls `mtnPlaceCrags`; `buildWorld` no longer does), from the walk mask as it is then (`mtnFreeAgain`).
- Hardy trees are added after every tree there was (`HTS.trees0` is the first); anything that counts trees for a placement made before `mtnHeights` (forage's shade, the herbs' shade) never saw them.
- The pond fill dithers the heights it raises with a fixed hash (`hash2(k, 4111)` in 01b_water.js), not `Math.random`, so the land is the same on every boot.
- Anything new that draws rock should share the look: `landRockTone`, `landFacets`, `landStreaks` and the snow line (`landSnowLine` with `landSnowHold`) from `GLSL_LAND`.
- Cost (`perf.py`, 640x360, SwiftShader; triangles / calls, version 9 against version 10): the mountain view from the Logres orchard at low 700k / 122 against 696k / 123 (crags and reshaping, before the towers), medium 1.49M / 171 against 1.47M / 171, high 2.46M / 207 against 2.48M / 202; the keep courtyard at low 711k / 129 against 672-721k / 130 with the towers (their rooms are drawn only within 70 m). Totals move by about 60k between runs at low as the farm soil and the crowds come and go: compare the per-mesh lines, not only the totals.
- [heights] Cost of the whole mountain shaped (`perf.py render`, 640x360, SwiftShader; triangles / calls, version 10 against version 11): the one mesh that comes into new views is the crags' (`mk`: more crags, and the outcrops; +13k triangles and one draw at low in the forest view, two draws at high); the hardy trees join the chunk meshes that already draw pines or birches there (no draw added); the terrain is the same grid. At low, less the farm soil (61k and one draw, which came and went between the runs): town 652k / 104 against 644k / 105, keep 654k / 120 against 651k / 120, forest 695k / 164 against 698k / 164, the mountains from the orchard 673k / 120 against 647k / 119, river 625k / 134 against 626k / 134. Medium: keep 1.26M / 149 against 1.29M / 151, forest 1.50M / 204 against 1.50M / 204, mountains 1.44M / 166 against 1.42M / 164; high: keep 2.05M / 192 against 2.13M / 194 (more crags near the keep, and their shadows), forest 2.59M / 240 against 2.59M / 238, mountains 2.54M / 211 against 2.53M / 209.
- A pattern in a shader never multiplies a world position by something that varies across the ground, nor projects it on a direction that turns with the normal: hundreds of metres from the origin either one stripes the ground with moire a few centimetres apart (both were found up close in version 10). Warp the pattern's grid by an offset instead, and pick fixed axes (`landAlong`).

**Buildings**
- Buildings are merged geometry with a per-vertex material id (`MAT` in `04_props.js`: stone 0 … rock 15, drystone 16).
- The building shader branches on that id. To add a surface type, add an id and a shader branch.
- [look3] A scaffold is built with `look3Scaffold` (04d_look3.js): pass the standards' places along the face and the way to the wall at each, the lifts' heights, the ground (`gy`) and a `clear` test (`look3Clear`); then `look3ScaffoldWorld(W, S, [info])` makes its boards floors and its ladders climbable while `look3ScafSync(W, on)` says it stands (a scaffold made anew for each repair calls `look3ScaffoldDrop(W)` when it comes down: its floors leave `FLOOR` and its ladders `LOOK3S`). Stone, logs or anything else waiting at a scaffold's foot lie on the ground or on each other, never a step up in the air.
- [look4] A scaffold rises with the work: its standards from the start, each lift (ledgers, putlogs, boards, rail, braces and the ladder up to it) as the work comes up to it (`look4LiftStep`, 04d_look4.js; a castle section's, a tower's and a palisade gap's). A builder of a new scaffold that places things on its top lift places them on the highest lift that is up (`Math.min(lifts.length, LOOK4.lifts)`), and one that would rebuild its mesh outside look3's machinery keeps `look3ScaffoldWorld` from laying out its floors and ladders twice (`LOOK4.geoOnly`) and gives `look3Scaffold` the places its standards stood (`LOOK4.prev`, each run's `ok`): the clear test, asked again, refuses the places under the scaffold's own boards. A scaffold's ladder stands upright, its rungs `LADDER_AHEAD` in front of the line its climber climbs on and every 0.3 m from where the climb starts (`fy`: its own foot), up to a climber's reach (1.95 m) over the boards it leads to, through an opening left in the next lift's boards. A house being built back has a scaffold of its own (04j_rubble.js `houseScafLay`).
- [look5] (version 17) A house's scaffold rises with the work too (04j_rubble.js `houseScafSync`: `look5HouseLifts`, a lift up once the walls stand within 0.45 m of it, at once for a house that burnt; its mesh made with `LOOK4.lifts`, its floors and ladder on only for the lifts up, `Q.l4n`), and its builders use it (13z_look5.js: one at a time up the ladder onto the boards once the walls stand 1.1 m over the lift, the life step `scaf`). A house being built back shows no course over its eaves (houseRubbleGeo): its gables come back with its roof, and a gable's course drawn over the bare walls floated over the house as a plank.
- [look3] A crack in coursed stone is drawn with `look3Crack(uv, k)` (the stone branch's `planarUV`), one in plaster, daub or timber with `look3Craze(p, k)` (04d_look3.js), on upright faces only. A line that follows the mortar joints exactly hides in them (the joints are dark): let it cut through some stones too, and give it a lit lip.

**Body actions** (`setAct(e, id, seconds)`; the humanoid shader's `atype`): 1 one-handed strike, 2 bow draw, 3 spellcasting, 4 a flinch, 5 using something (reach, pick, drink from a skin), 6 in the air, 7 whirlwind, 8 overhead smash, 9 leap strike, 10 guard, 11 parry, 12 kneel (07b_classes.js), 13 down on the haunches to reach the ground (picking, drinking at a lake; 09s_survival.js; [motion5] each foot where it stands, the legs reaching it wholly as the hips sink; a body falling from more than 0.9 m lands in it, 04m_ladders.js), 14 climbing a ladder (hand over hand, its cycle locked to the body's height: 04l_towers.js; [motion4] on the rungs' own cycle, the phase set by `towerLadderStep` to 2 pi for every 0.6 m from the ladder's foot, each foot on a rung and each hand round one: `ladderLegs`, `ladderHands`; [look2] what the hands carried hangs on the back meanwhile, in the shader: the shield over the cloak, a blade, mace or axe across it from the right shoulder, a staff across it, a bow over the quiver), 15 swimming under the water (in the swim block of the shader; the fraction is the body's lean, -1.2 rising .. 1.2 head down; 07d_dive.js), 16 at the oars (in the seated block; the fraction is the stroke; 07e_boats.js; [motion4] the hands on the grips where boatsDraw has the oars: `armIK` and the shoulder's swing, `uaLy`), 17 a game bird in the air (09v_birds.js: its progress is the wings' spread; birds only), 18 a blow from a ladder (held on the rungs as in 14, the right arm drawn back and cutting; 04m_ladders.js; [look2] the weapon in the right hand, the shield and the bow on the back), 19 shoving a boat off the shore (07e_boats.js: leaning in with both hands on the gunwale, the back leg driving, both feet flat; [polish]; [motion5] the hands on her gunwale by her end and following her down the beach for her first 0.3 m, the body bent as low as her gunwale lies: its height and her keel's offset come packed in the action's value, `motion5ActValue`), 21 beating out flames (04g_blaze.js: braced on bent knees and bent toward the fire, both arms swung up over the head and brought down hard in front, twice an action; what the hands carried slung on the back as on a ladder; [siege3]; [look4] a fire beater in the right fist, a wet leather flap on an ash pole, the part bit `WB.beater` set by drawActors while the action lasts), 20 a risen bear rearing for its blow (beasts only, [late4], 05c_beasts.js: it rises onto its hind legs over 0.3 of the action (the body turned 1.08 rad up about the hind legs' tops, `rearA`; the hind legs' swing undoes it so they stand where they stood, the hind paws kept flat, the hips sinking 0.1 of the hind leg), paws the air with its forelegs in turn and roars with its head brought down to its foe, and crashes down onto its forepaws by 0.89, where they stood: the wrath lands at 0.9), 22 a risen wolf or boar crouching to spring (beasts only, [late4]: forequarters low (pitch 0.17), the body lowered 0.24 of the front leg, haunches bunched, head low and forward, a quiver, all four feet planted (the IK reaches the ground under the lowered body); it springs at 0.84 to 0.92 as its blow lands; a wolf's pounce and a boar's gore rush crouch first too), 23 hammering at a wall ([motion5]: the builders at a house's scaffold, 08f_townlife.js, and the masons, 13v_look3.js: the left hand braced on the wall, the right raising a mallet over the shoulder and bringing it down onto the wall before the chest at about 1.35 m, once in 1.05 s, the feet standing; what the hands carried slung on the back as on a ladder; a mallet in the right fist, `WB.hammer` (bit 22), while `e._hamUntil` is ahead: the work steps refresh it; the blow lands `HAMMER_REACH` before the body). Actions 7 and up own the whole body. Take the next free number for a new one.

**Characters**
- Characters are instanced crowds. The per-instance attributes are in `HUMAN_ATTRS`: `iPos`, `iAnim`, `iColA`, `iColB`, `iMisc`, `iStyle`. A person's `iPos.w` is the yaw plus whole turns that carry the floor's slope and the lean into a turn ([motion], `humanSlopeYaw`: n = slope steps + 41 x lean steps); `humanVS` takes them off (`yawR`) before its sine and cosine, so anything new that reads a person's `iPos.w` must do the same. A wild or farm beast's `iPos.w` carries whole turns for its lean (`beastLeanYaw`), taken off in `beastVS`; [polish] and the slope of the floor along it: k = lean steps (0.04 rad, -5..5) + 11 x slope steps (0.05 of rise a metre, -20..20, eased in `e._bslope`; within 70 m of the camera), and the horse under a rider the same, which the rider's shader reads too; game birds and hens get the plain yaw. People are drawn by three crowds by distance: `crowdHuman` (near, `HUMAN_LOD`), `crowdHumanLo` and `crowdHumanFar` (beyond `HUMAN_FAR`, 13q_lod.js).
- [look] A body in a room is lit by the room: the people's fragment shader includes `GLSL_ROOFS` and sets `gRoom` (declared in `GLSL_ACTOR_LIGHT`, 0 by default) from `underRoof(vW)`: no direct sun or moon, the sky's ambient at 0.6, no sky in `env`, and a warm fill (stronger at night). `underRoof` knows the 8 roofs nearest the camera (houses, built roofs, the towers' rooms: `houseRoofsForRain`), so a body in a far house is lit as before. A beast's shader leaves `gRoom` at 0.
- [look] Cloth over the legs (the bits `robe`, `tabard` and `skirt`, below the hips, not on the arms) is pushed out ahead of a leg that has come forward and behind one that has gone back (`humanVS`, after the legs' skinning: the leg's line at the vertex's height from `thL`/`thR` and the knees, plus 0.1 m, a tabard 0.125 so it stays over the robe), weighted by how near the vertex is to that leg across the body. The middle of a robe follows neither thigh, so a striding or guarding leg came through it from the hip to the boot. A new garment over the legs should carry one of these bits, and a layer further out more room. [v18] It hangs from the leg: at each height the cloth clears the farthest the leg reaches forward or back at that height or above it (hip, the thigh and the shin where they cross that height, the knee, the ankle and heel: below a raised foot it hangs straight down from it), falling away 2 m a metre to either side of the leg (a tent of cloth, not a spike over the leg alone), and only within the cloth's slack (a robe 0.24 m, a skirt 0.12, a tabard 0.1): past it the leg lifts the cloth instead (the hem rides up the shin, at most 0.35 m). The leg's line was extended below the knee to any depth (the tangent of the shin's angle, to 3.6), so at a run the hem under a raised knee went 2.9 m out ahead and behind (`hem_probe`: a robe's hem from what the shader draws, the body's frame; 0.68 m at 7 m/s now, a tabard 1.39 m then and 0.45 now, the neighbouring hem points 19 times their rest spacing then and 3.4 now). A robe's skirts below the knee follow the thigh at 0.35 of their old weight (05a_rig.js's robe: turned rigidly with it, the hem swung 0.6 m out at its sides), and its hem stays on the floor's side of the slope along the body (`slopeK`: a runner's bob and a kneel took it 7 cm into the ground).
- [polish] `iStyle.z` is 'female' (0 or 1) plus twice the body's row of planted feet (`FOOT_LOCK`, 13s_footlock.js: 0 is none; [motion3] up to 1024 rows); `humanVS` reads `mod(iStyle.z, 2.0)` for 'female'.
