- For performance ([perf2]): nothing new is drawn but what the spells draw (two discs and some particles a blow, one ring a rally) and, while a standard is planted, its pole (one small mesh of 72 triangles drawn with the building shader: no program of its own; one draw and its shadow's; its flag is one more instance of the banners' cloth); the watcher looks four times a second at a few lists (the keeps, the relics, the campaign's last record, the nine risen camps); the risen are the camps' own bodies (the camps keep their counts, and a rally adds two that stay till they fall).
- Camps that rise: `late2Band(camp)` gives `spawnMob` the band (a camp that does not rise keeps its own `lmin`/`lmax` and its champion one above); a camp's members carry `l2off` (their place in the band) and its champion `l2risen`; when a camp rises or falls back (`late2Rescale`, from `rescaleWar`) its bodies are taken away (`removeEnt`, marked dead first) and new ones spawned. Anything that walks `CAMPS` should expect the nine farthest to change their bodies past 40.

**The deep and the veteran** ([late3], version 17; 10m_deep.js, 10n_veteran.js, 04_l3device.js)
- The Barrow's grid grew south (`DUN.GH` 84: the old halls' cells, their rooms and every saved index unchanged). A cell of a room with `deep` set (`late3IsDeepCell`) is the deep's: `buildDungeon` leaves its walls, headers, roofs and floor to 10m_deep.js (`deepShell`, `deepFloor`), which builds them from the grid, so a new hall down there is a room in `DEEP_ROOMS` (its `u`, `v`, `fy`, `h`), its cells in `late3Grid` if they are not flat, and its lights in `DUN.lights`. The deep is drawn only while you are in it or in the Hollow King's hall (`DEEP.root.visible`): anything new of it goes under `DEEP.root`.
- The deep's chests (`DEEP.chests`: the drowned coffer, the pyre-keeper's chest, the forgotten tomb's, the hoard) are also in `DUN.chests`, the Barrow's one list of chests: Use offers them (09_player.js), `updateChests` swings their lids and the maps mark them (10_ui.js), and `openChest` hands them to `late3OpenChest`. `initBarrow` (08e_barrow.js) sets up the Barrow's own two and then calls `late3Init`: until the fix after version 17 it called `late3Init` first and then emptied the list, so no chest of the deep could be opened in play (the tests opened them by calling `late3OpenChest`; `late3.py only=chests` now opens each by Use). Whatever empties or rebuilds `DUN.chests` must keep the deep's. A chest that waits on something sets `ready` (the hoard on its lord's fall, the tomb's on its wall: `deepWallShow`); while not ready it is neither offered nor marked.
- Cell type 4 is open ground drawn by a mesh of its own (a slab): walkable, its floor the cell's `fy`. A slab that falls sets its cells to 0 (no ground) until it rises; a body on it is taken by `deepFall` (`e.l3fall`: its own motion, which sets the body's place each step after its movement, so the player's own steering does nothing while it lasts) and never left standing in the rock. Its pit is drawn by its own mesh too: the grid has no floor under a fallen slab, and `dunFloorAt`'s bilinear blend at a fallen slab's edge would sink a body standing beside it (the cells keep their `fy` for that reason).
- Under the Barrow (x > 1000) `waterAt` asks `late3WaterAt` (the cistern only: bodies wade and swim there, a fire on them goes out, and it can be drunk: 07b_swim.js's `updateWater` and `waterOffers` let the deep through), `fireLandsAt` asks `late3FireAt` (the pitch: anyone's fire lights it, the caster is no matter) and `natureImpact` asks `late3Impact` (a meteor or a leap strike breaks a slab or the cracked wall). Nothing else of the land acts down there (no grass, no craters, no weather), as before.
- A new hall of the deep gets its light in `DEEP_AMB` (its ambient's colour, before the low quality's 1.5) as well as its fires and lamps in `DUN.lights`: at low only four point lights are drawn, so a great hall with no ambient of its own is black past its nearest fire.
- The deep's dead are the Barrow's (`spawnBarrowMob`; `dunPack` 100 + the pack's index, `e.deep`, `e.deepPack`; `baseLevel` + `barrowBoost()`), so everything that asks `isUndead` holds for them: a priest's holy light strikes them 1.6 times as hard (07b_classes.js), as it does the Barrow's. Their own moves are in `late3MobThink` (from 08_ai.js's think, after `thinkBarrowMob`); the lord's in `late3LordThink`.
- The lord's spells and the pyre-keepers' Kindle are custom casts (`e.casting = { id, custom: true, t, total }`), advanced by their own think and broken by anything that clears `casting` (a stun, `breakCast`, a parry's stun). 07c_balance5.js's `holyFlare` and `castBreakable` let a body with `deepLord` through (the role `dungeonBoss` alone is never flared, so the Hollow King keeps his rule); a new boss whose spell a priest should flare needs the same.
- The skilled bots see the deep's dangers through `late3BotHazard` (asked by `botDodge`, 07c_balance5.js): a cracking slab under them, a marker of the lord's cleave or stamp (`aoeMarker` with the lord's faction), burning pitch. A new danger a bot should step out of goes there or makes an `aoeMarker`.
- The device of a name: `L3_DEVICE_OF[deed]` (04_l3device.js). A new deed's names get a device there (else crossed blades); a new shader that draws it includes `L3_DEVICE_GLSL` and calls `l3DeviceMask(p, k)` (p in the device's own square, about -0.75 to 0.75, y up).
- The mantle: the player's `iStyle.y` is the emblem + 8 x (device + 1) while the mantle is worn (`late3MantleCode`, from drawActors), and the cape's bit is set; the people's shader reads `mdev = floor((vStyle.y + 0.5) / 8)` and the realm's emblem as what is left. Anything else that puts a value in `iStyle.y` must keep it under 8 or the people's shader takes it for a device. The standard's flag: the banners' `aB1.z` is the realm + 4 x (device + 1) (`late3StdCode`); a banner with `aB1.z` under 4 is drawn as before. The barding: a beast's `iColB.r` is the cloth's red + 4 x (device + 1) for the player's horse (`late3BardCode`); the beasts' shader reads it only in the cloth's branch (material 10), so a beast's second colour must stay under 4 in its red (every one is a colour under 1).
- The standard struck down: `L3V.std` (its strength `hp` 0..1, `fallen`, how far it has toppled `k`); `late2StdStep` asks `late3StdDown()` before it gives anyone strength, and calls `late3StdStep` once a second, where every foe fighting within `L3V_STD.reach` of it strikes it; `late3StdFall(by)` fells it and `late3StdRaise()` raises it (Use beside it). A new way to harm it goes through `L3V.std.hp` and `late3StdFall`.

**The late game alive** ([late4], version 18; 10o_late4.js)
- A risen champion's wind-up goes through `late4WindUp` (a humanoid 8, a bear 20, a wolf or a boar 22); a new kind of risen beast gets its own there (and its pose in the beasts' shader's action chain, 05c_beasts.js, where every turn of the body is undone along the legs: a rear turns the body about the hind legs' tops by `rearA` and the hind legs' swing undoes it (`hindPush`), the hind paws kept flat (`lowA += rearA`), a crouch lowers the body by `bob` and pitches it, which the legs' targets undo). Anything that interrupts a wind-up for a beast sends the action on to its descent (`late4WindBroken`), so the body comes down at once and not after the action's time.
- A body action a beast's pose reaches for must keep its feet where the lock holds them: no swing of a leg (`frontReach`) or tilt of a paw while the foot is near the ground (they are faded in by `smoothstep` of the rear as the body rises), and the body's own turns and drops undone along the leg (`tg`'s chain in the leg block). `late4.py motion` measures each foot frame by frame from what the shaders draw; a beast that fought or walked just before walks its feet back under it for a while (the lock's quick steps): measure a calm one (`T4.champ(type, realm, true)` spawns it afresh).
- A risen champion's second move is in `late4Second` (by `LATE4_SECOND[mobType]`), on its clock from the rally (`S.next3`, late2ChampThink). Every new move of a foe that a careful player should step out of makes an `aoeMarker` with the foe's faction (and `stun: true, src` when it stuns: balance8's rule sends a skilled warrior out of it too), a ring on the ground (`spellDisc`) and a word over the champion near you (`uiFloatAt`); things thrown are particles on an arc (`late4Throw`), not projectiles; a body moved by a move goes through `late4Shove` (`dashReach`: no farther than the land and what stands on it let it).
- A risen body is marked by `late4MarkRisen(e)` (its look and `LATE4.marked`). The people's shader reads the risen in flag bit 512 of `iColB.w` (with the glow kind in bits 4 to 6, the dead's 2 for cold fire); nothing else may set that bit. The beasts' shader reads it as 4 above the second colour's green (`l4ris`, then `fur2` is the colour: every use of the second colour in the beasts' fragment shader reads `fur2`, never `vFur2`); a beast's second colour stays under 4 in its green (and its red under 4: the barding's). The farm beasts' and the birds' shaders are built from the same fragment shader and never carry it.
- The roaming hosts are not camps: their bodies' `camp` is null, `e.l4host` their host, `e.home` the host's own (moving) home. Anything that walks `CAMPS` does not meet them; code that reaches a body's camp for the risen's moves asks `late4CampOf(e)` and gives a body spawned for a host to it with `late4Adopt(camp, m)` (a stand-in camp, `camp.l4host`, is what `spawnMob` gets). A host's leader is `l2risen` and `properName`, so late2ChampThink gives it the wrath, its kind's move, the rally and the second move. Far from you (no mob thinks 170 m off: updateNPCs) a host's bodies go with its point; a new system that moves bodies with no one to see them does the same rather than leaving them behind.
- The hosts keep off the measures (`late4Measuring`, asked by `late4HostOn`): no host walks while the player is played by a bot (`P.bot`: balance8.py, barrow.py), while any body of the measures stands (`e.balance`: classes.py's and duels.py's arenas lie on the homelands' ring where the hosts walk, and a host passes within 17 m of every borderland camp, the risen camps among them), or while a test sets `LATE4.off`; a host taken off the land walks again from where its point was once they are gone. A new test that fights in the borderlands at 40 and more with neither sets `LATE4.off` (or expects a host to come by).
- A standard struck down lies on the land, not on a floor: the flag's height is the ground's (`l4Ground`, the banners' vertex shader: the height map, `uHeightTex`, read by `texelFetch`), 5 cm over it and drawn 8 cm nearer the eye (the land is drawn in chunks that lie a few centimetres off the height map); anything else a shader lays on the land from the height map wants the same. A value packed into a varying's whole part and its fraction (the banners' kind and tear) is read with a margin, `fract(v + 0.002)`: a constant 3 comes out of the interpolation as 2.9999998 here and there (a fallen flag read fully torn in specks). `late4StdFallSide` keeps its pole and flag off what stands about it. The cover map's texels under it are raised to 255 and given back (`late4StdCover`, `late4StdUncover`: only those still 255); anything else that lies on the land for a while and should keep the grass out does the same and gives the texels back.
- The deep's state that is saved (`char.x.deep4`): `DEEP_PACKS[i].respawn` (each `{ at, spec: [type, lvl, u, v] }`), `DEEP.slabs[i].st` (3, lying in the pit, with `t` since it fell), `DEEP.cells[i]` (`st`, `t`, `heat`, `ch`, `rearm`), `DEEP.flood` (`st`, `t`, `next`) and `DEEP.wy`. A new thing of the deep that changes for longer than a minute goes there, sanitised by its index and its kind.
- The deep's air is three placed voices (`LATE4_AIR`: each with its sources in the deep's grid, `[u, v]`, its `ref`, `max` and level). A new sound of a place that lasts goes there with a buffer made once (`late4AirBuf`: seconds of sound that loop without a seam, normalised), placed through `sndMixAt` (no distance test of its own).

**The season** ([loops], version 19; 08m_realm.js, 08n_season.js)
- The war is a season of weeks (`RSM.days`, 42): the muster (a sixth), the war, the reckoning (two days). The live campaign of 20 to 60 minutes is a battle within it: in the muster its captures are skirmishes (they go back at its end, as before: no keep falls in the season), in the war a keep taken in the field is taken in the season (`realmSimLive`) and stays its taker's when the battle ends (`seasonKeepStays`); a battle won counts season points. Anything new that changes who holds a keep, a hallow or a store for longer than a battle tells RS (`realmSimLive`, `realmSimContribute`).
- RS is plain JSON: never put a function, a class or a reference to a body in it, and keep it small (about 11 KB; under 200 KB). Anything new in it is defaulted in `realmSimInit`, read back in `realmSimSanitize` (by its type and range: a field it does not know is dropped) and bumps `RSM_V` only if an old state cannot be read into the new.
- The page copies its stores into RS before each step and back after (`seasonCopyIn`, `seasonCopyOut`): RS's goods 0 to 6 are 08m_loops.js's `LOOPS_R` in order; gold is RS's alone (the treasury). While the page is open (`RS.live`) RS does not make or eat (08m_loops.js does), fight or move armies; its works draw on the stores above a reserve of half the target.
- **For net (the server)**: load `src/08m_realm.js` as it is (`require` gives the contract). One state for the March: `realmSimInit(seed, { days, keeps: [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2], names: { realms, keeps }, t0: Date.now() })`, then `realmSimStep(RS, seconds)` on a clock (a minute's step costs microseconds: 42 days by 60 s steps take about a second), `realmSimContribute` for each player's delivery (`kind` a good of `RSM_GOODS`, `'gold'` or `'work'` hours; `who` a name: `R.by` keeps the 40 who gave most), `realmSimOrder` for votes and officers' orders (`who.rank`: realm rank, 5 and up an officer), `realmSimSummary(RS, realm, since)` for a returning player (`since`: their last `RS.t`), `realmSimSanitize` for anything received. The page's own copy is `world.x.realm` (`{ rs, real }`); a shared March would send the server's RS to the page in its place and leave `RS.live` to the page (true while a player is in it: the page's live war then reports keeps taken through `realmSimLive`). The shape: `{ v, seed, rs, n (season), t (s into it), len, nextLen (the next season's length, 0 the same), phase ('muster'|'war'|'reckon'), winner, t0, live, ln (log lines ever), names: { realms[3], keeps[] }, realms[3]: { s[8] (stores, RSM_GOODS order), bank[8] (goods brought for the works), lev (soldiers under arms), sp (season points), del, work, proj { walls, granary, yard, smithy, engines }, act (the project at work), prog (0..1), votes { id: weight }, aim (an officer's keep, -1), short [goods], hungry (h), by { name: points }, raidAt, decideAt, levyAt, refillAt, stats }, keeps[6]: { h (holder), home, g (garrison), tier (walls 0..3), gate (0..1), siege { a (army id), t } }, hallows[3] (in whose temple), hallowAt[3], armies[]: { id, r, n, n0, kind ('raid'|'hallow'|'assault'|'offensive'), k (keep), q (realm raided), eng, p (0..1 on the road), len (m), state ('march'|'siege'), t0, siegeH, hungry, arm }, nextArmy, offs[]: { r, k, at, ann, state ('planned'|'live'|'siege'|'done'), army, res, liveUntil }, log[80]: { t, r (-1 all), k ('news'|'big'|'proj'), x (text) }, past[12]: { n, w, sp[3], keeps[], end }, stats }`.
- The real time away is capped at three weeks (`SEASONP.maxAway`); a season's war cannot be lost in a night: a realm behind works up to a third harder and its walls stand that much stronger (`RSM.catchUp`), the others turn on the leader, offensives are announced two days ahead (the defenders raise the walls of the keep named first), and a keep lost is always worth an army to win it back.

**The realms' stores** ([loops], version 19; 08m_loops.js)
- Anything new of the war that a realm makes or mends should be paid for from its stores: a lump drawn at once with `loopsTake(realm, need)` (it takes all or nothing and returns the share it had; `part` takes what there is) or `loopsKeepTake(K, need)` for a keep's, and a job that lasts with `loopsWork(K, kind, dt, T)` (its goods drawn over its time, `LT.work[kind]`; returns the pace, `LT.slow` without them). What it does without its goods must show in the field (fewer, thinner, slower, hungrier) and be said once in a while (`loopsSay(realm, key, text)`: the news, once in three minutes a key). Never stop a thing the stall guards watch outright: a band with no engine goes for the gate, a gate without timber is mended at a third of the pace, a column too thin still marches with two.
- Anything new that the land gives a realm goes in with `loopsAdd(realm, good, n)` (the town's) or `loopsKeepAdd(K, good, n)`; a good the player can carry that a store should take gets its place in `LOOPS_WORTH` (`[store, units each]`).
- The hungry and ill-armed marks (`e.lHungry`, `e.lIll`: times) are set only on the war's own bodies (soldiers, guards, lords); the player, the bots and the beasts are never marked, so the callings' measures (`classes.py`, `duels.py`, `balance8.py`) and `loot.py` are untouched. A test that wants version 18's war sets `__hm.loops.LOOPS.on = false`.
- Carts are entities with roles of their own (`carter`, `escort`, `carthorse`: updateNPCs hands them to 08m_loops.js) and a mesh of their own while near the camera; they are not warbands (no order, no stall guard), so `campaign_soak.py`'s band watcher never sees them. A carter and its escort are of their realm (the other realms' bands fall on them); the horse is neutral.
- **For net (multiplayer)**: the realm's stores are one world save part with a plain shape, `world.x.loops` = `{ v: 1, r: [[food, timber, stone, iron, hides, wool, horses] for each realm], k: [[food, timber, stone, iron] for each keep], c: [[realm, food, timber, stone, iron] for each cart in flight] }` (integers); a shared March would keep `r` and `k` on the server, add each player's deliveries to them (`loopsDeliver`) and send them back; everything else (the carts' bodies, the yards' stacks, the workers) is made from them. The player's own record is the char part `char.x.loops` (`u` units, `n` deliveries, `e` escorts, `x` raids, `rp`, `g`).

**Townsfolk's ways** (version 10)
- Out of doors a townsman or farmer who stops getting nearer the work asks `localPath(ax, az, bx, bz)` (08f_townlife.js): A* on a 1 m grid over the colliders within the box round both ends (doors open for townsfolk, so they are no wall), smoothed to a few waypoints; a sidestep is the fallback when there is no way. Indoors `houseRoute` does the same round the furniture. [v15] `localPath(ax, az, bx, bz, pad, maxSpan, gates, cs)`: `cs` is the cells' size in metres (1 by default); on a finer grid (a narrow way: 0.25) a sight line in the smoothing keeps a cell clear on either side, so the way stays as dense as the cells in a narrow part and does not cut a corner (a body cut one straight into the wall beyond it and was held there); the span is in metres either way, so a fine grid wants a short one (48 m: 37k cells).
- Companions (08h_animals.js): a straight way counts as clear only over ground the body can walk (or swim) as well as past colliders and paddocks (`anSegClear`), else the trail, then `localPath`, then a sidestep. One that makes no headway for 3.5 s out of sight (8 s in sight), or is held fast 5 s, comes back in a few metres behind you on your trail, or at its waiting spot by you when the trail is far behind (`anCatchUpSpot`), never at a stale trail point.
- A town's fisher (07e_boats.js) is a villager within 110 m of the jetty's foot; it leaves its house by the door first and walks with the time the walk needs (`boatWalkPlan`; a `go` step's `T` is its time in seconds, else 16, or 28 after a sidestep).
- A fire with `wall` set (the towers' torches) lights a brand but cooks nothing (`fireNear` skips it). Collider circles with `jetty` set are the jetties' posts (07e_boats.js), which the land's checks leave out.

**Farming**
- A bed's slots are 0.6 m apart; `slotPos(P, s)` is where a plant stands; `plotAt(x, z)`, `plotLocal`/`plotWorld` convert to the bed's furrows (u across, v along).
- Beds and strips go into the cover map (`farmCoverAll` at the end of `buildCoverMask`), so no grass grows through the soil; removing a bed rebuilds the cover map.
- Growth is stepped every half second in `updateFarming` (`FARM.speed` speeds it for tests); drawing refills the instances twice a second, when the camera moves 3 m or when `FARM.drawDirty` is set.
- The town fields are `W.fieldRects` (01_world.js): Brackenford's, then the gardens of Ériu and Thule (`realm`, `garden`, narrower `stripW`/`gap`; placed after the towns are built, clear of the houses with a clear walk from the plaza, and kept free of camps), so the saved strips keep their order. Apples hang on the trees only from late summer through autumn (`forageShown` asks the season), the trees blossom in spring. A garden strip has its town in `P.stand.town` and its rotation in `P.rotList` (`FARM_GARDEN_ROT`). No tree grows in a field: a tree that would is placed off its edge, keeping its index.

**Saves**
- [guide] `char.lore.pv`: the path's version the save was made with (1 when missing). `loreOnStart` takes the early steps added since quietly for a character past them; a step added later needs `pv` set to the new `PATH_VERSION`.
- Old saves must always keep loading.
- When you add fields, default them in `startGame` / `validSave` and include them in `coreKey`.
- [late4] World part `roam` (each roaming host: where its point is on its track, its point's index, the seconds till one brought down walks again, its leader's health; a host's bodies are not saved, it walks out again from its point) and char parts `deep4` (the Deep Barrow as it lay: its dead not yet back, its slabs down, its pitch burning or charred, the cistern's water) and `late4` (the standard's tear). An old save with none: the hosts start at their tracks' beginnings, the deep as new, the standard whole.
- [war2] World part `gates`: the keeps' and temples' broken gates (rammed, battered or burnt down: a burnt one lies charred), with the seconds since they broke; on loading they lie broken and are rebuilt by the war's own rule (a broken gate came back whole on loading).
- [weather2] World part `wx` (12c_weather2.js): the weather systems (kind, place, line, size, age, life, speed, rain), the wind and where it is turning, the air carried, and the ground's wetness on the 32 x 32 grid (about 2 KB); an older save has none (a few systems are seeded at their ages on the first step). The shelter map is not saved (made from what stands).
- [war3] World part `war3`: the pact (against whom, its age), the presses and the rallies (each realm's named keep), and the keeps newly taken (age, by whom) while the war lasts; a column, a band's hold and the gate's mending are not saved (the bands are not), and a keep taken loads with the garrison the war's own load gives it.
- [war4] World part `war4`: `{ g: [...] }`, each keep's gate being hung, its work in hundredths (0 for none); read back, the work goes on from there when it begins again (`t0`). A column, a relief, the masons at a gate and a pact's truce are not saved (the pact itself is war3's).
- [water2] World parts `dive` (the finds taken, with the seconds until they come back) and `boats` (each boat away from its berth: where, its state, its char). [polish] World part `tracks` (the prints still showing near the player, capped at 320; see 07f_tracks.js).
- [look5] World part `masons` (13z_look5.js): for each scaffold with masons at work, `[castle, section or -1, palisade gap or -1, one up on the boards]`; read back, the masons come back at their work once the scaffold stands (`LOOK5.masonLoad`, `look5MasonsInPlace`). An older save has none (they come out of the hall as before).
- [siege3] World part `blaze` (the burhs' walks' and the timber hallow's ring's cells that are not whole, and burning gates). A gate burnt down comes back whole on loading, as a broken one does (the doors are not saved).
- [loops] (the season) World part `realm` (`{ rs: RS, real: ms }`: the season's whole state and when it was written; read back it is stepped on by the real time since, at most three weeks) and character part `season` (`p` season points given, `g` gold, `v` votes, `n` deliveries). An older save has neither: a fresh season begins at its muster.
- [loops] World part `loops` (the realms' and the keeps' stores, the carts in flight: see The realms' stores) and character part `loops` (the player's deliveries, escorts and raids). An older save has neither: the stores begin at 0.8 of their targets, the keeps' at theirs.
- [late3] Character parts `deep` (the seal broken `o`, the Ash-Crowned's falls `k`, the cracked wall down `w`, the deep's chests taken with the seconds until they fill again `c`) and `vet3` (the mantle worn `m`, the standard fallen `f`). An old save has neither: the seal whole, the mantle worn, the standard standing. The deep's dead, its slabs, its pitch and its water are not saved (a reload finds them as new).
- New systems keep their state in save parts (`registerSavePart`, 06d_goods.js): `s.char.x[key]` with the character, `s.world.x[key]` with the world; `load` gets `undefined` for an older save and must sanitise whatever it reads; `key` says what counts as a change worth writing.
- `coreKey` counts the land by what changed in it (`landKey`: felled trees, logs, craters, tiles, piles, house and wall states), never by its clocks, so regrowth alone does not cause writes. `char.gift` holds the realm ultimate's cooldown and is no reason to write either.
- A busy land (four trees down, a grass fire, five craters, three houses and three walls changed) adds about 10 KB; an untouched world adds 7 bytes.

**Sound** ([audio2], version 16; 11c_sound.js)
- A sound that happens at a place is asked for there: `sfxAt(name, x, y, z, o)` or `sfxAtE(name, e, o, h)` (h: metres up the body, by its scale). It is faded by distance, panned by its bearing from the camera, low-passed by the air and by a wall, a closed door, a roof or a hill between (`shotHit`), muffled from under the water, and left out beyond its `max` or when louder ones fill the frame (a few new voices a frame, a cap at once). Do not test the distance yourself before asking (the old `if (near) sfx(...)`): ask, and the engine decides. `sfx(name)` is for the interface and the player's own doings (a click, a level, a potion, the player's own swing may go either way).
- A new sound: its synth in `SND_SYNTH` (11c_sound.js: `(t, v, o) => { ... }` built from `tone`, `noiseBurst`, `brass`, `sndToneF`, `sndVoiceSyn`, `sndRing`, writing into `AUDIO.sfxBus`), a little different each time (`R_(a, b)`), and its reach in `SND_DEF` (`ref`, `max`, `lvl`: how loud it is at its source, which decides what is played when the frame is full; `per`, `gap`, `roll`; `cue: true` for what a player must hear over the rest: it is never capped and the rest dips under it). Short (a few seconds at most), no click (`audio2.py levels` checks every sound: a peak within 22 dB of its loudest 50 ms; the onset of a `'highpass'` noise burst clicked in one sound), not loud and all highs, and not only bass: on a phone's speaker nothing under 300 Hz is heard (the check: under 9 dB lost with a 300 Hz high-pass and the phone's harmonics). Render it offline (`__hm.snd.render(name, { at, seed })`) and read its numbers rather than trusting an ear.
- A cue only where it matters to you: something a player must hear when it is about them and not across a battle (a spell flared, a ward broken) passes `{ cue: sndMatters(e) }` (your body, your target or within 12 m); elsewhere it is an ordinary placed sound. A new kind of floor tells `sndStepKind` what it is (boards or stone) for the footsteps on it.
- A module with its own sound function (`xxxSfx(kind, x, z)` that measured its own distance from the camera) is wrapped by `sndAdopt` in 11c_sound.js: add it to the microtask there with how its place is given; its synth then runs as if at the listener. New code should not add such functions: ask `sfxAt` with a new name.
- Something that sounds while it lasts (a fire, a forge, a mill) is a loop, not a stream of one-shots: fires are found in `FIRES` already (`sndLoopsStep`); a new kind of continuous source adds candidates there with its own buffer (`sndBuf`: made in JS once, seamless, at the first touch).
- The places' air reads `sndPlaceAt` (town, keep, walls, forest, meadow, mountain, shore, roof, room, barrow): a new kind of place adds its measure there and its layer in `sndAirInit`/`sndAirStep` (a gain eased with `lerpK`, on `SND.air.duck`, which dips under a cue).
- The settings' sound rows are `SOUND_ROWS` (Volume, Effects, Ambience; Music is 11b_music.js's own); the levels multiply `AUDIO_BASE`; saved as `settings.master`, `effects`, `ambience` (0 to 1.4; an old save keeps Medium; Volume Off is the old `settings.sound` false).
- Cost (`audio2.py cost` and `perf.py low views=town,battle js audio`, against version 15's main on the same machine, at a load of 12 to 14 on 2 CPUs): see Phones and performance.

**Phones and performance** (version 9)
- Budgets: low about 700k triangles and 160 draw calls at most in every view of `perf.py`, medium about 1.6 million; high may spend more but nothing wasteful. Measure with `perf.py` before and after. [perf2] `perf.py budget` fails a run with a view over its budget (`BUDGET`: low 770k and 176 calls, medium 1.76 million and 240, high 2.9 million and 290: a tenth over the aims, so a view whose bodies come and go with the war does not fail one run in three); its views now take in the newest systems (`siege`: a Thule burh on fire stormed by a band of ten, its garrison at the fires; `townfire`: three houses of the Logres town burning, their crews at them; `rubble`: a house in rubble and one behind its scaffold; `masons`: a breached tower mended by the masons).
- A mesh taken out at runtime uses `removeFromParent()`: after its first frame it lives in the outdoor group (`regroupOutdoors`), so `scene.remove` misses it (grass rebuilt on a quality change was drawn twice over until version 9).
- Anything instanced gets a draw radius per quality and, if it is many, a far model; low has no shadow map at all.
- Far work: bodies more than 40 m from the camera are weathered every third step (`updateWear`); townsfolk and the town's and the wild's beasts more than 90 m from the player think every other step with two steps' time (`updateNPCs`). New per-body systems follow the same pattern (`let dt = dt0` per body).
- Where things stood and stand (`perf.py`, 640x360, SwiftShader; triangles / draw calls per frame, main and shadow pass; "before" is version 8, whose grass rebuilt on a quality change stayed drawn: the stale share is in brackets):

Under SwiftShader a frame's JS time is mostly first-use shader compiles (`getProgramInfoLog` in a profile), not steady work. Boot: about 23 s to ready here (the shader compile in "Lighting the sky" is the biggest step, then "Raising the keeps"); the JS heap after boot is about 180-190 MB.

From this version `perf.py` measures the deep's views after every other view at every quality (they move the war on by about 16 s: the views above ground at the next quality met another war than version 17's runs did; in this work's run, measured that way, the keep at medium drew 251 calls against version 17's 204, not looked into: measure both builds the same way before reading anything into it).
- [perf2] (version 16) The March on a phone, measured as a whole (`tools/tests/perf2.py`, 13x_perf2.js). What holds a page's memory: the JS heap is small (26-31 MB after the boot, 39 MB after an hour of war); the ArrayBuffers are the bulk (180 MB after the boot in version 15), and most of them were three.js's CPU copies of geometry already on the GPU (the houses 40 MB, the keeps and temples 11, the towers' rooms 8.6, the castles 7.3, the Barrow 6.8) and the wrecks of things that had not fallen (every tower's rubble, every curtain's breach: 11 MB); the GPU at low 52 MB of buffers, 24 MB of textures and 1 MB of renderbuffers after a minute (at high the shadow map and the MSAA targets add 45 MB). Rules from it:
  - A mesh built once and moved only by uniforms lets go of its arrays once it is on the GPU (`perf2Release(geo)`; add it to `perf2ReleaseStatic`). Never release a geometry anything reads or rewrites later (the terrain, which craters rewrite; the towers' moving parts; anything instanced; banners; the farm's soil), nor dispose of a released one (three.js would send it again from its arrays); a lost WebGL context reloads the page for the same reason.
  - Something shown only after an event (a wreck, a heap, rubble) is made when first shown (`perf2LazyMesh(() => geometry, material)`, hidden until then), not at the boot; its maker must give the same geometry whenever it is called (seeded, from the state at the boot). Never `Object.defineProperty` over a property an object already has (three.js's `visible`, `geometry`): V8 moves the object's properties into a dictionary, and every walk over the scene reads it slowly (`node`'s `%HasFastProperties` shows it); an accessor belongs on a class's prototype.
  - Geometries with the same grid share one index (`TERRAIN_IDX`, `TERRAIN_LOD_IDX`), 16-bit where the vertices allow.
  - A mesh taken away for good drops its shadow proxies (`shadowDrop(mesh)`, 02_render.js): a palisade gap's wreck and scaffold stayed in the shadow scene, holding their geometry, a gap at a time.
  - Nothing reads the layout in the frame after writing to the HUD (the minimap's size comes from a ResizeObserver: `clientWidth` every third frame laid the page out each time); a style set each frame is compared first (`s._p`).
  - Work a step does for every body allocates nothing: no closure a body (the separation loop is written out), no Set a query (`collidersNear` stamps the colliders it takes: `c._cq`), no fresh lists (the spatial grid's cells keep theirs: `SGRID_USED`); a mesh moved part by part sends only the moved part (`addUpdateRange`, the towers' doors and lids).
  - Batch (04_props.js) and HouseBatch (04e_houses.js) gather into typed arrays grown by doubling (JS arrays of doubles held twice the bytes and were copied twice); their `pos`, `nrm`, `col`, `mat`, `ao` and `idx` are views of what is filled (towerParts reads them). `perf2.py geohash` checks the merged meshes come out byte for byte as before.
  - The boot asks for the shaders once the screen is sized (`perf2Compile(false)` after `resize()`), draws the map while the GPU's process compiles them, and waits for them with the veil counting (`perf2Shaders`, where KHR_parallel_shader_compile tells whether a program is ready without waiting); `renderer.compile` prepares every material in the scene, hidden or not (the Barrow, a tower's rooms, the crowds' far models), and the shadow pass's are asked for once the title is up (`perf2Compile(true)`). A sync call to the GL between the compile and the first frame (a canvas resize, `readPixels`, `getParameter`) waits for every shader asked for: compile after `resize()`. What is made after the boot still compiles at its first sight (3 programs at the game's start, those of a quality switch, a siege engine's charring material, a fire's own): ask for a new material's program at the moment it is made (`renderer.compile` on a scene holding it) if it would stall a fight.
