The touch controls' own cost, on that slowed CPU: a move of the stick 0.019 ms, of a camera drag 0.004 ms, a tap that picks what is under the finger 0.135 ms, and the style and layout after 200 moves of the stick 0.4 ms: nothing to a frame.
  - An hour of AI-only war (`perf2.py long`, on this work's first build): the JS heap 27.8 MB at its start, 34.7 at the tenth minute, 36.7 at the twentieth and 39.3 at the sixtieth (2.6 MB from the twentieth minute on), the ArrayBuffers 123 to 138 MB, the GPU's buffers 52 to 66 MB, the scene 718 to 798 objects, the renderer's geometries 290 to 429 and programs 84 to 88 (most in the first ten minutes: engines, scaffolds, rubble and fires shown for the first time), no error and nothing non-finite; the shadow scene's proxies went 415 to 501, which is how the palisade gaps' leak was found (`shadowDrop`). Twenty minutes on the final build: the JS heap 27.9, 35.6 and 36.8 MB at 0, 10 and 20 minutes, the ArrayBuffers 121.3, 122.0 and 122.8 MB, the scene 718, 796 and 770 objects, the geometries 291, 390 and 413, programs 85, 88 and 87, the shadow's proxies 415, 457 and 437 (they follow the engines in the field: 0, 4 and 1), the animals 71 to 95 (the towns' herds filling their pens: 22 a pen at most), no error. The wrecks made at their first sight in those twenty minutes: 21 (3.3 MB), 30 ms in all, the costliest 6.6 ms of its step (`__hm.perf2.mem()`: `made`, `makeMs`, `makeMax`); of the 70 static geometries 34 had been drawn and let go of their arrays (43 MB), the rest (38.5 MB: the towns and keeps not seen, the Barrow, the towers' rooms) keep them until they are.
  - The worst steps and frames (`perf2.py views` under load 10 to 14, the systems of each step over 40 ms and of each frame over 60 ms named; both builds alike): a soldier's think of 40 to 90 ms now and then (a band's leader finding its way round, `bandLeaderDetour`: `localPath`'s A* on a 1 m grid up to 76 m across, an array made at each push, and when that finds nothing a second on a quarter-metre grid; the CPU profile puts 46 ms of 8 s simulated there in the town view), a posted guard's of 46 to 110 ms (`thinkPosted`, in a battle), the castles' step once 134 ms (`updateCastles`, not traced; the wrecks made at a first sight cost 7 ms at most), the callings' step of 25 ms; the first frame in a place new to the camera up to half a second (11 to 20 MB of geometry sent to the GPU, the HUD, the farm and the forage drawn for the first time), the frame after it 85 to 105 ms in `updateHUD`; the test boots at a desk's quality and switches to low, and the first frame after the switch links 3 programs (made with the switch, after the boot's compile; a phone boots at low).
- [audio2] (version 16) The sound's cost, for whoever weighs a frame's budget (perf2): it runs only once a gesture has started the AudioContext (`perf.py ... audio` clicks first; without it updateAudio does nothing, as in every test that does not click). Measured with `audio2.py nooffline only=cost` (120 frames of `updateAudio` after `simulate(1/30)` each, a town by day and beside a fight of 32), version 15's main and this branch by turns on the same machine (four builders' runs on 2 CPUs), the mean a frame and the worst frame: main a town 0.53 ms (45) and 1.55 (180), beside the fight 2.96 (205) and 0.56 (24); this branch a town 0.22 (6) and 0.58 (29), beside the fight 1.17 (29) and 1.10 (45), with 291 to 294 sounds asked and 72 to 74 played in the 120 frames, 73 to 75 wall tests. Main's means are its score's (a mood change makes a burst of voices: its worst frames); this branch adds about half a millisecond a frame beside a big fight (a voice is a dozen nodes and their links, 0.3 to 1 ms each here, most of it Web Audio's node creation, which waits on the audio thread's lock on a loaded machine), and little in a town. A frame makes at most 2 new voices (1 at low and on a phone) and holds 26, 20 or 14 (12 a phone); the loops (5, or 3) and the air are steady nodes, eased four times a second; a wall test (`shotHit`) per voice played within 110 m and per loop, cached half a second (0.02 to 0.07 ms each). The loops' buffers are made at the first touch on the title (about 150 ms here, once), as is the trees' grid. The first frame's start-up is in `perf.py low views=town,battle js audio` (its six measured frames: main 28 ms of updateAudio each, this branch 9.7, both mostly the score's and the voices' first nodes). Memory: six mono buffers of 3 to 4.5 s at 22 kHz (about 2 MB), one convolver of 1.7 s (1.1 on a phone or at low).
- [war3] (version 17) The war's thinking and drawing at its worst: `localPath` (08f_townlife.js) keeps its A*'s arrays between calls (`LP`: a typed heap of (f, cell), stamps for the costs and the closed set instead of a fill a call, the walk mask read a texel at a time, and a box collider's cells looked at only within its own padded bounds inside its circle's square: a wall's circle took in 120 by 120 cells on the quarter-metre grid), and the same ways come out (240 seeded queries about every keep, temple, muster and town, a quarter of them on the quarter-metre grid, run on version 16's build given a test hook and on this one: all 240 the same; their time, the first pass 611 ms against 390, each call's least of five 94 ms against 57 in all, the quarter-metre grid's 69 against 42, on a machine shared with three other builders); one band leader's way round a step at most (`war3PathToken`); `pickTarget` (08_ai.js) asks whether it can reach and see a foe of the nearest first, only until three are found (the same three come out). A siege engine farther than `W3_ENG_FAR` (36, 55, 85 m by quality) from the camera is drawn as one merged mesh of its frame, uprights, wheels and drum (made once a kind and realm: `w3Merge`) with its arm, counterweight or log, its ropes, slings and stones left out (`war3EngineLod`, from `siegePose`): two or three draws and their shadows' instead of nine to twelve (an intact engine only: a wreck or a burning engine keeps its own pose).
- The HUD: a new panel joins `HUD_ORDER` and `HUD_PREF` in `10p_hud.js` (and `HUD_COMPACT` / `HUD_HIDE` with a `.hl-compact` rule if it can shrink or wait). Touch controls are 40 px at least. Safe areas: `--safe-t`, `--safe-b`, `--safe-l`, `--safe-r` (the HUD sits inside the left and right ones).
- [look5] (version 17) The layout pass reads the panels' sizes only when one has changed: a ResizeObserver and a MutationObserver (`hudWatch`, `HUDL5`) mark it dirty (a size changed by a pixel or more, a panel shown or hidden, the zone's name fading in, a banner or a pad button added; the pass's own `hl-*` classes left out), and a pass runs then, when something asks for one (`HUDL.k = 0`, as before) or once in 5 s besides (`hudKey` read every panel's size four times a second, and the pass ran once a second whatever happened). A new panel joins `HUD_WATCH` through `HUD_ORDER`; one that changes its place without changing its size or showing (a class that moves it) adds its class changes to what the MutationObserver watches. A panel in the columns that loses a line keeps its taller place for `HUD_HOLD_T` (6) s (`hudHeld`, `HUD_HOLD`), so the panels under it stay put; it gives the room back when its hold runs out (`HUDL5.wake`). On an upright phone the path tracker comes straight after the target frame (`HUD_ORDER_TALL`) and may take the right column or the bottom's middle before it waits: with the plant card and the companion bar up it waited out of sight.
- [look6] (version 18) A field note that does not fit whole on a small phone (360x640, or one on its side) may show its title and its first two lines (`hl-brief`, 10p_hud.js; "Field note · tap to read": 83 px tall and 223 wide at 360x640, where the title alone is 49 by 126) before its title alone (`hl-compact`), but on the phones measured that never fits (55 px free between the frames and the class panel at 360x640: `guide.py` prints which a note took); a tap on either reads it whole on the field notes' page (10c_lore.js). `hl-*` classes are the pass's own: the MutationObserver leaves them out.
- On a desk the layout pass stacks the bottom: the hotbar, the class panel over it, the builder's bar (while open) over both, and the prompt and cast bar lifted over the builder's bar; the log keeps its corner, narrows beside them, or rises (112 px tall) over them, and waits (`.hl-off`) when there is no room; panels in `HUD_HIDE` wait on a desk too when nothing is free. The zone's name keeps its place while it fades.

**The capture build** ([capture], 14_capture.js)
- A new shot: an entry in `CAP_SHOTS` (`id`, `name`, `line`, `tod`, `season`, `weather`, `dur`, `pre`, `need`, `set`). `set` stages the scene with the world's own functions (what a player could do, or the war could) and returns the camera: `{ keys: [capKey(x, y, z, tx, ty, tz, fov)] }` for a path, `{ follow: { id, ox, oy, oz, ly, lz, k } }` or `{ orbit: { x, y, z, r, h, a, w } }`, and an `act(t, dt)` if something must be moved each step (bodies driven along a lane). Bodies it makes go in `CAPTURE.made` (they go when the next shot is staged); where the player must be for the scene to live (a camp thinks only with the player near, the deep is drawn only with the player in it), `capPlayerTo` it (hidden, no one's foe). Look at it with `tools/film.py look shots=<id> q=low w=640 h=360` before filming it. A shot that a character's progress gates (the deep, the risen, the standard) says why in `need`, and never changes that progress itself (film.py and capture.py give their character what the shots need).
- What runs the world while a shot is staged is `capRun(sec)`, never `__hm.simulate`: simulate runs the particles' clock ahead of the frames' (see Gotchas), capRun keeps `renderTime` with it.
- Code that reads the player's place to decide what to draw or think goes on working in capture mode (the player is still there, hidden); code that would show it, or let a foe find it, asks `e.capHide` (drawActors and isEnemy do).
- A new input in the game that should do nothing while capture is on needs nothing: capture takes the keys and the canvas's pointers in the capture phase and stops them. A new HUD panel is hidden with `#hud`; anything drawn in the world for the player alone (a marker, a ring) should ask `CAPTURE.on`.

**What players are told** ([guide], version 13; 10c_lore.js and 10e_guide.js)
- [gearstats] What a stat does is said where it shows: the kit's sums and a piece's card (10g_gearstats.js `GEAR_STAT_INFO`), the Character page and the Gear page. A new stat needs its line in `GEAR_STAT_INFO` and in `gsWhat` with its own numbers as the game reckons them (read them from what `setupStats` and `computeDamage` do, never from memory). The kit's card is sticky at the foot of the sheet: a new thing in the kit that shows a card keeps its target above it with `gsReveal`.
- A new system's first-time word is a field note: `Object.assign(FIELD_NOTES, { id: { t, x: (R) => text, fight?, ok? } })` and a watch `GUIDE_WATCH.id = (P, ctx) => bool` (`ctx.prompt` is what the E prompt says now); `loreNote(id)` queues one from anywhere. A note shows once per character, one at a time, never over a window, never in a fight unless `fight: true`, never before the first-steps note, and only while `ok()` holds; text short enough for a phone (about 40 words), the device's own words (`IS_TOUCH ? 'Use' : 'E'`). Prefer a note to a `uiToast(..., 'hint')`: a toast is for what is happening now (move to stop, the grass under you burns).
- Its help: a function returning HTML pushed to `GUIDE_HELP` (10e_guide.js), in the order a player meets it. Its Chronicle page: `chronAdd(key, label, group, fn, after)` (groups `land`, `you`, `war`, `life`); a section of an existing page: push a function to `CHRON_EXTRA.sieges`, `.gear` or `.goals` (siege engines, palisades and burning towers belong on Sieges). Its tips: `LOADING_TIPS.push(...)`. A deed worth a reward: a step in `PATH_STEPS` with `lv`, `pv` (the new `PATH_VERSION`), `old` if an old character past it should have it quietly, a hint, a reward, its event in `loreWatch`, and its place in `guideMarkOf`.
- Field notes and toasts live in `#banners`. While a field note shows, the HUD's layout places it on an upright phone right after the target frame and the class panel, and the path tracker right after it (`HUD_ORDER_NOTE`; on a phone on its side the note right after the target frame, `HUD_ORDER_NOTE_WIDE`): a note lasts seconds, the panels that stay (the companion bar, the war panel; sideways the class panel too) make room, shrink or wait for it; a toast alone keeps its old place after them (`HUD_ORDER`), so the panels you reach for do not jump at every toast; and a new banner is laid out in the frame it appears (`HUDL.k = 0`), so a note is always on the screen and never lies over a panel (placed after the class panel and the companion bar, most notes shrank to their titles on an upright phone): when the lane will not fit, the older banners wait (`hl-old`) and the newest shows; when even that will not fit (a 360x640 phone, a 667x375 one on its side) it shrinks to its title (`#banners` is in `HUD_COMPACT`: "Field note · tap" over its title), and a tap on it opens your path in the Chronicle, where every note seen is kept, the newest first. On a phone on its side a note is 300 px wide, beside the frames. The menu's Resume and New character stay at the foot of the sheet (sticky), and How to play folds each system's block under its heading (`guideFold`).
- [war2] (version 15) New things a player meets that nothing tells them of yet (for the guide: a field note, a line on the Chronicle's Fire and land and Sieges pages, a loading tip): townsfolk run to a burning house and beat it out, and **Use beside a burning house's walls beats the flames down** ('Beat out the flames', the same prompt as on a burh's walls; desk and touch); a house saved stands black under its eaves for a few minutes, and the log says "The people of <town> have beaten out the fire."; a fire that has taken the whole roof is past saving. The war's news has a new reason for a march ("marches on <keep> through the breach in its walls": a second band sent to a keep with a breach open) and a new way in ("<band> goes in by the gap burnt in the log wall of the Hall of the Ring!", the phase word 'going in by the gap'): a gap burnt in the Thule hallow's log ring is a way in once Thule has lost a keep, and the hallow may be taken while it is open. A band waits by a fallen tower until it is strong enough for the garrison it will meet (half again its number), or a second band comes, or a minute has passed. The long war's news says a hold on the March counts for more the longer the war lasts (a claim grows up to 1.6 times as fast from 15 to 40 minutes: the claim's countdown on the war panel follows it). A broken gate is kept with the world (a player who saves at a burnt-down gate finds it so). A new campaign begins with every keep's garrison whole. Soldiers no longer stand about on the walls, in towers' rooms or in a fallen tower's rubble after a fight, nor walk into walls: a band always gets on with its order or fights (the war panel's orders move).
- [war3] (version 17, 08k_war3.js) What the war panel, the map and the herald now say (for whoever lays them out: look5 has the map's names and the War page): the war panel's claims show a claim built on three keeps with its clock ("holds 3 keeps", the clock at a third of the pace) or "held" (three keeps, not more than every other realm: it does not fade), and under them one line (`war3HudLine`, `.cw-w3`, a realm's colour at its left edge): the pact ("Ériu and Thule in common cause against Logres") when your realm is in it or its mark, else a press ("Logres presses for a fourth keep: Kestrel Hold"), else a keep of yours newly taken ("Kestrel Hold: garrison 3/6 · column on the march · gate down"), else a pact elsewhere. The map rings a keep pressed for (or rallied to) in the presser's colour, a dashed ring turning and a sword badge to its upper left (`war3MapMarks`, from `drawCampaignMap` after the routes); a column is a band like any other there (its route, a shield badge, "Garrison" and the keep in the side panel's list; the player may give it another order, and it is then a band like any other). The herald's war text has a paragraph "The war now" (`war3HeraldText`: presses, the pact, a claim close to winning, keeps of yours newly taken with their guards, column and gate). The Chronicle's War page has a section "Holding what you take" (`war3ChronHTML`, three paragraphs: holding, pressing and the pact, the peace). The news cries the column, the press (and that the owners see it coming), the pact and its end, the rally of a realm down to one keep, the column taking its posts, and the peace's mending. Field notes `keepheld` (your realm took a keep near you) and `presses` (a press or a pact), a help block, two loading tips. The rule's texts elsewhere (the path's hint, the Aims page, the guide's tips: "four of the six keeps for five minutes") stay true: three keeps only build the claim more slowly.
- [war4] (version 18, 08l_war4.js) What players now meet (for whoever lays it out or looks at it: look6 has the gate's scaffold and the columns): a broken gate stands broken until the keep has been quiet ten seconds, then a scaffold goes up over the gateway on its court side, two masons come out of the hall to it (one at its foot, one up on its boards), two guards hang the new leaves below, the leaves rise board by board standing open, and about seventy seconds of quiet later the gate is hung whole and shuts; the news says "The masons of <keep> put up a scaffold in the gateway to hang a new gate." and "<keep> has hung a new gate."; the war panel's line for a keep of yours newly taken says "new gate 40%" instead of "gate down" while it is hung; field note `gatemend` (a gate being hung within 60 m). While a gate is down and foes are about, the court's two front guards stand in its mouth. A keep thinned to half its garrison sends for a column: "<realm>'s column for <keep> marches from <keep or the muster> to fill the posts of <keep>" (an order like a band's, on the map); every column says where it marches from (the nearest keep, out of its hall, or the muster), in the news and the side panel's order. A pact is cried with "...neither will march on the other nor fall on the other's bands in the field..." and its end with "...rivals again, and their bands in the field are foes once more."; while it holds, the player cannot strike the ally's soldiers either (they are not foes). A claim full before the twentieth minute of a campaign is cried ("...the elders hear no claim before the twentieth minute of a campaign: hold on until then") and its clock on the war panel runs to the twentieth minute. The peace hands the keeps back at its start, and their garrisons march in. The Chronicle's War page has a section "Gates, garrisons and pacts" (inside war3's, `war4ChronHTML`), a help block and three tips. The rule's texts elsewhere ("four of the six keeps for five minutes") stay true.
- [guide2] (version 15, 10f_guide2.js) A Chronicle page is written so it folds on a phone (`chronFold`): a lead paragraph first, then `<h3>` sections (each folds under its heading), cards (`.card`, folded under their head and first paragraph when tall) or tiers (a `<div>` whose first child is an `<h4>`); a figure stays open (it is a summary); what the page says of now and its links go at its end with the classes `now`, `acts`, `tide`, `live`, `fineprint` or `skills` (they stay open); `data-cf-open` on an `<h3>` or a tier opens it by default; a long run before the first section takes its title from `G2_INTRO[page]`. Text in a closed fold is still in the page (`textContent`), so tests that read a page keep working; a test that taps inside a page scrolls the control into view first.
- [loops] (version 19, 08m_loops.js) The realm's stores: the Chronicle's Stores page (under The war, after Orders: each realm's stores as bars, what the war draws, the carts, your part, the peace's trade, your keeps' stores), the war panel's line (`.loops-hud` under war3's: who is short of what, yours first, at most two), the war table's word (a log line when you use your realm's), the news (a realm's granaries low and its bands thin, no timber for an engine, empty stables, a keep with no bread, a garrison hungry, a cart taken, a yard set alight, the border fairs), field notes `lstores` (by the quartermaster), `lcart` (a cart of yours near), `lshort` (your realm short of food, timber, stone or iron, from level 8), a help block, three tips, and two path steps (`deliver` at level 6, `caravan` at 16; `PATH_VERSION` 3: an older character past 12 or 25 has them quietly). The quartermaster stands by each town's square (a merchant-role body); the stores dialog is the shared `#dialog` with one Give button a store (`data-lgive`) and one a horse (`data-lhorse`). Heavy packs are said once in two minutes as a hint toast and in the bags' goods list.
- [guide2] A note id is one module's: `G2_NOTES` adds its notes only where the id is free (an `Object.assign` with an id already taken replaced the portal stones' note in this work's first build). A deed done at no place (a step whose place `guideMarkOf` cannot give) gets a pointer: `g2Pointer(step)` names the button that does it (it glows, `.g2-point`) and what to say in the tracker. The war panel ends with your aim (`guideWarAimHTML`). Prefer a field note to a hint toast for anything a player meets once (the hall's greeting and the farmers' tips were toasts).
- [guide2] No panel moves under a finger: `hudLayout` waits while `g2TapHeld()` (a finger down on a panel the layout moves or the prompt, until that press's own click lands; `G2.tap.pending` is set by any press on the HUD and cleared by its click, and only that click lets the layout go on; a press never shortens a longer hold already asked for). A test that measures a HUD control and then taps it first waits for the last tap's click (`!G2.tap.pending`), lays out, holds the layout (`G2.tap.until = performance.now() + 30000`: a hold of 4 s ran out on a loaded machine between the measure and the finger), measures, taps, waits for its own click before it reads the world, and lets the hold go (touch_flows.py's `tap()`); a test that lays the HUD out by hand clears the hold (`G2.tap.until = 0`: guide.py's and guide2.py's `lay()`).
- [look5] (version 17) How to play on a phone (`look5HelpHTML`, from `guideHelpHTML` on a touch screen or a window up to 760 px wide): the first four controls of the pad (`guideKeysHTML`'s first four rows: keep the ones a new player needs first there) and What to do (`GUIDE_HELP[0]`) open, every other control under "All the controls" and every system's block (`GUIDE_HELP[1..]`, each folded under its own heading as before) under "Every part of the March": 1,620 px on a 390x780 phone to 622 (the sheet 746), 1,715 on a 360x640 one to 680 (606). A Chronicle page's drawing taller than half a phone's sheet folds under its own title (`chronFold`, `look5FigTitle`, `LOOK5_FIG`): the War page 2,819 px natural on a 390x780 phone, 852 folded (1,450 before), 2,958 on a 360x640 one, 875 folded (606 the sheet). Field note `l5fold` (once a character has been given four notes: the Chronicle folds, and the notes have a page of their own).
- [look6] (version 18) On a short phone (under 700 px tall) How to play's What to do is folded under its heading too (`look5HelpHTML`): the page is one screen at 360x640 (it was 1.1).

### Gotchas

- Grass and flowers are rebuilt when quality changes. Anything rebuilt at runtime must go back into the right group; see `regroupOutdoors`.
- Do not shadow common globals inside functions; a stray `P` in `gatherLights` once broke the build.
- Under SwiftShader, screenshots need a long timeout (300 s), and in-page timers lag behind wall time.
- [capture] The canvas's drawing buffer is not kept (`preserveDrawingBuffer` is off): `toDataURL` reads black unless it runs in the same task as the frame that drew it. Draw and read in one `page.evaluate` (`(__hm.capture.step(dt), canvas.toDataURL(...))`, as film.py and look.py do); in the page, draw a frame first (`captureStill` calls `tick(1e-4)`).
- The building shader in `04_props.js` is patched by other modules at anchor strings. Keep these lines intact, or update the patches with them:
  - the houses patch, which throws at boot if an anchor is missing;
  - the castles patch at `void main(){` and `vec3 col = lightSurface(alb, n, vAO);`, which silently loses its cracks instead, and ([keeps]) at `float wSnow = snowAmount(vW, n, uSnowCover * snowHere(vW), gPL) * (m == 14 ? 0.0 : 1.0);`, which silently lets snow and the wet film onto the floors inside the towers;
  - `alb *= 1.0 - 0.22 * uWet;`.
- [late3] The building shader's rune material (`MAT.rune`, 7) always lays a cold blue glyph over the colour it is given (the Barrow's runes): a red glow drawn with it reads as blue and white stripes on red up close. The deep's embers have their own material (`deepEmberMat`, `DeepBatch` in 10m_deep.js); anything else that should glow red or warm needs the same.
  - the building pieces' shader (`06k_build.js`, throws at boot if an anchor is missing): `attribute vec3 aCol;` and `vec4 w = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);` in the vertex shader, `uniform float uFlash, uWet, uSnowCover;`, `void main(){` and `vec3 col = lightSurface(alb, n, vAO);` in the fragment shader.
- [walls] The castle shader's cut (`CASTLE_CUT_GLSL`) includes `TBREACH_GLSL` from 04g_breach.js (it loads first), and both of its discards (`CASTLE_FS` and `CASTLE_DEPTH_FS`) ask `towerBreachCut` as well as `castleCut` and `towerCut`; the castle material and `castleCutUniforms` carry `uKA`, `uKB`, `uKC`. The tower fire's char (`tChar`) is charcoal with checks and ash, its embers (`tGlow`) glow in the checks (a burnt-out tower's fade over a couple of minutes: `T.fallen.ember`). A tower's hatch lids and its gallery's boards are drawn in the plaster branch tinted as wood (the wood branch's planks run along world x on a level face), and the gallery's boards butt up against each other (gaps between boards out in the sun caught light the roof's shadow could not reach).
- [siege3] The castle shader's cut also includes `BLAZE_GLSL` (04g_blaze.js, loads before 04g_castles.js): both discards (`CASTLE_FS`, `CASTLE_DEPTH_FS`) ask `deckCut(vW, vMat)` too, and the castle material and `castleCutUniforms` carry `uDS`, `uDY`, `uDA`, `uDB` (a burh's walk in zones of cells, a timber hallow's ring in sectors). `deckCut` writes the same `tChar`, `tGlow` and `tFresh` the towers and palisades do, and touches only the wood (1) and log (13; a hallow's ring also 5) ids. The timber hallow's two meshes are drawn with the castle material now (its own `cutU`). The siege engines' charring shader (`siegeMat`) also draws a burh's or the timber hallow's gate leaves while they burn or stand charred, and the walks' wrecks.
- `09u_depth.js` adds pieces to `BP`, `B_MODEL`, `B_ICON` and `BP_ORDER` at load (hip roof, lean-to, well) and replaces `B_MODEL.window` with leaded glazing; it also adds recipes to `RECIPES`. The forage shader (`FG_VS`/`FG_FS` in `09s_survival.js`) is patched at `attribute vec4 iPos;`, `float c = cos(iPos.w), s = sin(iPos.w);`, `vO = position;`, `varying vec3 vW;` and `vec3 col = lightSurface(alb, n, ao);` (an error is reported if one is missing).
- Keep halls are houses (`H.keepHall`): code that walks `HOUSES` meets them too (fire, lightning, the cover map, the save). Tests that count town houses filter them out (`houses.py`).
- A material id (`aMat`) is interpolated across a triangle whose corners carry different ids (a sheep's face meeting its fleece); the farm beasts' shader sends a blended id to the nearer of the two (`farmBeastFS`, version 9), so whole ids such as horn and udder are only ever read exactly. Keep separate materials on separate pieces of geometry where you can.
- [water2] `GLSL_ATMOS` declares `uUnder` and `uUnderCol` (02_render.js's `U`): a material made without `mat()` that includes it gets 0 (no underwater fog) unless it adds them. The composite's fragment shader is patched by 07d_dive.js at `uniform sampler2D tScene, tBloom, tRays;` and `vec3 col = clamp(finite3(texture2D(tScene, vUv).rgb), 0.0, 8.0);` (an error is reported if one is missing). The wildlife's leaping fish are `FISH`/`buildFish` (08b_wildlife.js); the diving fish are `DIVE.schools`/`buildDvFish`.
- The human crowd uses 15 of the 16 guaranteed vertex attributes. Pack new per-instance data into spare channels rather than adding attributes.
- [siege2] `addFire` adds no timed fire while 60 are in the list (40 until version 13's fitting together, when seven burning stretches of palisade filled it; a stretch keeps three flames at most, `PAL_FLAMES`), and only `drawFires` (each frame) lets the burnt-out ones go: a long `__hm.simulate` piles them up, so a burning thing that adds its flames during one gets none after the first few seconds. Code that keeps its own fires lets the burnt-out ones go first (`fireLetGo`, 04g_burn.js) and pushes `FIRES[FIRES.length - 1]` only when the list grew (a capped call left another fire's entry there, which it later put out as its own): `palisadeBurnStep`, the tower fire.
- [walls] Particles in tests: `__hm.simulate` runs the particles' clock (`U.uTime`) on ahead while the frames' clock (`renderTime`) stands still, and the next `tick` sets `U.uTime` back to `renderTime`. Whatever was emitted while simulating is born in the frames' future and shows later, frozen where it was emitted: a column of smoke over a fire that burnt during the simulation, a scatter of pale dust along a wall that was struck, in a picture taken minutes later. A test that simulates and then takes a picture should let those go after its first frame (`walls.py`'s `shot()` drops every particle born after `U.uTime`). A particle keeps the colour it is given: dust is pale at night unless it is lit as the light is (`wallLit`, or the ambient-lit colours of `05h_wear.js`).

## Multiplayer ([net], version 19)

The owner asked for multiplayer "on a spectrum all the way to persistent massively multiplayer", with accounts and saves, "a triple-A experience", and offered his Railway; then (version 19's second round) for a season-based war "on the scale of days or weeks or months", where individuals and teams log in and out asynchronously to build up their realms and join the main battles, the realms living on the whole time ("a season based mmorts"). Three rungs: rung 1 (built) shares the March among whoever has the published artifact open, through the artifact runtime's own `room`; rung 2 (built and deployed on Railway: The season, Railway, below) is the March's own server (`server/`), which the same client reaches over a WebSocket, and which runs the season of the realms while nobody plays; rung 3 (on paper, below) is a persistent March of many players on servers that run the detailed war themselves.

### Rung 1: the March shared inside the artifact (14n_net.js, 14o_netui.js)

**Who simulates what.** Each page runs its own March as before: its own armies, camps, weather, land. What is shared:
- **The players** (always): each page tells the others its own player, and draws theirs as bodies (role `remote`, a "ghost": made by `makeEnt`, drawn by the people's crowds like any person, moved only by what its own page says: `netRemoteStep` from `updateNPCs`, never thought for, never stepped by `tickBuffs` or `autoAttack`).
- **The war's shared state** (the host's): one page is the host: a server peer when there is one, else the page that has been in the room longest (`since`, then the peer label; `netHostElect`, each page elects the same from the presence it holds). Its profile carries the war (`w`: every keep's owner `k`, its gate standing `g`, the hour `td` while the sky cycles `tm`, the campaign's number `cn` and its claims `cl`); every other page takes the keeps' owners (`captureKeep` with `NET.applyingWorld`), the claims (same campaign) and the hour (`netWorldTake`), and its own war's captures are held (`netCaptureHeld` at the top of `captureKeep`: the lord who fell there is gone, the keep stays its owner's): a capture the player itself makes standing at the keep is told to the host (`cap`), which takes it if the player is of that realm and within 110 m of the keep on the host's own page, and it comes back as the host's word. When the host leaves, the next longest takes over (its own war goes on from where its page had it). The host keeps the war in the artifact's db too (`net/world`: `netWorldKeep`, once in 30 s when it changed, by a viewer who may write), and the first host of a later session takes it up (`NET.srvWorld`, 3 s after linking with nobody else there): the shared war goes on across sessions, as the server's does (rung 2).
- **The land players change**: a tree a player fells, a player's fire landing (spells, burning arrows, a brand: `fireLandsAt` with the player as its caster) and a player's meteor or leap (craters) are told as `land` moments and done the same way on the pages there now (`netLand`; checked: the remote body within reach of where it happened). A page that comes later has its own land.
- **Not shared yet** (each page has its own): the armies and their bands, the camps' beasts, the hallows' carriers (only keeps are agreed), the campaign's victory (each page declares its own; the keeps and claims are the host's, so they come together), the land the March itself changes (its armies' fires, the engines' stones, lightning) and any change made while you were away, the weather, the boats a player rows (a rower is drawn seated at the oars where he is, without his boat), the dragon. A remote player's blows at the March's bodies on its own page land only there (here you see the strike, not its foe's wound). A remote player's spell broken on your page (`breakCast`, `flareBreak`: a flare, a storm, a blunt arrow) is told to its page (`brk`), which breaks it by its own rules (a steadied spell, a mage's ward; a flare through a Renewal's steadiness); a bash's stun goes as a buff and does the same. These are what an authoritative server would share (rung 3).

**The link** (one interface, three ways): `{ kind, setSlow(obj), setFast(obj), connected(), close() }`, and it calls `netPeerUpdate(peer, { by, kind, slow, fast })`, `netPeerLeft(peer)`, `netPeerEvents(peer, evs)`. `netLinkRoom` (the artifact's `room`: the lobby's presence carries the profile under `hm`, the named room `march` (`room.join('march')`) carries the fast state under `f`; with no named rooms the lobby carries both); `netLinkWS` (14p_netws.js: the server); the stand-in (00n_netstub.js) is the room's own API, so the room's code is what the tests run. A viewer's other tab (`isMe && !sameTab`) is not another player.

**Presence only.** Viewers who opened the artifact by its link may set presence but may not send on a topic (topics are admin-only unless opened to Contributors, never to Viewers), so rung 1 sends nothing on a topic: the moments ride in the fast state as a ring (`ev`: `[seq, kind, to, data]`, each read once by its number, kept 2.6 s and at most 22, so a page that hears only every few updates still has them; a moment that must not be lost (an invite and its answer, a chat line, a death, a capture told to the host) 9 s and the land's 6 s (`NET_EV_KEEP`: a page busy for a few seconds still finds them in the latest state it reads, which is all presence keeps); to: a peer label or 0 for all). The platform coalesces presence (latest wins, about 30 a second) and caps it at 4 KiB: the fast state is about 230 bytes, the profile about 300 (`netPump` trims the ring before it would pass 3,700). Kinds of moment: `hit` (a blow struck at that player: `{a, c, k, pi, dt, ab, ar, el, pet}`), `hr` (what landed: `[dealt, crit, killed, hp lost]`), `buf` (a buff laid: `[kind, value, dur]`, only the kinds in `NET_BUFFS`, a foe's only harm, a friend's only help, each within its bounds), `heal`, `die` (`[killer's peer]`), `pj` (a bolt loosed: shown with `spawnProjectile(..., visualOnly)`), `ar` (a drawn arrow: a `vis` arrow in `CLS.arrows` that strikes nothing), `say` (`[channel 'r' | 'p', text, party]`), `inv`, `pa` (a party's invite and its answer), `cap` (a capture told to the host), `brk` (a spell broken: 1 a flare), `land` (`['fell', tree, dx, dz]`, `['fire', x, y, z, r]`, `['imp', x, z, 'meteor' | 'leap', r]`).

**What each page says of its player.** The profile (`netSlowObj`, sent when it changes, looked at once a second): `on`, `since`, the name and the name worn (`n`, `dn`: `late2Named`), realm, calling, level, realm rank, the look (`lk`: fifteen numbers: tabard, armour, skin, hair, mask, flags, scale, outfit, emblem, fem, bulk; the torch, beater and hammer bits left out), the mantle's device (`mc`: `late3MantleCode`, laid on the emblem as drawActors does, so nothing in drawActors changes), the horse's coat and cloth (`hz`), the wear on its gear (`wr`), the party (`pt`, `pl`), and from the host the war (`w`). The fast state (`netFastObj`, ten times a second while anything in it changes; nothing is sent while nothing changes): `s` (its number), `t` (the sender's clock in ms), `p` (place, cm), `y` (heading), `v` (pace, for prediction), `a` (the body's action as `animActValue` gives it: strikes, the bow drawn, a spell cast, a ladder climbed, the oars, swimming under water, kneeling, beating flames), `ph` (the rungs' phase on a ladder), `h`, `m` (health as a share, the most), `d` (dead), `mo` (mounted), `sw` (swimming: depth share and stroke), `st` (the seat's height in a boat), `cs` (a spell in hand and how far), `fl` (burning 1, a brand 2, stunned 4, in the Barrow 8), `tg` (whom it targets, if a player), `ev`.

**Drawing them.** A body's snapshots go in a buffer with the sender's clock; the offset to ours is the least seen, creeping up slowly when deliveries slow down for good (`netBufPush`); the body is drawn `NET.cfg.delay` (120 ms) behind the sender, between the two snapshots either side (heading by the short way round, one action's progress run on, another taking over at the half), and past the newest predicted along its pace for up to 0.25 s, then held (never onto ground nobody walks: `stepOkForGhost`); a jump of more than 24 m between snapshots (a release, a portal, a journey) starts afresh. Its gait comes from `updateAnim` (its legs, the foot lock, the lean), its action from `e.netAct` (`animActValue` returns it for a remote body), swimming from `swimK`/`swimAmt` (the stroke's phase run on here), the horse from `hz`, the seat from `st`, a spell's glow from `cs`, burning flames from `fl`, its health and death from `h` and `d` (the fall played once; `killEnt` never runs on a remote body), and a chat line over its head for 7 s.

**Players meeting.** A remote player is a foe only to you and only of another realm (`isEnemy` asks `netIsEnemy` first whenever either side is remote): the March's own bodies never take it for a foe or a friend (no NPC targets it, no NPC's area or heal reaches it), so a page's war never acts on another's player. A blow you strike at one (`dealDamage` with a remote body: auto-attack, abilities, areas, bolts and arrows that reach it on your page) goes as `hit` (`netOutHit`: the amount after your own side's measures, `computeDamage`'s level, crit and buffs; your page plays the hit's flash, sound and momentum with an estimate), and the struck page deals it to itself with its own armour, shields, parries, wards, gifts and draughts (`dealDamage(ghostOfStriker, player, amount, opts)`), and sends back what landed (`hr`), which your page shows as the number over it and the log's line. The struck page checks first (`netHandle`): the striker's body there alive and a foe, within 12 m for a blow and 60 m for anything else, at most 14 blows a second from one player, no blow harder than six of the striker's level's hardest (`baseDmg`). A buff you lay (`addBuff` on a remote body: stuns, snares, roots, dots, burns, bleeds, wounds, the dazzle, tracking; a friend's heals over time, shields and wards) goes as `buf` and is laid by its page within `NET_BUFFS`' bounds (a stun at most 4 s); a heal on a friend (`healEnt`) as `heal`. Death: your page tells who struck the last blow if it was a player (`die`); that player's page counts the kill (`prog.realmKills`, 40 + 6 a level realm points, the log and a toast), and your death screen names the slayer and its realm.

**Party and chat** (14o_netui.js). The Players sheet (P on a desk; the Players button by the minimap on a phone, a count on it, glowing while an invite waits): everyone in the March now (name, realm, calling, level, how far, in your party, who keeps the shared war), Target, Invite (players of your realm; up to six), an invite to Join or Decline, Leave, the chat's last lines and Say to your realm / Say to your party. Enter on a desk opens the chat line (a channel button: Realm or Party; Escape closes it); the line (140 characters, no control or invisible characters: `netStr`) goes as `say`, shows in the log and over the speaker's head; a realm's chat is heard only by that realm, a party's only by the party (each page filters what it hears; over the server, the server sends it only to them); one line a second at most from a page. The party's frames (`#netparty`: name, level, health, fallen; a tap targets; in every HUD order after the companion bar, compact on a phone when it must be), the party on the minimap (green, ringed) and on the map (green, named); the others of your realm blue, foes in their realm's colour (on the map only where they are drawn). A party is the shared id in each member's profile (`pt`): invite (`inv`, the inviter's party made if it has none), accept (`pa`), leave. Every name and line another page sent is set as text (`textContent`, the log's `uiLog`), never as markup.

**Joining late, leaving, reconnecting, alone.** A newcomer gets everyone's presence at once (the platform hands it over), so it has every body and the host's war on its first delivery; a page that leaves (or, in the stand-in, stops answering for 12 s) is in `left`: its body goes, the host moves on if it was the host. The platform re-asserts presence on reconnect; the server's link reconnects by itself (1, 2, 4 ... 15 s) and sends everything again. With no room (no runtime, a signed-out viewer, a public visitor the platform does not admit, a page opened as a file) `NET.state` is `alone` and nothing of this runs: the page plays exactly as before (the Players button never shows).

**On the wire** (`net.py` room, the stand-in, two pages; `perf`): one walking player sends about 230 bytes ten times a second while it moves (2.3 KB/s, about 8 MB an hour of steady walking; nothing while it stands; the profile about 300 bytes when it changes); a page with ten others walking about it would hear about 23 KB/s (each update is the whole presence object; reckoned from the senders: a page busy with a long frame reads only the latest of each, so a slow phone hears fewer). A phone on mobile data can keep a party; a crowd wants the server's interest management (rung 2) or named rooms by region (rung 3). The cost of others on a page (`net.py perf`, 640x360, SwiftShader on 2 CPUs at a load of about 14, the medians of 40): with ten players walking round it a step took 3.3 ms against 2.9 alone, a frame's JS 12.8 ms against 16.9 (the GPU drained first; within the machine's noise), one draw call more (63) and 66k triangles more (638k against 572k: ten people near, and their shadows); the page heard 1,008 of their updates, about 250 bytes each.

**Publishing it.** The artifact must declare `room` beside `db` and `user`: republish once with `capabilities: {db: {}, user: {}, room: {}}` (no topics: everything rides in presence; the db's default rules are enough: the server's token is kept in `data/users/<id>/server`, each player's own). From then on republish omitting `capabilities` as before. A viewer who may not write the db (a Viewer at `view`) still plays with the others (presence is open to every viewer the platform admits); a signed-out or public visitor gets no room and plays alone.

**The stand-in** (00n_netstub.js): `window.claude` with `room` (lobby and named rooms over a BroadcastChannel: presence merged, capped at 4 KiB and sent coalesced about 30 a second, `onPeers` with joined, left and updated once a frame, newcomers handed everyone's presence, a heartbeat and `left` after 12 s of silence (`silence`), and a page heard again after it was taken for gone makes everyone say again who they are (as a room hands a reconnected page everyone's presence: under SwiftShader a page's timers can starve for seconds, and a returning page came back with its fast state and no profile), `emit` refused unless `emit: true`), `db` (documents and collections over localStorage, onSnapshot over a second channel, `{self}` privacy under `data/users`, writes refused for `dbWrite: false`, leases) and `user` (`id`, `me`, `can('data.write')`). Installed only when `window.__HM_NET` is set before the page's script (`{ room, user, latency, jitter, drop, emit, dbWrite, noDb, noRoom, noJoin, silence, server }`: the tests) or the address carries `?net=local` (two tabs of the built file on one machine: `hallowmarch.html?net=local&room=x`), and never over a real `window.claude`. Installed at the top of the module script (it loads after 00_util.js) so the boot's save sees it.

**For new code.** Anything a player does to another player goes through `dealDamage`, `addBuff` and `healEnt` (they are forwarded) or a new moment (`netEvent(kind, toPeer | 0, data)` and a branch in `netHandle`, every field read with `netNum`/`netStr` and bounded, never trusted). Anything that should show on the others' pages goes in the profile (rarely changing) or the fast state (each field in `netFastObj`, `netFastRead` and the buffer's snapshot) and is read on the remote body in `netRemoteStep`. A system that walks `ENT` meets remote bodies (role `remote`, `e.netPeer`): it should leave them alone unless it is drawing them (`updateNPCs` hands them to `netRemoteStep`; `isEnemy` keeps the March's own off them). A new keep-changing path calls `captureKeep` (held for the host on a follower). Nothing a player types or another page sends goes into `innerHTML`.

### Rung 2: the March's own server (server/, 14p_netws.js)

`server/server.js` (Node 20+, `ws`): `node server/server.js` (`PORT`, `HM_DATA` for its files, `HM_SECRET` to sign tokens, `HM_PAGE` the built page it serves at `/`, `HM_INTEREST` metres, `HM_ROOM_CAP` players a shard). A page reaches it with `?server=wss://host/ws` on its address (or `window.__HM_NET.server`), or is served by it (`/` serves the built `hallowmarch.html` with `window.__HM_NET_SERVER` set to its own `/ws`).
- **Accounts**: a guest account at the first hello, its signed token (HMAC-SHA256, 180 days) kept by the page for that host (`localStorage` `hallowmarch.token.<host>`, and inside the artifact the player's private db document `data/users/<id>/server`, so the claude.ai account finds its server account on another device), presented at the next hello; or a name and a password (scrypt). The Players sheet's account part (`#netsheet-acct`, `netAcctRender`: only while the page is linked to a server) lets a guest name its own account (`acct` `claim`: the name and password set on it, so it keeps its character and save) or sign in to a named one (`login`: its token is kept and the page loads again, so the boot reads that account's save; the socket stays the guest's until then, so nothing the page saves before it reloads lands on the named account), and a named one sign out (its token dropped: a new guest); six tries a minute a socket; at a hello, `reg` and `login` do the same. A token for one host is never sent to another.
- **Saves**: `initSaveBackend` (12_save.js) asks `netServerSaveRef` first: with a server, the save is the server's (`load`, `save`, `wipe`; at most 768 KB; `saves/<account>.json`), read at the boot as the db's was, written by the same heartbeat; `SAVE.server` is set. Without one, the artifact's db and this browser as before.
- **The shared war**: the host is chosen by the server's clock (it stamps `since`: no page can claim to have come first); the host's `w` is checked (as many keeps as the world has, realms 0 to 2) and kept (`worlds.json`, by shard), handed to every page at its welcome (`world`), and taken by the first host of a session (`NET.srvWorld`): the war goes on across sessions.
- **The relay with interest**: a profile goes to everyone in the shard; a fast state to those within `HM_INTEREST` m (300) and the party, and every 2.5 s to the rest (for their maps: `far`); its moments only to whom they concern (a blow, an invite, an answer to its `to`; a realm's chat to its realm; a party's to the party; sent once each over the socket: the ring's repeats are dropped); a moment for a reader far off goes alone (`t: 'ev'`).
- **Checks**: 60 messages a second (more are dropped, 240 closes the socket), 8 KB a message (768 KB a save), a pace over 45 m/s is not relayed unless the jump ends at a town or a muster (the portals, a release) or in the Barrow, a blow from farther than 70 m is dropped, the host by the server's clock. Shards: `march`, then `march-2` ... when one holds `HM_ROOM_CAP` (64) players.
- **Not in it yet**: the March's detailed simulation (the season's strategic war runs there: The season, below). It knows the world's sites (it loads `00_util.js` and `01_world.js`: the keeps, towns and musters; `buildWorld`'s land needs the page's other modules and three.js), not the land: no walkability check, no armies. The war is simulated by the host's page and kept by the server, as in rung 1.
- **Deployed on Railway**: see Railway, below.
- **From the artifact**: whether a published artifact's page may open a WebSocket to another host is not known here (its sandbox and content policy were not reachable from this container). The client is written for either answer: `netLinkWS` fails within 7 s when the socket is refused and the page falls back to the artifact's room (or plays alone); the save falls back to the artifact's db. If the artifact may not reach the server, the server's own page is the way in for rung 2 and 3, and the artifact's room stays rung 1.
- `/health` (players, shards), `/stats` (messages, bytes, relays, drops by reason, saves, accounts named, sign-ins and tries refused, each shard's host and kept war).

### The season: the realms live on while nobody plays ([net], version 19, second round)

**What a player meets.** The March opened from its server (`https://march-production-f6d9.up.railway.app/`, or any page with `?server=wss://march-production-f6d9.up.railway.app/ws`) is one season of weeks (28 days by default). The war panel ends with the season's line ("Season 1 · day 3 of 28 · War · 4 of Ériu on", the time left), and the Chronicle's Season page (The war part, after The war) tells: the season's day and phase (Building for its first 15%: no levies, no musters; War; The final week: every keep held counts twice; Over: the realm with the most points holds the March, and a new season begins a day later), each realm's season points and keeps, your realm's stores (food, timber, stone, iron, hides, wool, horses), its works (walls, a forge, a granary, siege engines, stables: what each needs and has, its votes, a button to vote; the realm builds the most-voted work from its stores as the goods come), the keeps (who holds each, its guards, its gate, a siege; a button to vote to march on a foe's keep, and the realm's target), the armies in the field, the next levy (an officer of the realm, rank 5, may call a muster), who of your realm is on now and who was on today (and what each brought today), and the season's news (the Players sheet tells the realm's roster too, with a button to the Season page; the map shows your realm's armies and every siege as pennants with their numbers). Bring your goods: every carried good the stores take (by loops's table `LOOPS_WORTH` when it is here, else `NETS_WORTH`) is brought to the realm's stores on the server by a tap, paid in realm points; the server takes what one could have gathered and says so (the rest stays in your packs). With loops's quartermasters, a delivery there is told to the season too (`loopsDeliver` wrapped). A returning player is told how long it was away and what happened (a toast and the log's lines: the news since it was last seen), and its realm's chat while it was away (the last 20 lines, kept by the server). Field note `netseason`, a How to play block, a tip.

**The shared contract** (loops and net, CLAUDE.md's prompt for version 19): `src/08m_realm.js` (loops's: no three.js, DOM, window or audio; it runs unchanged in Node) holds the realms' strategic state as one plain JSON object `RS` and `realmSimInit(seed, opts)`, `realmSimStep(RS, dt)`, `realmSimContribute(RS, realm, kind, amount, who)`, `realmSimOrder(RS, realm, order, who)`, `realmSimSummary(RS, realm, since)`, `realmSimSanitize(obj)`, `RS.v`. net's extension: `realmSimCapture(RS, keep, realm, who)` (a keep taken in the live war; when the module has none, the server sets the keep's holder `r`, or `holder`). The server loads `src/08m_realm.js` when it exists, else its own stand-in **`server/realm_stub.js`** (the same functions and a plain shape: `realms[r].st` the stores in loops's goods, `pts`, `built`, `proj`, `votes`, `levyAt`; `keeps[i]` `{ i, name, home, x, z, r, g, gate, siege }`; `armies` `{ id, r, n, x, z, to, st }`; `log` `[t, realm, text]`; `t`, `len`, `n`, `phase`, `over`, `winner`; steps of a minute at most inside, 28 days in about 0.7 s; deterministic for a seed). **For the integrator:** when loops's module lands, the server takes it with no change if it has the functions; what the client reads of a summary is in `netsRead` (14q_netseason.js): `n, t, len, day, days, phase ('build' | 'war' | 'final' | 'over'), over, winner, pts[3], keeps[{i, r, g, gate, siege}], armies[{r, n, to, st, x, z}], st{good: n}, built[], proj[{id, label, did, built, votes, need, have}], target, levyIn, news[[t, realm, text]]`: map loops's summary onto it there (or make loops's summary that shape), and the keeps' holders through `SEASON.keepsOf` (server/season.js reads `r`, `holder` or `owner`).

**The server's side** (`server/season.js`, `server/server.js`): the season stepped by the server's clock every `HM_SEASON_STEP` ms (5 s) at `HM_SEASON_SPEED` season seconds a real second (1), its length `HM_SEASON_DAYS` (28), its seed `HM_SEASON_SEED`; kept in `season.json` on the volume every 30 s when it changed and on SIGTERM (Railway's redeploys), with the roster (`roster.json`) and the realms' chat (`chat.json`); after a restart the time it was down is stepped at once (a week at most). Told (`season`) to every player of a realm every `HM_SEASON_PUSH` ms (10 s) and at once after an order of its realm: `realmSimSummary` for its realm (the news since its last telling), the roster (`rosterOf`: the accounts of the realm seen in the last day, on now or not, what each brought today), and on the first telling the news since the account was last seen (`away` s) and the realm's chat. **Contributions** (`contrib` `{k, n, q}`): a good of the contract's, from a player with a realm, at most 4 a second; each account has a bucket a good that fills at a gatherer's best pace and holds a long trip's load (`GATHER`: food 40 a minute up to 600, timber 20/300, stone 12/200, iron 5/80, hides and wool 4/60, horses 0.2/4); what is over is cut (`contribClipped`) and told; full stores take nothing and give the bucket back. **Orders** (`order` `{o: {kind: 'project' | 'target' | 'muster', id, keep}}`): one at a time a socket (2.5 s), one vote an account for each choice a season (`acct.votes`), an officer's (realm rank 5 and up, from the profile) counting thrice, a muster only by an officer and not while the realm builds. **The live war writes back**: a keep the region's keeper (below) takes in its war is taken in the season (`SEASON.capture`: a change between two of one keeper's reports), and a keep the season's armies take is told to the pages and taken by the keep's keeper (`netsApply`: only what the season changed since its last word, so the live war's own captures stand). The realm's stores are laid into loops's `LOOPS.r` when it is here (the server's are the truth while linked). `/season` (public: the keeps, points and news, no realm's stores), `/stats` (`season`: its step's milliseconds, the roster's size; `proc`: the server's memory and CPU), `POST /admin` with the header `x-hm-admin: <HM_ADMIN>` (`op=keep&i=&r=` a keep's holder set as the season's armies would; `op=reset` a new season, its roster, chat and votes cleared; `op=save`).

**Who simulates what** (the regions). Each page runs its own March round it (its armies, camps, weather, land); the players and the season are shared. The March is seven regions (`regionOf` in server.js: each realm's third of the frontier `f0` `f1` `f2` (nearest muster, within 190 m of the middle: the keeps stand there), each homeland `h0` `h1` `h2`, the Barrow `b`); of the pages in a region the one there longest keeps it (`regionHosts`, by the server's clock), told to every page (`hosts`: `h` region to peer, `kr` each keep's region). A keep's word is its region's keeper's (else the shard's host's): the keeper's page takes a capture there and its own war's keep changes are reported (`o.w` in its profile: `netKeepsMine`); the server merges each keep from its keeper (`worldReport`), keeps it, tells every other page (`world`, taken with `netWorldTake(w, 'keeps')`: never a keep the page keeps itself) and writes the change into the season; a page that does not keep the region holds its own war's capture there and tells the keeper (`cap` to `netKeepHost(i)`, as rung 1 told the host). The shard's host (the page longest in the shard) keeps the hour, the claims and every region with no keeper. Handed on when a keeper leaves the region or the March. The armies of the live war near a page are that page's own (they are not yet shared: rung 3), and the season's armies are numbers on the server (shown on the Season page; not yet bands in the live war: below).

**Tested** (this round, on a machine at a load of 11 to 15 on 2 CPUs shared with three builders): `net.py season` (21 checks), `server` (rung 2's, with the regions and the phone's budget), `room three` (rung 1's: unchanged) and `deployed` (two pages on the Railway server seeing each other, told the season; round trip 241 ms from here) pass; `net_season.mjs` passes against a local server (with a restart) and the deployed one; `net.py perf`: a step 3.6 ms alone and 4.4 with ten others walking round, a frame's JS 13.6 and 14.9 ms, one draw call more (the stand-in room); `merged.py noshots`, `integration.py`, `worldstate.py`, `lore.py`, `phone.py`, `guide.py noshots`, `hud_layout.py noshots sizes=390x780,360x640,844x390,1280x720` (the season's line on the war panel) and `touch_flows.py only=net` pass; nothing new is drawn in the world (the season's armies are 2D marks on the map), no shader touched. The deployed season was started afresh (`POST /admin op=reset`) after the tests that played it: season 2 is the owner's first real one.

**Not yet** (for the next round): the season's armies near a player becoming real bands of the live war and the live war's bands reported back as the season's armies (the contract asks it of the detailed war: loops's side and this one's); the weather shared from the server (weather2's systems: the season's message keeps a slot, `RS.weather` or a `wx` field beside `s`, which the client does not read yet); RS's levy and siege numbers tuned against the live war's pace (the stand-in's are a guess: loops's module replaces them); the published artifact reaching the server (`tools/net/probe.html`: not published from these sessions); the account's identity handed over from claude.ai (`claude.use('user')`'s id is not proof to the server: the token kept in the player's private db document is how a claude.ai account finds its server account on another device).
